63. ENTERPRISE RECOMMENDATIONS



Based on comprehensive architecture analysis, the consulting consortium presents the
following recommendations:



Recommendation 1: Begin with Event-Driven Modular Architecture Immediately
The architecture style selection is the most consequential decision. The Event-Driven Modular
approach has been validated as optimal for Agbofa's specific constraints and ambitions.
Implement strict module boundaries and event contracts from the first line of code.



Recommendation 2: Invest in the Event Bus Abstraction Early



While Phase 1 will use in-process events, the event bus abstraction layer should be production-
quality from day one. This is the single most important architectural enabler for the P1→P3+
evolution path.



Recommendation 3: Prioritise Provenance Architecture



Content provenance is both a competitive differentiator and a compliance requirement. The
event sourcing approach for content lifecycle should receive dedicated architectural attention
and not be treated as a secondary feature.



Recommendation 4: Build the AI Model Abstraction Layer Incrementally



Start with direct API integration in Phase 1, but design the abstraction interface immediately.
This enables rapid Phase 1 development while ensuring the multi-model architecture is
achievable without redesign.



Recommendation 5: Conduct Regular Architecture Fitness Evaluations



Implement automated architecture fitness functions that validate:



· Module boundary integrity (no unauthorised cross-module dependencies)

· Event schema compliance
· Tenant isolation enforcement

· API versioning compliance

 Run these in CI/CD to prevent architecture erosion.



Recommendation 6: Plan the Database Evolution Path



Begin with shared PostgreSQL with tenant_id columns, but design for schema-per-tenant or
database-per-tenant as enterprise requirements demand. Document the migration path and
triggers.



Recommendation 7: Establish the Architecture Review Board



Form an Architecture Review Board with representatives from all architecture domains.
Establish meeting cadence (bi-weekly during P1, monthly thereafter) and decision-making
authority.



Recommendation 8: Invest in Observability from Sprint One



Implement OpenTelemetry instrumentation, structured logging, and standard metrics collection
from the very first service. The autonomous nature of the platform makes observability non-
negotiable.



Recommendation 9: Design for Failure from the Start



Implement circuit breakers, retries, timeouts, and graceful degradation for all external
dependencies. An autonomous AI platform operating 24/7 cannot rely on human intervention
for dependency failures.
Recommendation 10: Document All Architecture Decisions



Continue the ADR practice established in this volume. Every significant architecture decision
should be documented with context, options, rationale, and consequences. This documentation
is essential for future teams, enterprise customers, and AI agents.



---



64. CONCLUSION



This Volume 3 Enterprise Architecture establishes the complete structural foundation for the
Agbofa Nexus AI platform. The architecture has been designed to meet an exceptionally
challenging set of requirements: operate on free-tier infrastructure, scale linearly to enterprise
workloads, support multi-tenancy and white-label deployment, enable autonomous AI-driven
content operations, and maintain architectural integrity throughout the evolution.



Key Architectural Achievements:



1. Event-Driven Modular Architecture that deploys as a cohesive application in Phase 1 yet
enables gradual extraction to distributed services as scale demands.

2. Complete technology stack selection optimised for free-tier viability in Phase 1 and
enterprise-grade capability in Phase 3+, with TypeScript/Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, and cloud-
agnostic infrastructure abstractions.

3. Domain-Driven Design with bounded contexts that align architecture with business
capabilities, enabling team autonomy and independent evolution.

4. Comprehensive event-driven content pipeline where every stage from discovery through
monetisation is connected by events, providing loose coupling, observability, and provenance.

5. AI-native architecture where AI agents are first-class architectural components with defined
interfaces, observability patterns, and lifecycle management.
6. Multi-tenancy architecture supporting shared infrastructure through dedicated deployments,
enabling the full spectrum from free-tier MVP to Fortune 500 enterprise customers.

7. Cloud-agnostic design with abstraction interfaces that prevent provider lock-in while
pragmatically optimising for Phase 1 free-tier services.

8. Complete observability, security, and resilience patterns designed into the architecture from
day one, not layered on afterwards.



The architecture is now ready for:



· Volume 4: AI & Machine Learning Architecture (detailed agent design, model strategies,
training pipelines)

· Volume 5: Software Architecture & Design (component specifications, API contracts, database
schemas)

· Volume 6: Infrastructure & DevOps Architecture (IaC, CI/CD, environment management)

· Volume 7: Security & Compliance Architecture (detailed security controls, threat models)

· Volume 8: Operational Framework (runbooks, monitoring, incident management)



All subsequent volumes will reference and comply with the architectural decisions, patterns,
and constraints defined herein.

2. AI ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES



These principles govern all AI-specific architectural decisions. They extend the general
architecture principles from Volume 3 into the AI domain.



Principle AI-1: Agent Specialisation Over Generalisation
Statement: AI agents shall be specialised for specific tasks within the content pipeline rather
than relying on a single general-purpose model. Each agent shall have clearly defined
responsibilities, capabilities, and boundaries.



Rationale: Specialised agents can be optimised independently—better prompts, specific models,
tailored evaluation. This enables quality improvements in one agent without risking degradation
in others. It aligns with the Unix philosophy applied to AI: do one thing well.



Implications:



· Minimum set of agent types defined with clear boundaries

· Each agent has independent prompt configuration

· Each agent can use different AI models

· Agent outputs are validated against agent-specific quality criteria

· Agent specialisation enables independent scaling and optimisation



Principle AI-2: Verification-First Content Generation



Statement: Verification is not a post-generation step—it is embedded throughout the content
pipeline. Every factual claim must be traceable to verified sources. Content confidence scores
determine publishing routing.



Rationale: Trust is Agbofa's primary value proposition. AI-generated content without verification
is a commodity. Verification-first design ensures quality is built in, not inspected in.



Implications:



· Research agent establishes verified fact base before writing begins
· Writer agent constrained to verified facts

· Fact-checker agent validates every claim post-generation

· Quality scoring gates determine autonomous vs. human-review publishing

· Unverifiable claims are explicitly marked, not silently published



Principle AI-3: Progressive Autonomy



Statement: AI autonomy shall increase progressively as the platform demonstrates reliability.
Content categories, brands, and platforms may have different autonomy levels based on risk
assessment.



Rationale: Building trust with audiences and operators requires demonstrated competence.
Progressive autonomy allows the platform to earn trust while managing risk.



Implications:



· Autonomy levels configurable per brand, content type, and risk category

· Autonomy increases based on verified quality metrics, not time

· Human oversight always available as override

· High-risk content categories (finance, health, news) have higher human oversight initially

· Autonomy regression triggered by quality metric degradation



Principle AI-4: Explainable AI by Default



Statement: Every AI agent decision that affects content output shall be explainable. The
rationale for content choices, source selection, quality scores, and publishing decisions shall be
available for audit.
Rationale: Black-box AI is unacceptable for a media company. Audiences, regulators, and
enterprise customers require explainability. Explainable decisions enable continuous
improvement.



Implications:



· Agents produce structured outputs with reasoning, not just final content

· Quality scores include component breakdowns, not just aggregate numbers

· Source selection includes credibility reasoning

· Editorial changes include rationale

· Explainability data stored in provenance records



Principle AI-5: Human Sovereignty



Statement: AI agents operate within boundaries defined by humans. Humans set editorial
direction, ethical guidelines, and quality standards. AI executes within these boundaries.
Humans can override any AI decision.



Rationale: Agbofa is an AI-augmented media company, not an AI-controlled one. Human
editorial judgment remains sovereign, particularly for ethical decisions and brand strategy.



Implications:



· Editorial guidelines are human-defined and machine-interpreted

· AI cannot modify its own ethical boundaries

· Human override available at every pipeline stage
· Strategic direction (brand voice, content strategy) is human-set

· AI recommends; humans decide for critical categories



Principle AI-6: Continuous Learning from Operations



Statement: The AI ecosystem shall continuously learn from its operations—content
performance, human feedback, quality metrics, and audience engagement—to improve future
output.



Rationale: A learning system compounds its advantages over time. Each piece of content, each
human correction, each engagement signal should make the system better.



Implications:



· Performance feedback loops from analytics to content strategy

· Human corrections fed back to improve agent prompts

· Successful content patterns reinforced in future generation

· A/B testing framework for systematic improvement

· Learning is per-brand and per-content-type for specificity



Principle AI-7: Cost-Aware AI Operations



Statement: AI model selection shall consider cost alongside quality and latency. The platform
shall optimise the cost-quality trade-off based on content value and strategic importance.



Rationale: AI API costs can become the dominant operational expense. Intelligent model routing
ensures appropriate resource allocation—premium models for high-value content, efficient
models for routine content.
Implications:



· Model cascade architecture: route to cheapest capable model

· Cost tracking per content piece, per brand, per agent

· Budget enforcement mechanisms

· Open-source model adoption for high-volume tasks

· Cost optimization is continuous, not one-time



Principle AI-8: Safety by Architecture



Statement: AI safety shall be implemented architecturally—through system design, not prompt
engineering alone. Safety constraints are enforced at multiple layers.



Rationale: Prompt-based safety is brittle and bypassable. Architectural safety provides defence
in depth—content classifiers, output validators, policy engines, and human escalation paths.



Implications:



· Content safety classifiers independent from generation models

· Policy engine for configurable safety rules

· Safety violations trigger content rejection, not just warnings

· Safety architecture is provider-independent

· Regular red-teaming and safety evaluation

4. AI AGENT ARCHITECTURE



4.1 Agent Anatomy
Every AI agent in the Agbofa Nexus AI ecosystem follows a standardised architecture pattern:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│               STANDARD AGENT ANATOMY                           │

│                                            │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │              AGENT BOUNDARY                          │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ IDENTITY │ │ CONTEXT │ │              CAPABILITIES       │ │ │

│ │ │         │ │ MANAGER │ │                      │ │ │

│ │ │ • Agent ID │ │           │ │ • Supported tasks │ │ │

│ │ │ • Agent Type │ │ • Memory        │ │ • Input formats       │ │ │

│ │ │ • Version │ │ retrieval │ │ • Output formats             │ │ │

│ │ │ • Capability │ │ • Context │ │ • Quality metrics │ │ │

│ │ │ Profile │ │ assembly │ │ • Constraints              │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                 │                       │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │             PROMPT ENGINE                     │ │ │

│ │ │                                     │ │ │

│ │ │ • Template selection (agent type + brand + task)           │ │ │

│ │ │ • Variable injection (context, guidelines, data)         │ │ │
│ │ │ • Context window optimisation                    │ │ │

│ │ │ • Safety instruction injection                 │ │ │

│ │ │ • Output format specification                   │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                │                        │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │            MODEL ROUTER                       │ │ │

│ │ │                                      │ │ │

│ │ │ • Model selection (primary, fallback chain)            │ │ │

│ │ │ • Provider adapter invocation                   │ │ │

│ │ │ • Cost estimation and tracking                  │ │ │

│ │ │ • Timeout and retry management                        │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                │                        │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │            RESPONSE PROCESSOR                   │ │ │

│ │ │                                      │ │ │

│ │ │ • Response parsing and validation                 │ │ │

│ │ │ • Structured output extraction                  │ │ │

│ │ │ • Quality check (basic validation)              │ │ │

│ │ │ • Error detection and handling                  │ │ │

│ │ │ • Output normalisation                         │ │ │

│ │ └──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                │                        │ │

│ │ ┌──────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │            OBSERVABILITY LAYER                 │ │ │
│ │ │                                     │ │ │

│ │ │ • Execution logging (input, output, model, tokens, latency) │ │ │

│ │ │ • Metric emission (success rate, quality score, cost)               │ │ │

│ │ │ • Trace context propagation                             │ │ │

│ │ │ • Provenance event emission                             │ │ │

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



4.2 Agent Interface Contract



All agents implement a standard interface, enabling the Orchestrator to manage them
uniformly:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│               AGENT INTERFACE CONTRACT                              │

│                                            │

│ interface IAgent {                                      │

│                                            │

│ // Identity                                     │

│ agentId: string;                                    │

│ agentType: AgentType;                                       │

│ version: string;                                    │
│ capabilities: Capability[];                                   │

│                                           │

│ // Lifecycle                                  │

│ initialise(config: AgentConfig): Promise<void>;                               │

│ healthCheck(): Promise<HealthStatus>;                                     │

│ shutdown(): Promise<void>;                                            │

│                                           │

│ // Execution                                      │

│ execute(request: AgentRequest): Promise<AgentResponse>;                               │

│ executeStreaming(request: AgentRequest): AsyncIterable<AgentChunk>;                       │

│                                           │

│ // Introspection                                      │

│ getCapabilities(): Capability[];                                  │

│ estimateCost(request: AgentRequest): CostEstimate;                                │

│ getModelInfo(): ModelInfo;                                            │

│ }                                         │

│                                           │

│ interface AgentRequest {                                          │

│ taskType: string;                                     │

│ context: AgentContext;                                            │

│ input: any;                                   │

│ constraints?: AgentConstraints;                                       │

│ correlationId: string;                                    │

│ tenantId: string;                                 │

│ brandId?: string;                                     │

│ }                                         │
│                                              │

│ interface AgentResponse {                                   │

│ output: any;                                       │

│ metadata: {                                       │

│       agentId: string;                             │

│       modelUsed: string;                                │

│       tokensUsed: { input: number; output: number };                    │

│       latency: number;                                  │

│       cost: number;                                 │

│       confidenceScore?: number;                                 │

│ };                                           │

│ provenance: ProvenanceRecord;                                       │

│ }                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



4.3 Agent Configuration Model



```

AGENT CONFIGURATION SCHEMA

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



AgentConfig {

 identity: {

      agentType: "WriterAgent" | "EditorAgent" | "FactCheckerAgent" | ...
 version: "1.2.0"

 displayName: "Default Writer Agent"

},



modelConfig: {

 primary: {

     provider: "openai" | "anthropic" | "google" | "open-source"

     modelId: "gpt-4o" | "claude-3.5-sonnet" | ...

     parameters: {

         temperature: 0.7

         maxTokens: 4096

         topP: 0.9

         frequencyPenalty: 0.3

         presencePenalty: 0.1

     }

 },

 fallbackChain: [

     { provider: "anthropic", modelId: "claude-3-haiku" },

     { provider: "openai", modelId: "gpt-4o-mini" }

 ],

 timeout: 60000, // milliseconds

 maxRetries: 2

},



promptConfig: {

 promptId: "writer-agent-v2.1.0",
    promptVersion: "2.1.0",

    systemPrompt: "...",

    taskTemplates: {

        "article-generation": { ... },

        "social-post-generation": { ... },

        "headline-generation": { ... }

    },

    brandOverrides: {

        "tech-media": { systemPromptAdditions: "..." },

        "finance-media": { temperature: 0.3 }

    }

},



constraints: {

    maxTokensPerRequest: 8192,

    maxCostPerRequest: 0.05, // USD

    requiredConfidenceThreshold: 0.7,

    bannedTopics: ["topic1", "topic2"],

    requiredDisclosures: ["ai-generated-content"]

},



safetyConfig: {

    contentSafetyLevel: "standard", // "permissive" | "standard" | "strict"

    harmCategories: ["hate", "harassment", "violence", "self-harm", "sexual"],

    policyViolationAction: "reject" // "reject" | "flag" | "warn"

}
}

```

11. MULTI-AGENT COLLABORATION FRAMEWORK



11.1 Collaboration Patterns



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│           MULTI-AGENT COLLABORATION PATTERNS                        │

│                                           │

│ PATTERN 1: SEQUENTIAL HANDOFF                                   │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                   │

│ Agent A completes task → passes structured output to Agent B            │

│                                           │
│ ┌────────┐ Structured         ┌────────┐ Structured     ┌────────┐            │

│ │ Agent A│──────────────────          │ Agent B│──────────────────                │ Agent C│   │

│ └────────┘ Handoff         └────────┘ Handoff          └────────┘         │

│                                             │

│ USE: Content pipeline (Research → Write → Edit → Verify)                  │

│ CONTRACT: Each agent produces output matching next agent's input schema                   │

│                                             │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 2: REVIEW & REFINE                                │

│ ─────────────────────────                                   │

│ Agent A produces → Agent B reviews → Agent A refines based on feedback                │

│                                             │

│ ┌────────┐ Draft      ┌────────┐                         │

│ │ Writer │─────────────        │ Editor │                             │

│ │ Agent │         │ Agent │                        │

│ └────────┘          └────┬───┘                          │

│    ▲              │ Feedback                      │

│    └───────────────────────┘                                  │

│                                             │

│ USE: Content quality improvement (Write → Edit → Rewrite)                     │

│ MAX ITERATIONS: 2 (prevent infinite loops)                            │

│                                             │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 3: PARALLEL PROCESSING                                    │

│ ──────────────────────────────                                        │

│ Single input → multiple agents process in parallel → aggregate results            │
│                                          │

│            ┌────────┐                           │

│         ┌───     │ Agent B│───┐                         │

│         │ └────────┘ │                              │

│ ┌────────┐      │ ┌────────┐ │ ┌──────────┐                        │

│ │ Agent A│─────┼───       │ Agent C│───┼───         │Aggregator│                       │

│ └────────┘      │ └────────┘ │ └──────────┘                        │

│         │ ┌────────┐ │                              │

│         └───     │ Agent D│───┘                          │

│            └────────┘                           │

│                                          │

│ USE: Multi-platform adaptation, ensemble verification                  │

│                                          │

│                                          │

│ PATTERN 4: CONSENSUS                                    │

│ ─────────────────────                                    │

│ Multiple agents evaluate same input → consensus determines output                  │

│                                          │

│ ┌────────┐                                      │

│ │ Agent A│──┐                                   │

│ └────────┘ │ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────┐                                 │

│ ┌────────┐ ├───       │ Consensus │───       │ Final │                         │

│ │ Agent B│──┤ │ Mechanism │ │ Verdict │                       │

│ └────────┘ │ └──────────────┘ └──────────┘                                 │

│ ┌────────┐ │                                    │

│ │ Agent C│──┘                                   │
│ └────────┘                                         │

│                                             │

│ USE: Fact-checking critical claims, content safety decisions       │

│                                             │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 5: BROADCAST & RESPOND                                 │

│ ──────────────────────────────                                 │

│ Agent broadcasts event → any interested agent can respond               │

│                                             │

│ ┌────────┐                                         │

│ │ Agent A│──       Event Bus ──    Agent B (subscribed)                │

│ └────────┘           ──     Agent C (subscribed)               │

│               ──     Agent D (subscribed)                 │

│                                             │

│ USE: Content published event → Analytics, Monetisation, Notifications       │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



11.2 Agent Handoff Protocol



```

AGENT HANDOFF PROTOCOL

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──
Every agent-to-agent handoff follows a standardised protocol:



1. OUTPUT SCHEMA VALIDATION

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Producing agent's output validated against consumer's input schema│

 │ Schema registry maps agent output types to input types                       │

 │ Validation failure → workflow error handler                          │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



2. CONTEXT ENRICHMENT

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Orchestrator enriches handoff with:                          │

 │ • Correlation ID (links entire pipeline execution)                   │

 │ • Causation ID (previous agent's execution ID)                       │

 │ • Tenant/Brand context                           │

 │ • Pipeline state summary                             │

 │ • Relevant memory context                                │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



3. HANDOFF RECORD

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Every handoff recorded as ProvenanceEvent:                               │

 │ • From agent (type, version, execution ID)                       │

 │ • To agent (type, version, execution ID)                     │

 │ • Input summary (hash, size, key fields)                     │

 │ • Timestamp                                  │
  │ • Correlation context                         │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



4. QUALITY GATE (Optional per workflow configuration)

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ Before handoff, output evaluated against quality gate:            │

  │ • Confidence score ≥ threshold?                       │

  │ • Required fields present?                        │

  │ • Safety check passed?                            │

  │ Gate failure → routing decision (retry / fallback / human)        │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



5. HANDOFF COMPLETION

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ Consumer agent acknowledges receipt                           │

  │ Orchestrator records handoff completion                       │

  │ Pipeline state updated                            │

  │ Next workflow step determined                             │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```



---



12. AGENT COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS



```
AGENT COMMUNICATION PROTOCOLS

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



1. DIRECT INVOCATION (Orchestrator → Agent)

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Protocol: Function call with standardised request/response           │

 │ Sync/Async: Synchronous with timeout                         │

 │ Contract: IAgent.execute(request) → Promise<AgentResponse>                   │

 │ Use: Pipeline stage execution                        │

 │ Retry: Configurable per agent type                       │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



2. EVENT-DRIVEN COMMUNICATION (Agent → Agent via Event Bus)

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Protocol: Event publication/subscription                     │

 │ Sync/Async: Asynchronous                             │

 │ Contract: Standard event envelope + domain-specific payload              │

 │ Use: Cross-cutting concerns, analytics, notifications            │

 │ Delivery: At-least-once (P1-P2); Exactly-once (P3+)              │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



3. AGENT REGISTRY DISCOVERY

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Protocol: Registry lookup                        │

 │ Sync/Async: Synchronous (cached)                         │
  │ Contract: Registry API → Agent metadata, capabilities, status │

  │ Use: Orchestrator discovers available agents and capabilities │

  │ Cache: Registry data cached with configurable TTL                 │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



4. AGENT HEALTH CHECK

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ Protocol: Health endpoint call                    │

  │ Sync/Async: Synchronous                          │

  │ Contract: GET /health → { status, version, modelStatus, ... } │

  │ Use: Orchestrator verifies agent availability before invocation │

  │ Frequency: Before each invocation + periodic (configurable)           │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



5. STREAMING RESPONSE (Phase 2+)

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ Protocol: Server-Sent Events or WebSocket                     │

  │ Sync/Async: Asynchronous stream                       │

  │ Contract: AsyncIterable<AgentChunk>                       │

  │ Use: Long-form content generation with progressive delivery           │

  │ Backpressure: Consumer controls stream pace                       │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

13. AI MODEL ARCHITECTURE

```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

│ │ }                                     │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘

│ │ │                                    │ │ │

│ │ │ • Custom fine-tuned models (Phase 3+)                    │ │ │

│ │ │                       3. GPT-4o            │       │ │

│ │                                           │ │
│ │ Budget Check → Can we use premium model?                          │ │

│ │    │                                    │ │

│ │         threshold                             │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ Cost Factors:                                 │ │

│ │ • Content value classification (high/medium/low)                  │ │

│ │ • Time-of-day pricing (if applicable)                     │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

14.2 Fallback Strategy



```

FALLBACK STRATEGY

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



FALLBACK TRIGGERS:
1. Primary model returns error (5xx, timeout, rate limit)

2. Primary model latency exceeds threshold

3. Primary model returns low-confidence output

4. Primary model provider health check fails



FALLBACK CHAIN EXECUTION:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                        │

│ Try Primary Model                                   │

│   │                                     │

│   ├── SUCCESS → Return result                                   │

│   │                                     │

│   └── FAILURE → Log primary failure                             │

│            │                            │

│            ▼                                │

│        Try Fallback 1                           │

│            │                            │

│            ├── SUCCESS → Return result + Log fallback used │

│            │                            │

│            └── FAILURE → Try Fallback 2                     │

│                         │               │

│                         ├── SUCCESS → Return result │

│                         │               │

│                         └── FAILURE → Escalate          │

│                                │        │

│                                ▼            │
│                            Dead Letter Queue        │

│                            + Alert Generation   │

│                            + Human Review Option │

│                                         │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



FALLBACK CONFIGURATION PER AGENT TYPE:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ AGENT TYPE            MAX FALLBACKS FALLBACK STRATEGY                   │

│ ──────────            ───────────── ─────────────────                   │

│ Writer (Premium) 2             Alternate provider → economy         │

│ Writer (Standard) 2            Economy → alternate economy          │

│ FactChecker           3      Ensemble → premium → standard │

│ Editor        2           Alternate provider → economy      │

│ Safety Classifier 1          Local model fallback       │

│ Discovery         2         Economy → alternate economy         │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

15.2 Prompt Version Control



```

PROMPT VERSIONING SYSTEM

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



PROMPT IDENTIFIER: {agent-type}-{task}-v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}

Example: writer-agent-article-generation-v2.1.3



VERSION INCREMENT RULES:

• MAJOR: Fundamental change in prompt strategy or behaviour

• MINOR: New feature, instruction, or significant improvement

• PATCH: Bug fix, clarification, minor wording change



PROMPT REPOSITORY STRUCTURE:

prompts/

├── writer-agent/
│ ├── article-generation/

│ │ ├── v2.1.3.yaml

│ │ ├── v2.1.2.yaml

│ │ ├── v2.0.0.yaml

│ │ └── metadata.yaml

│ ├── social-post-generation/

│ └── headline-generation/

├── fact-checker-agent/

│ └── claim-verification/

└── shared/

     ├── safety-instructions/

     └── brand-overlays/



PROMPT METADATA:

version: "2.1.3"

status: "active"        # "draft" | "testing" | "active" | "deprecated"

created: "2026-08-07"

author: "ai-engineering-team"

performance: {

    qualityScore: 87.3,

    successRate: 0.964,

    avgLatency: 3200,

    costPerUse: 0.012

}

abTest: {

    testId: "AB-2026-042",
    variant: "B",

    improvement: "+3.2% quality score"

}

16. AI MEMORY ARCHITECTURE



16.1 Memory System Overview



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│                   AI MEMORY ARCHITECTURE                   │

│                                            │

│ MEMORY TYPES AND THEIR ROLES:                                  │

│                                            │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                  WORKING MEMORY                   │ │

│ │                                       │ │

│ │ SCOPE: Single agent execution                      │ │

│ │ LIFETIME: Duration of agent invocation                   │ │

│ │ CONTENT: Task input, context, instructions, response             │ │

│ │ IMPLEMENTATION: Context window of LLM call                       │ │

│ │ SIZE LIMIT: Model context window (8K-200K tokens)                │ │
│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                            │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │              EPISODIC MEMORY                         │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ SCOPE: Content pipeline execution / brand / tenant                 │ │

│ │ LIFETIME: Configurable (default: 90 days rolling)                │ │

│ │ CONTENT: Previous content, editorial decisions, corrections             │ │

│ │ IMPLEMENTATION: Vector store + metadata in PostgreSQL/Redis                    │ │

│ │ RETRIEVAL: Semantic similarity search on embeddings                     │ │

│ │ USE CASES:                                     │ │

│ │ • "Write in similar style to our top-performing articles"          │ │

│ │ • "Avoid repeating topics covered in last 7 days"                │ │

│ │ • "Recall editorial feedback from similar content"                │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                            │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │              SEMANTIC MEMORY                         │ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ SCOPE: Global / Brand / Domain                             │ │

│ │ LIFETIME: Persistent (versioned)                       │ │

│ │ CONTENT: Brand guidelines, style guides, verified facts,           │ │

│ │      platform best practices, editorial policies            │ │

│ │ IMPLEMENTATION: PostgreSQL + Vector embeddings                           │ │

│ │ RETRIEVAL: Hybrid (keyword + semantic)                       │ │

│ │ USE CASES:                                     │ │
│ │ • Brand voice and style enforcement                         │ │

│ │ • Platform algorithm knowledge base                         │ │

│ │ • Editorial policy compliance                         │ │

│ │ • Verified fact database                         │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                           │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │              PROCEDURAL MEMORY                         │ │

│ │                                       │ │

│ │ SCOPE: Global / Agent-specific                        │ │

│ │ LIFETIME: Continuously updated                          │ │

│ │ CONTENT: Optimised prompts, model selection patterns,                 │ │

│ │      effective strategies, performance correlations           │ │

│ │ IMPLEMENTATION: Analytics-derived configuration                     │ │

│ │ UPDATE MECHANISM: Performance feedback loop                          │ │

│ │ USE CASES:                                   │ │

│ │ • "This prompt variant performs 15% better for tech content"          │ │

│ │ • "Use GPT-4o for finance content, Claude for creative"             │ │

│ │ • "Publish LinkedIn content between 9-11am for best engagement"             │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```



16.2 Memory Retrieval Architecture
```

MEMORY RETRIEVAL FLOW

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                 MEMORY RETRIEVAL PIPELINE                        │

│                                          │

│ 1. QUERY FORMULATION                                        │

│     ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│     │ • Current task and context analysed                      │ │

│     │ • Retrieval queries generated:                   │ │

│     │ - Semantic query (embedding-based)                         │ │

│     │ - Metadata query (filtering by date, type, brand, etc.) │ │

│     │ - Hybrid query (combination)                         │ │

│     └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                   │                       │

│                   ▼                           │

│ 2. PARALLEL RETRIEVAL                                  │

│     ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│     │                                   │ │

│     │ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐               │ │

│     │ │ Semantic │ │ Episodic │ │ Procedural │                  │ │

│     │ │ Memory        │ │ Memory       │ │ Memory          │     │ │

│     │ │ Store     │ │ Store    │ │ Store          │   │ │

│     │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘                 │ │
│   │     │           │          │        │ │

│   │     ▼               ▼          ▼             │ │

│   │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│   │ │         RETRIEVAL RESULTS                    │ │ │

│   │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                 │                        │

│                 ▼                            │

│ 3. RESULT RANKING & FILTERING                                  │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Relevance scoring (semantic similarity + metadata match) │ │

│   │ • Recency boost (newer content weighted higher)                  │ │

│   │ • Performance boost (successful content weighted higher) │ │

│   │ • Diversity filter (avoid redundant results)               │ │

│   │ • Top-K selection (configurable K per memory type)               │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                 │                        │

│                 ▼                            │

│ 4. CONTEXT INTEGRATION                                     │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Retrieved memories formatted for LLM context window                  │ │

│   │ • Prioritised within context window constraints                │ │

│   │ • Source attribution maintained                    │ │

│   │ • Integrated into agent prompt                     │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

17. CONTEXT WINDOW MANAGEMENT



```

CONTEXT WINDOW MANAGEMENT STRATEGY

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



CONTEXT BUDGET ALLOCATION:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                         │

│ TOTAL CONTEXT WINDOW (e.g., 128K tokens)              │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                 │

│                                         │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ SYSTEM PROMPT (20-30%)                       │ │

│ │ • Agent identity, role, core instructions     │ │

│ │ • Brand voice and guidelines                │ │

│ │ • Safety and ethical constraints            │ │

│ │ • Output format specification               │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                         │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ RETRIEVED MEMORY (20-30%)                              │ │

│ │ • Relevant episodic memories (past content, feedback)              │ │

│ │ • Relevant semantic memories (guidelines, facts)             │ │

│ │ • Procedural memories (optimised strategies)                 │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                           │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ TASK CONTEXT (40-50%)                           │ │

│ │ • Task description and instructions                  │ │

│ │ • Input data (brief, research, draft)              │ │

│ │ • Examples (few-shot)                          │ │

│ │ • Current state and constraints                    │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                           │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ RESPONSE BUDGET (remaining tokens)                         │ │

│ │ • Reserved for model output                        │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



CONTENT TRUNCATION STRATEGIES:

1. SUMMARISATION: Long content summarised to key points

2. PRIORITISATION: Most relevant sections included first

3. CHUNKING: Content split across multiple calls with continuity

4. PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE: High-level first, detail on demand

5. REFERENCE REPLACEMENT: Full text replaced with references + summaries
```

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                      │

VECTOR STORE STRATEGY:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                      │
│ Phase 1: PostgreSQL with pgvector                                │

│ • Zero additional infrastructure                             │

│ • Adequate for MVP-scale vector search                                │

│ • Simple integration with existing database                           │

│                                          │

│ Phase 2: Redis with vector search (or continue pgvector)                  │

│ • Lower latency for high-frequency retrieval                          │

│ • In-memory performance                                      │

│                                          │

│ Phase 3+: Dedicated vector database (Pinecone/Qdrant/Weaviate)                │

│ • Purpose-built for vector search at scale                        │

│ • Advanced filtering and hybrid search                           │

│ • Multi-tenancy support                                  │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



VECTOR STORE SCHEMA:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ Collection: episodic_memory                                  │

│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │{                                     │ │

│ │ id: "uuid",                                │ │

│ │ tenantId: "string",                          │ │

│ │ brandId: "string",                           │ │

│ │ contentType: "article" | "social_post" | ...,                  │ │

│ │ contentId: "uuid",                               │ │
│ │ text: "content text or summary",                         │ │

│ │ embedding: [...], // 1536-dimension vector                     │ │

│ │ metadata: {                                  │ │

│ │    title: "string",                        │ │

│ │    publishedAt: "ISO8601",                           │ │

│ │    performance: { engagement: 0.85, ... },                 │ │

│ │    topics: ["AI", "regulation"],                   │ │

│ │    qualityScore: 87                            │ │

│ │ },                                   │ │

│ │ createdAt: "ISO8601"                               │ │

│ │}                                     │ │

│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

```

20. VERIFICATION & TRUTH-SEEKING ARCHITECTURE



20.1 Multi-Layer Verification System



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│             MULTI-LAYER VERIFICATION ARCHITECTURE                      │

│                                              │
│ LAYER 1: SOURCE VERIFICATION (During Research)                       │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                  │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ • Source credibility scoring before information is used          │ │

│ │ • Multi-source requirement for key facts                  │ │

│ │ • Contradiction detection across sources                  │ │

│ │ • Source freshness and relevance check                    │ │

│ │ • Research brief confidence scoring per fact              │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                              │

│ LAYER 2: GENERATION-TIME VERIFICATION (During Writing)                     │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────                               │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ • Writer agent constrained to verified research facts           │ │

│ │ • Factual claim generation linked to research sources            │ │

│ │ • Internal consistency check (no self-contradiction)        │ │

│ │ • Brand safety boundary enforcement                       │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                              │

│ LAYER 3: POST-GENERATION VERIFICATION (After Writing)                     │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────                              │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ • Fact-Checker Agent: Claim extraction and source verification         │ │

│ │ • Plagiarism Detector: Originality verification           │ │

│ │ • Editor Agent: Logical consistency and quality review           │ │

│ │ • Safety Classifier: Content safety verification          │ │
│ │ • Quality Scorer: Composite quality assessment                     │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                            │

│ LAYER 4: PUBLISHING-TIME VERIFICATION                                 │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                       │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ • Platform compliance check                              │ │

│ │ • Final safety screening                           │ │

│ │ • Disclosure requirement verification                        │ │

│ │ • Rate limit and quota check                          │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                            │

│ LAYER 5: POST-PUBLICATION VERIFICATION                                │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────                                        │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │ • Audience feedback monitoring (corrections, flags)                 │ │

│ │ • Performance anomaly detection (low engagement = possible issue) │ │

│ │ • Periodic re-verification of evergreen content                │ │

│ │ • Correction workflow trigger if issues detected                   │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                                            │

│ TRUTH-SEEKING DESIGN:                                      │

│ ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│ │                                         │ │

│ │ CORE PRINCIPLE: Agents are designed to seek truth, not optimise                  │ │

│ │ for engagement.                                    │ │
│ │                                        │ │

│ │ IMPLEMENTATION:                                 │ │

│ │ • System prompts prioritise accuracy over engagement            │ │

│ │ • Reward functions include accuracy metrics              │ │

│ │ • Confidence thresholds enforced at multiple stages            │ │

│ │ • Uncertainty is acceptable—marked as such, not hidden           │ │

│ │ • "I don't know" is a valid and encouraged response when appropriate │ │

│ │ • Corrections are prompt and transparent                 │ │

│ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┘

```

21. HALLUCINATION DETECTION & PREVENTION



```

HALLUCINATION DETECTION & PREVENTION ARCHITECTURE

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



HALLUCINATION TYPES ADDRESSED:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                      │

│ 1. FACTUAL HALLUCINATION: Stating facts not in source material     │

│ 2. SOURCE HALLUCINATION: Citing non-existent or incorrect sources │
│ 3. LOGICAL HALLUCINATION: Drawing incorrect conclusions from facts │

│ 4. CONTEXTUAL HALLUCINATION: Misrepresenting source context                  │

│ 5. TEMPORAL HALLUCINATION: Outdated or anachronistic information                 │

│ 6. ATTRIBUTION HALLUCINATION: Misattributing statements or quotes │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



PREVENTION STRATEGIES:



1. GROUNDED GENERATION

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ • Writer agent required to cite research sources for factual        │

 │ claims                                   │

 │ • Generation constrained to information in research brief           │

 │ • "Unknown" or "unverified" markers for ungrounded claims               │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



2. CLAIM-BY-CLAIM VERIFICATION

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ • Every factual claim extracted and individually verified       │

 │ • Claim classification: verifiable vs. opinion vs. common knowledge│

 │ • Different verification strategy per claim type            │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



3. CROSS-MODEL VERIFICATION (Phase 2+)

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ • Same claim verified by different models                   │
  │ • Disagreement triggers deeper verification                    │

  │ • Ensemble confidence scoring                          │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



4. SOURCE GROUNDING VALIDATION

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ • Verify cited sources actually exist and contain cited info       │

  │ • URL validation and content retrieval                     │

  │ • Quote verification against original source                   │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



5. KNOWLEDGE CUTOFF AWARENESS

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ • Each model's training cutoff date tracked                    │

  │ • Claims about events after cutoff flagged for verification        │

  │ • Research agent provides current information to fill gap          │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



DETECTION METRICS:

• Hallucination rate (verified hallucinations per content piece)

• Source attribution accuracy (correct source for claim)

• Claim verification pass rate

• Correction frequency (post-publication corrections)

```

22. CONTENT SAFETY ARCHITECTURE



```

CONTENT SAFETY ARCHITECTURE

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



SAFETY LAYERS:



LAYER 1: PROMPT-LEVEL SAFETY

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Safety instructions embedded in every agent's system prompt             │

│ • Content boundaries explicitly defined                       │

│ • Prohibited topics and behaviours listed                     │

│ • Disclosure requirements specified                       │

│ • LIMITATION: Prompt-level safety is bypassable                   │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



LAYER 2: INPUT VALIDATION

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Input sanitisation before processing                    │

│ • Prompt injection detection                          │

│ • Source content filtering (block known malicious sources)            │

│ • Research data validation                        │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
LAYER 3: OUTPUT CLASSIFICATION (Primary Defence)

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Safety Classifier Agent reviews all generated content                   │

│ • Independent from generation model (different architecture)                  │

│ • Multi-category classification                     │

│ • Configurable per brand and content type                         │

│ • Automatic rejection of violating content                    │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



LAYER 4: HUMAN ESCALATION

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • Borderline cases escalated for human review                         │

│ • Human decisions fed back to improve classifiers                     │

│ • Emergency content takedown capability                           │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



LAYER 5: AUDIT & MONITORING

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ • All safety decisions logged and auditable                   │

│ • Safety violation trends monitored                       │

│ • Regular safety model evaluation and updates                         │

│ • Red-teaming exercises (Phase 2+)                        │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



SAFETY POLICY CONFIGURATION:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ SAFETY LEVEL DESCRIPTION                 USE CASE             │

│ ─────────── ───────────                  ────────             │

│ Permissive    Block only critical      Entertainment content       │

│          violations                          │

│ Standard     Block critical + high     General content        │

│          violations; flag medium                    │

│ Strict     Block critical + high     Finance, health, news │

│          + medium violations                      │

│ Maximum        Block all flagged        Children's content,    │

│          content; human review all regulated industries │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

23. BIAS DETECTION & MITIGATION



```

BIAS DETECTION & MITIGATION ARCHITECTURE

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



BIAS DIMENSIONS MONITORED:

1. POLITICAL BIAS: Partisan slant in content selection and framing
2. DEMOGRAPHIC BIAS: Representation bias across groups

3. SOURCE BIAS: Over-reliance on specific viewpoint sources

4. TOPIC BIAS: Systematic over/under coverage of topics

5. LANGUAGE BIAS: Tone and framing differences across subjects

6. CONFIRMATION BIAS: Favouring information confirming existing narratives



DETECTION METHODS:



1. CONTENT ANALYSIS

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ • Sentiment analysis across topics and subjects               │

 │ • Framing analysis (how topics are presented)                 │

 │ • Source diversity metrics                        │

 │ • Topic coverage distribution analysis                    │

 │ • Comparative analysis with baseline (diverse human-written)              │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



2. SOURCE DIVERSITY MONITORING

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ • Track source political/ideological lean distribution        │

 │ • Alert on source concentration                       │

 │ • Require minimum source diversity for controversial topics           │

 │ • Cross-reference sources across ideological spectrum             │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



3. OUTPUT AUDITING
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

  │ • Regular bias audits by external evaluators        │

  │ • Blind comparison with human-written content           │

  │ • Audience perception surveys on fairness           │

  │ • Automated bias scoring using specialised models       │

  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



MITIGATION STRATEGIES:

• Diverse source requirements in research agent

• Bias-awareness instructions in writer agent prompts

• Editor agent bias review pass

• Override capability for Editorial Director

• Regular bias training data updates

• Transparency in content selection rationale

```

27. A/B TESTING FRAMEWORK FOR AI



```

A/B TESTING FRAMEWORK

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
──



TESTABLE AI COMPONENTS:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                       │

│ COMPONENT            WHAT CAN BE TESTED                      │

│ ─────────          ─────────────────                     │

│ Prompts          Variant A vs. Variant B system prompts          │
│ Models              Different models for same task           │

│ Parameters           Temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty               │

│ Agent Configurations Different agent sequences or rules                  │

│ Quality Thresholds      Different auto-publish thresholds            │

│ Scheduling           Different publishing time strategies        │

│ Adaptation           Different platform adaptation strategies        │

│                                          │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



A/B TESTING ARCHITECTURE:



┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│                                          │

│ 1. EXPERIMENT DESIGN                                     │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Hypothesis definition                       │ │

│   │ • Success metrics definition                     │ │

│   │ • Sample size calculation                        │ │

│   │ • Duration estimation                         │ │

│   │ • Variant configuration                       │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                 │                         │

│                 ▼                             │

│ 2. TRAFFIC SPLITTING                                 │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Random assignment at content creation time                 │ │
│   │ • Consistent hashing (same topic → same variant)               │ │

│   │ • Configurable split ratio (default 50/50)              │ │

│   │ • Brand-level or content-type-level scoping              │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                  │                        │

│                  ▼                            │

│ 3. EXECUTION & MONITORING                                    │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Content produced with variant configuration                 │ │

│   │ • Performance metrics collected per variant                  │ │

│   │ • Real-time monitoring for safety issues                │ │

│   │ • Automatic kill switch if critical issues detected      │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                  │                        │

│                  ▼                            │

│ 4. ANALYSIS & DECISION                                  │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│   │ • Statistical significance testing                │ │

│   │ • Effect size calculation                     │ │

│   │ • Segment analysis (different effects by content type?)        │ │

│   │ • Recommendation: promote, iterate, or discard                 │ │

│   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

│                  │                        │

│                  ▼                            │

│ 5. ROLLOUT                                        │

│   ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│     │ • Winner becomes new default                    │ │

│     │ • Gradual rollout (canary → 10% → 50% → 100%)            │ │

│     │ • Previous version retained for rollback         │ │

│     │ • Experiment results documented in knowledge base         │ │

│     └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



A/B TEST GOVERNANCE:

• All tests require approval (automated for low-risk, manual for high-risk)

• Content safety maintained across all variants

• Audience trust preserved (no deceptive testing)

• Test duration minimums enforced for statistical validity

• Results and decisions documented as ADRs

```

29. AI COST MANAGEMENT



```

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Cache identical/similar AI responses                  │

 │ Semantic similarity matching for near-duplicate requests          │

 │ Savings: 5-15% (varies by content type)                   │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



3. PROMPT OPTIMISATION

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Minimise prompt token count while maintaining quality             │

 │ Remove redundant instructions                      │

 │ Compress examples and context                         │

 │ Savings: 10-20% per invocation                    │

 └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘



4. BATCH PROCESSING

 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

 │ Batch multiple requests where supported by API                │
    │ Savings: 25-50% on supported APIs                        │

    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

33. AI-SPECIFIC RISKS & MITIGATIONS



Risk ID Risk Description Likelihood Impact Mitigation

AIR-1 LLM hallucination in published content Medium Critical Multi-layer verification; fact-
checker agent; human review for critical content; source grounding
AIR-2 AI bias in content selection or framing Medium High Diverse source requirements; bias
detection; regular audits; editorial override

AIR-3 Prompt injection attack compromises agent behaviour Medium High Input sanitisation;
prompt structure isolation; output validation; safety classifier

AIR-4 Model API outage halts content pipeline Medium High Multi-provider architecture;
fallback chains; local model fallback for critical tasks

AIR-5 AI cost overruns exceed budget Medium Medium Cost tracking; budget alerts; model
cascading; spending caps

AIR-6 Agent quality degradation over time Medium Medium Continuous monitoring; automated
quality regression testing; prompt versioning

AIR-7 Multi-agent collaboration failures Medium Medium Robust orchestration; error recovery;
dead letter queues; monitoring

AIR-8 Safety classifier bypass Low Critical Multi-layer safety; independent classifier; human
escalation; red-teaming

AIR-9 Model provider deprecates critical model Low High Model abstraction; multi-provider;
prompt portability; model evaluation pipeline

AIR-10 Embedding drift reduces RAG quality Low Medium Regular embedding evaluation; re-
embedding pipeline; hybrid retrieval fallback

34. ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS (AI-SPECIFIC)



ADR-AI-001: Multi-Agent Architecture Over Single-Model



Field Detail

ADR ID ADR-AI-2026-001

Status Accepted

Context Choose between a single large model handling all content tasks vs. specialised agents.
Decision Multi-agent architecture with specialised agents for each pipeline stage.

Rationale Specialised agents can be independently optimised, use different models, have
targeted prompts, and be evaluated separately. This enables quality improvements in one area
without risking others.

Consequences Increased orchestration complexity; requires agent handoff protocols; higher
total prompt engineering effort; enables independent scaling.



ADR-AI-002: Verification-First Design



Field Detail

ADR ID ADR-AI-2026-002

Status Accepted

Context Position of verification in the content pipeline.

Decision Verification embedded throughout pipeline, not as final gate only. Source verification
during research, generation constrained to verified facts, post-generation fact-checking, and
ongoing post-publication monitoring.

Rationale Trust is the primary differentiator. Multi-layer verification catches errors early and
provides defence in depth. Post-hoc verification alone is insufficient for autonomous operation.

Consequences Higher initial latency; more complex pipeline; higher AI cost per piece;
significantly higher accuracy.



ADR-AI-003: Model Cascade for Cost Optimisation



Field Detail

ADR ID ADR-AI-2026-003

Status Accepted

Context How to balance AI quality and cost across diverse content tasks.
Decision Implement model cascade architecture—route tasks to cheapest capable model based
on complexity, quality requirements, and content value.

Rationale Not all content requires premium models. Routine social posts can use economy
models; long-form analysis requires premium. This optimises the cost-quality trade-off.

Consequences Model routing logic required; task classification needed; may occasionally route
to suboptimal model; significant cost savings.



ADR-AI-004: Prompt as Code



Field Detail

ADR ID ADR-AI-2026-004

Status Accepted

Context How to manage prompt templates across agents, brands, and versions.

Decision Treat prompts as code—version-controlled, tested, reviewed, and deployed through
CI/CD pipeline. Prompt changes require testing against evaluation sets before deployment.

Rationale Prompts are critical infrastructure determining content quality and safety. Ad-hoc
prompt changes create quality and safety risks. Engineering discipline around prompts ensures
reliability.

Consequences Prompt change process slower than direct editing; requires prompt testing
infrastructure; enables safe prompt evolution.



---



35. ENTERPRISE AI RECOMMENDATIONS



Recommendation 1: Invest in the Verification Architecture First
The verification system (Fact-Checker, Plagiarism Detector, Quality Scorer, Safety Classifier) is the
primary differentiator. Allocate significant Phase 1 resources to building robust verification
before optimising content generation quality.



Recommendation 2: Build the Agent Orchestration Framework for Extensibility



Design the Orchestrator with future agent types in mind. The ability to add new agents without
modifying the orchestration core will determine how quickly the platform can evolve.



Recommendation 3: Start Prompt Engineering Discipline Immediately



Establish prompt version control, testing, and review processes from the first agent
implementation. Prompt discipline is much harder to retrofit than to build from the start.



Recommendation 4: Implement Comprehensive AI Observability



AI-specific telemetry (traces with prompt hashes, token counts, model decisions, confidence
scores) is essential for debugging, optimisation, and compliance. Build this before you need it.



Recommendation 5: Plan for Model Independence



While Phase 1 will use specific commercial models, design the model abstraction layer to
support easy provider switching. The AI model market is evolving rapidly—provider
independence is a strategic necessity.



Recommendation 6: Establish the AI Ethics Committee Before Content Publication
Ethical governance must be in place before autonomous content reaches audiences. The
committee should review and approve all agent types and content categories before they go
live.



Recommendation 7: Design for Progressive Autonomy



Begin with higher human oversight and systematically reduce it as quality metrics demonstrate
reliability. This builds trust with operators and audiences while managing risk.



Recommendation 8: Budget for AI Costs Realistically



AI API costs will be the largest operational expense. Implement cost tracking and budgeting
from day one. Plan the transition to open-source models for high-volume tasks in Phase 2.

36. CONCLUSION



This Volume 4 establishes the complete AI & Machine Learning Architecture for the Agbofa
Nexus AI platform. The architecture transforms the platform from a conventional software
system into an autonomous AI media company operated by a collaborative ecosystem of
specialised AI agents.



Key Achievements:



1. Complete AI Agent Ecosystem: Defined 15+ specialised agent types across content pipeline,
verification, analytics, publishing, monetisation, and operations domains.

2. Multi-Agent Collaboration Framework: Established patterns for sequential handoff, review-
refine, parallel processing, consensus, and broadcast-respond collaboration.
3. Verification-First Architecture: Multi-layer verification system embedding truth-seeking
throughout the content pipeline—from source verification through post-publication monitoring.

4. Model Architecture: Provider-independent abstraction layer with model cascade routing
optimising the cost-quality trade-off across diverse content tasks.

5. Memory Architecture: Working, episodic, semantic, and procedural memory systems
enabling agents to learn from experience and maintain brand consistency.

6. Safety Architecture: Multi-layer defence including prompt-level safety, input validation,
independent safety classification, and human escalation.

7. Continuous Learning: Performance feedback loops, human feedback integration, A/B testing
framework, and model evaluation systems for ongoing improvement.

8. AIOps: Comprehensive AI operations including monitoring, alerting, cost management, and
incident response.



The architecture is now ready for detailed implementation in:



· Volume 5: Software Architecture & Design (component specifications, API contracts, database
schemas)

· Subsequent volumes covering infrastructure, security, and operations

PART I: FOUNDATIONS



---



1. THE AGENT PHILOSOPHY



1.1 What Agbofa Agents Are



Agbofa AI agents are not chatbots. They are not prompt templates. They are not API wrappers
around large language models.



An Agbofa agent is a persistent, specialised, collaborative AI entity with:



Attribute Description

Identity A defined role, purpose, and personality within the media organisation

Expertise Deep specialisation in a specific media function

Memory Persistent recall of past work, decisions, and learnings

Agency Ability to make decisions within defined boundaries

Accountability Every action logged, explained, and auditable

Collaboration Ability to work with other agents and humans

Self-Improvement Capacity to learn from outcomes and feedback



An Agbofa agent is more analogous to a skilled employee than a software function. It has a role,
responsibilities, performance expectations, and a career trajectory of improvement.
1.2 The Media Company Metaphor



Agbofa Nexus AI is architected as a complete media company staffed by AI agents:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

1.3 Agent Principles



These principles govern the design and behaviour of every agent in the ecosystem:



Principle Description

P1: Specialisation Over Generalisation Each agent does one thing exceptionally well. No single
agent handles the entire content pipeline.
P2: Collaboration Over Isolation Agents are designed to work together. Handoffs are explicit,
structured, and validated.

P3: Transparency Over Opacity Every agent decision is explainable. Reasoning is captured
alongside output.

P4: Learning Over Static Behaviour Agents improve from every piece of content, every human
feedback, every performance signal.

P5: Safety Over Speed Content safety and accuracy take precedence over publishing velocity.

P6: Human Sovereignty Humans set boundaries. Agents operate within them. Humans can
override any decision.

P7: Brand Consistency Every agent enforces brand voice, guidelines, and quality standards.

P8: Cost Awareness Agents make cost-aware decisions about model usage, research depth, and
processing.

P9: Graceful Degradation When optimal resources are unavailable, agents adapt rather than fail.

P10: Continuous Observability Agent behaviour is monitored, measured, and audited at all
times.
