III.3 ONE STORY, MANY OUTPUTS



III.3.1 The Derivative Generation Model



The canonical Story contains the complete intelligence. Platform-specific outputs are
derivatives—generated, not duplicated:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│         ONE STORY → MANY PLATFORM OUTPUTS                            │

│            The Derivative Model                            │

│                                            │

│              ┌─────────────────┐                               │

│              │ STORY GRAPH │                               │

│              │ (Canonical) │                       │

│              │          │                      │

│              │ • Full content │                        │

│              │ • All sources │                     │

│              │ • All claims │                      │

│              │ • All entities │                    │

│              │ • All versions │                    │
│              │ • All media │                           │

│              └────────┬────────┘                                   │

│                   │                            │

│                   │ FORMAT ADAPTATION AGENT                                │

│                   │ (AGB-MME-FMT-001)                          │

│                   │                            │

│        ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐                                       │

│        │           │            │                  │

│        ▼               ▼            ▼                  │

│ ┌───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────┐                                      │

│ │ WEB ARTICLE         │ │ SOCIAL MEDIA      │ │ EMAIL/NEWSLETTER │                     │

│ │ ───────────── │ │ ───────────── │ │ ──────────────── │                                   │

│ │ • Full content │ │               ││           │          │

│ │ • Full context │ │ PLATFORM VARIANTS: │ │ • Summarised                       │       │

│ │ • All media     ││            │ │ • Personalised │                   │

│ │ • SEO optimised │ │ • X (Twitter)       │ │ • Curated        │               │

│ │ • Related links │ │ • Facebook        │ │ • Scheduled            │           │

│ │ • Full provenance │ │ • LinkedIn       │ │ • Tracked         │               │

│ └───────────────────┘ │ • Instagram            │ └───────────────────┘                             │

│              │ • Threads       │                       │

│ ┌───────────────────┐ │ • TikTok             │ ┌───────────────────┐                           │

│ │ AUDIO/VISUAL         │ │ • YouTube      │ │ MOBILE/APP               │           │

│ │ ───────────── │ └───────────────────┘ │ ───────────── │                                      │

│ │ • Audio brief   │                │ • Mobile card     │           │

│ │ • Podcast version │                │ • Push notification│                │

│ │ • Video brief   │                │ • Offline support │               │
│ │ • Infographic   │              │ • Swipe format │          │

│ └───────────────────┘                    └───────────────────┘            │

│                                             │

│ KEY PRINCIPLE:                                      │

│ Every derivative links back to the canonical Story. When the Story       │

│ is updated or corrected, ALL derivatives are refreshed automatically.     │

│ Factual consistency is guaranteed because there is only one source of truth. │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



III.4 GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE & STORY RELATIONSHIPS



III.4.1 Story Relationships in the Graph



Stories do not exist in isolation. The Story Graph explicitly models relationships between stories,
creating a web of editorial intelligence:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           STORY RELATIONSHIP TYPES                          │

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│
│ │ FOLLOWS_UP — Temporal sequence                                 ││

│ │ Story A → FOLLOWS_UP → Story B                               ││

│ │ "This story is a follow-up to an earlier story about the same topic"     ││

│ │ Example: "MPC Decision" follows up "MPC Meeting Scheduled"                    ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PROVIDES_CONTEXT — Background relationship                             ││

│ │ Story A → PROVIDES_CONTEXT → Story B                              ││

│ │ "This story provides background context for understanding that story" │ │

│ │ Example: "History of Ghana Policy Rates" provides context for current │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RELATED_TO — General relationship                            ││

│ │ Story A → RELATED_TO → Story B                              ││

│ │ "These stories are related but neither follows from the other"           ││

│ │ Example: "Stock Market Reaction" related to "MPC Decision"               ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ CONTRADICTS — Contradictory information                             ││
│ │ Story A → CONTRADICTS → Story B                              ││

│ │ "This story presents information that contradicts that story"          ││

│ │ Example: "BoG Denies Report" contradicts "Report Claims Rate Change"         ││

│ │ TRIGGERS: Fact-check review; potential correction                    ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ CORROBORATES — Supporting evidence                                ││

│ │ Story A → CORROBORATES → Story B                                ││

│ │ "This story's reporting supports the claims in that story"           ││

│ │ Example: "IMF Report" corroborates "Inflation Analysis"                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ DERIVED_FROM — Content derivation                               ││

│ │ Story A → DERIVED_FROM → Story B (or Analysis/Opinion Piece)                ││

│ │ "This analysis/opinion piece is based on that news story"             ││

│ │ Example: "Analysis: What Rate Hike Means" derived from MPC story            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ MERGED_FROM — Story merge history                                 ││
│ │ Story A → MERGED_FROM → Story B                               ││

│ │ "This canonical story absorbed content from that duplicate story"      ││

│ │ Permanent record of merge event for audit trail                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART IV — EDITORIAL WORKFLOW



IV.1 END-TO-END EDITORIAL WORKFLOW



IV.1.1 The Complete Editorial Journey



The editorial workflow is the operational realisation of the Story Lifecycle defined in Volume 5.
Every story passes through defined stages, each with specific agents, quality gates, and decision
points:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│         COMPLETE EDITORIAL WORKFLOW — STANDARD STORY                          │

│                                            │
│
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐│

│ │ STAGE 1: NEWS DISCOVERY                                ││

│ │ ────────────────────────                                   ││

│ │ Agent: Monitoring Agents → Event Detection Agent                       ││

│ │ Input: Raw signals from configured sources                      ││

│ │ Process: Signal correlation → Entity extraction → Event hypothesis              ││

│ │ Output: Event with confidence score                         ││

│ │ Decision: Event confidence ≥ 0.6? → Proceed to Story Candidate                  ││

│ │      Event confidence < 0.6? → Observation Queue (monitor further) ││

│ │                                              ││

│ │ STAGE 2: STORY CANDIDATE EVALUATION                               ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Agent: News Director Agent                            ││

│ │ Input: Event data with initial context                  ││

│ │ Process: Newsworthiness assessment → Duplicate check → Prioritisation                 ││

│ │ Output: Prioritised Story Seed or Update trigger                  ││

│ │ Decision: New story? → Create Story in Story Memory                        ││

│ │      Update to existing? → Trigger Update Workflow                    ││

│ │      Not newsworthy? → Archive candidate                         ││

│ │                                              ││

│ │ STAGE 3: VERIFICATION & RESEARCH                             ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Agent: Research Agent → Source Verification Agent → Fact-Check Agent                 ││

│ │ Input: Story Seed with initial information                  ││

│ │ Process: Background research → Source discovery → Claim extraction                   ││
│ │      → Claim verification → Source reliability scoring             ││

│ │ Output: Verified Research Brief with confidence scores                   ││

│ │ Decision: All critical claims verified? → Proceed to Content Planning             ││

│ │      Unverified claims remain? → Flag for writer attention               ││

│ │      Source reliability concerns? → Flag for editorial review           ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ STAGE 4: CONTENT PLANNING                                     ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────                                     ││

│ │ Agent: Editorial Angle Agent → News Director Agent                       ││

│ │ Input: Verified Research Brief                           ││

│ │ Process: Angle selection → Structure planning → Format requirements                     ││

│ │ Output: Content Plan with angle, structure, and format specifications              ││

│ │ Decision: Content plan approved? → Assign Writer Agent                        ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ STAGE 5: ARTICLE CREATION                                 ││

│ │ ────────────────────────                                      ││

│ │ Agent: Writer Agent (appropriate specialist)                       ││

│ │ Input: Content Plan + Verified Research Brief                      ││

│ │ Process: Draft writing → Self-review → Draft submission                      ││

│ │ Output: First Draft                               ││

│ │ Quality Check: Writer self-assessment against quality criteria               ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ STAGE 6: EDITORIAL REVIEW                                 ││

│ │ ────────────────────────                                      ││

│ │ Agent: Copy Editor Agent → Senior Editor Agent                          ││

│ │ Input: First Draft                               ││
│ │ Process: Grammar/style check → Substantive edit → Structure review                         ││

│ │     → Angle refinement → Factual consistency check                      ││

│ │ Output: Edited Draft with editorial notes                     ││

│ │ Decision: Draft meets quality standards? → Proceed to Fact Check                      ││

│ │      Draft needs revision? → Return to Writer with feedback                 ││

│ │      Draft fundamentally flawed? → Escalate to human editor                  ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 7: FACT CHECKING                                  ││

│ │ ─────────────────────                                   ││

│ │ Agent: Fact-Check Agent → Context Verification Agent                        ││

│ │ Input: Edited Draft                               ││

│ │ Process: Claim extraction → Claim verification → Source cross-reference ││

│ │     → Context accuracy check → Statistical claim verification               ││

│ │ Output: Fact-Check Report with per-claim verification status                 ││

│ │ Decision: All claims verified? → Proceed to Styling                    ││

│ │      Unverified claims found? → Return to Writer/Editor                 ││

│ │      False claims detected? → Correction workflow + Escalation               ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 8: STYLING & HEADLINE                                  ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────                                       ││

│ │ Agent: Style Guide Agent → Headline & SEO Agent                             ││

│ │ Input: Fact-Checked Draft                              ││

│ │ Process: Style guide compliance → Formatting → Headline generation                         ││

│ │     → SEO optimisation → Metadata creation                         ││

│ │ Output: Final Draft with headlines, metadata, SEO elements                       ││

│ │                                             ││
│ │ STAGE 9: QUALITY ASSURANCE                                       ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────                                        ││

│ │ Agent: Editorial Quality Agent                            ││

│ │ Input: Final Draft                                ││

│ │ Process: Holistic quality assessment → Cross-check all prior stages              ││

│ │ Output: Quality Score (feeds into Confidence Engine)                        ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ STAGE 10: GOVERNANCE & CONFIDENCE                                          ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────────                                       ││

│ │ Agent: Ethics Agent → Compliance Agent → Copyright Agent                             ││

│ │     → Confidence Engine                                ││

│ │ Input: Final Draft + Quality Score                          ││

│ │ Process: Ethics review → Legal/compliance check → Copyright verification ││

│ │     → Confidence score calculation (5 dimensions)                      ││

│ │ Output: Confidence Score + Publication Decision                            ││

│ │ Decision: Score ≥ 0.85 → AUTONOMOUS PUBLISH                                     ││

│ │      Score 0.75-0.84 → CONDITIONAL PUBLISH (queued for human review) ││

│ │      Score 0.60-0.74 → HUMAN REVIEW REQUIRED (cannot publish)                             ││

│ │      Score < 0.60 → REJECT (return to drafting or kill)               ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ STAGE 11: MULTIMEDIA & FORMATTING                                      ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────────                                         ││

│ │ Agent: Format Adaptation Agent → Image Gen → Audio → Video                                ││

│ │ Input: Published Canonical Story                            ││

│ │ Process: Platform-specific derivative generation (parallel)                 ││

│ │ Output: Platform-optimised content for all configured channels                   ││
│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 12: DISTRIBUTION                                  ││

│ │ ────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Agent: Scheduling Agent → Distribution Agent                       ││

│ │ Input: Platform derivatives                         ││

│ │ Process: Schedule optimisation → Platform publishing → URL tracking                   ││

│ │ Output: Live content across all platforms                    ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 13: CONTINUOUS MONITORING                                    ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Agent: Source Monitors → Analytics Agent → Feedback Agent                        ││

│ │ Input: Published story                            ││

│ │ Process: Performance monitoring → Update detection → Sentiment tracking ││

│ │     → Competitor monitoring → Feedback collection                      ││

│ │ Output: Continuous monitoring data; triggers for updates/corrections              ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 14: UPDATES & CORRECTIONS                                   ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Triggered by: New information detected OR error identified                  ││

│ │ Process: Update/Correction workflow (see Parts V and X)                     ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ STAGE 15: LEARNING                                 ││

│ │ ────────────────                                   ││

│ │ Agent: Continuous Learning Engine                            ││

│ │ Input: All performance data, feedback, outcomes                        ││

│ │ Process: Pattern analysis → Insight generation → Action planning                 ││
│ │ Output: Agent prompt updates, policy recommendations, workflow optimisations││

│
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│

│                                         │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

IV.1.3 Failure Handling & Retry Paths



The editorial workflow includes defined failure handling at every stage:



```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            FAILURE HANDLING & RETRY PATHS                                │

│                                                   │

│ FAILURE TYPE                 HANDLING                 RETRY STRATEGY         │

│ ────────────                  ────────                ──────────────             │

│                                                   │

│ Agent Unavailable             Reassign to pool          Immediate            │

│ ─────────────────                ────────────────            ─────────                       │

│ Agent instance fails or is     Workflow Orchestrator Retry up to 3x                      │

│ at capacity             detects unavailability with exponential │

│                    Reassigns to next          backoff        │

│                    available agent of      Escalate to human │

│                    same type             after 3 failures │

│                                                   │

│ AI Model Error               Model fallback           Immediate          │

│ ──────────────                 ──────────────             ─────────                  │

│ Model returns error, timeout, Same-provider fallback Retry 2x with                               │

│ or rate limit           (GPT-4o→GPT-4o-mini)            fallback models          │

│                    Cross-provider fallback Flag for quality          │

│                    (OpenAI→Anthropic)             review if using    │

│                    Local fallback (Llama) lower-tier model │

│                                                   │

│ verified against sources       UNVERIFIED in draft         alternative sources │

│                     Confidence reduced         claims unverified │

│                                                 │

│                     Seek alternative source sources               │

│                     Major: Return to Style Escalate if pattern │

│                     Agent with notes         persists         │

V.1 THE BREAKING NEWS WORKFLOW



V.1.1 Speed with Verification



The Breaking News Workflow is designed for a single purpose: publish verified information as
quickly as possible, then continuously enrich it. It is not a shortcut around verification—it is an
accelerated verification pipeline:

---
PART VI — VERIFICATION PIPELINE (TRUTH ENGINE)



VI.1 THE TRUTH ENGINE: CONCEPTUAL FOUNDATION



VI.1.1 Beyond Fact-Checking



The Truth Engine is not merely a fact-checking module. It is the epistemological core of the
Agbofa Nexus AI newsroom — the system that determines what the platform considers true,
with what degree of confidence, based on what evidence, and with what acknowledged
uncertainties.



In traditional newsrooms, truth verification is distributed across reporters, editors, fact-
checkers, and legal review. In the autonomous newsroom, the Truth Engine formalises this
process into a deterministic, auditable, continuously operating pipeline that serves as the
foundation for all editorial decisions.



The Truth Engine operates on a single principle:



Every claim must be verified. The depth of verification scales with claim criticality. No claim is
published as fact without evidence. Uncertainty is acknowledged, not hidden.



VI.1.2 The Truth Engine Architecture



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│               THE TRUTH ENGINE ARCHITECTURE                        │

│            Verification Pipeline — End-to-End                 │
│                                               │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ INPUT: Content Draft + Source Materials + Story Graph Context                 ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                      │                        │

│                      ▼                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STAGE 1: CLAIM EXTRACTION                                     ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────                                      ││

│ │ Agent: Fact-Check Agent (AGB-EDE-FCT-001)                               ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ Process:                                            ││

│ │ • Parse content to identify all factual assertions                 ││

│ │ • Classify claims by type:                               ││

│ │ - Numerical/Statistical ("increased by 100 basis points")                ││

│ │ - Attribution ("according to the Governor...")                     ││

│ │ - Temporal ("on August 7, 2026...")                           ││

│ │ - Causal ("due to inflation concerns...")                     ││

│ │ - Comparative ("higher than the previous quarter...")                   ││

│ │ - Predictive ("analysts expect...")                       ││

│ │ • Assign criticality score to each claim                      ││

│ │ • Link claims to their stated sources in content                   ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ Output: Structured Claim Set with criticality scores                    ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                      │                       │

│                      ▼                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STAGE 2: EVIDENCE RETRIEVAL                               ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────                                 ││

│ │ Agent: Research Agent (AGB-NGE-INT-001) + RAG Pipeline                  ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ For each claim:                                    ││

│ │ • Query provided source materials first                    ││

│ │ • Query Editorial Knowledge Graph for related facts               ││

│ │ • Query external authoritative sources (government databases,            ││

│ │ official publications, verified data sources)              ││

│ │ • Retrieve relevant context from related stories in Story Graph         ││

│ │ • Identify corroborating and contradicting evidence               ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ Output: Evidence Set per claim (supporting, contradicting, neutral)      ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                      │                       │

│                      ▼                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STAGE 3: CROSS-SOURCE CORRELATION                                 ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────────                                 ││
│ │ Agent: Context Verification Agent (AGB-EDE-FCT-002)                    ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ For each claim with multiple evidence sources:                    ││

│ │ • Compare evidence across sources                            ││

│ │ • Identify consensus, discrepancies, contradictions                ││

│ │ • Weight evidence by source reliability                      ││

│ │ • Determine if discrepancies are substantive or presentational          ││

│ │ • Flag contradictory evidence for resolution                  ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ Output: Correlated Evidence with consensus/discrepancy flags                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                      │                      │

│                      ▼                       │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STAGE 4: CLAIM VERDICT                                  ││

│ │ ──────────────────────                                   ││

│ │ Agent: Fact-Check Agent (AGB-EDE-FCT-001)                         ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ For each claim, assign verdict:                         ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ VERDICT          CRITERIA                      │ ││

│ │ │ ───────          ────────                       │ ││

│ │ │ VERIFIED        Confirmed by ≥2 reliable sources or         │ ││

│ ││              1 official primary source           │ ││
│ │ │ LIKELY TRUE       Confirmed by 1 reliable source, consistent         │ ││

│ ││              with Knowledge Graph, no contradiction          │ ││

│ │ │ UNCERTAIN           Single source with moderate reliability or     │ ││

│ ││              sources disagree                        │ ││

│ │ │ UNVERIFIED          Claim cannot be checked against available        │ ││

│ ││              sources (acknowledged in content)              │ ││

│ │ │ DISPUTED         Reliable sources present contradictory           │ ││

│ ││              evidence                              │ ││

│ │ │ FALSE          Claim contradicted by authoritative evidence │ │ │

│ ││              (triggers correction workflow)               │ ││

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ │                                            ││

│ │ Output: Claim Verdict Set with per-claim confidence                    ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                     │                         │

│                      ▼                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STAGE 5: SOURCE RELIABILITY UPDATE                                ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │ Agent: Source Verification Agent (AGB-NGE-SRC-002)                      ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ • Update source reliability scores based on verification outcomes            ││

│ │ • If source claims consistently verified → score increases             ││

│ │ • If source claims disputed/false → score decreases                 ││

│ │ • Score changes feed into Source Intelligence Memory                    ││
│ │ • Significant score changes trigger alert to News Director             ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ Output: Updated Source Reliability Scores                        ││

│                      │                        │

│ │ STAGE 6: CONFIDENCE CALCULATION                                   ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────────                                   ││

│ │ Agent: Confidence Engine (AGB-POE-CON-001)                             ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ Calculate overall factual accuracy score:                    ││

│ │ • VERIFIED claims: full weight                          ││

│ │ • LIKELY TRUE claims: 0.8 weight                            ││

│ │ • UNCERTAIN claims: 0.4 weight (reduces confidence)                     ││

│ │ • UNVERIFIED claims: 0.2 weight (significant confidence reduction)           ││

│ │ • DISPUTED claims: 0 weight (major confidence reduction)                    ││

│ │ • FALSE claims: negative weight (triggers rejection)              ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ Combined with other confidence dimensions:                         ││

│ │ • Source Reliability (20%)                             ││

│ │ • Style Compliance (10%)                                ││

│ │ • Ethical Alignment (15%)                              ││

│ │                                             ││
│ │ Output: Overall Confidence Score → Publication Decision         ││

VI.2 MULTI-SOURCE VERIFICATION WORKFLOW



VI.2.1 The Verification Ladder



Not all claims require the same depth of verification. The Truth Engine applies a "verification
ladder" that scales effort to criticality:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             THE VERIFICATION LADDER                        │

│                                              │

│ CLAIM CRITICALITY          VERIFICATION DEPTH       SOURCES REQUIRED           │

│ ─────────────────            ─────────────────        ────────────────           │

│                                              │

│ LEVEL 5: EXTREME           MAXIMUM DEPTH            3+ independent reliable │

│ ─────────────────            ─────────────         sources + primary       │

│ • Head of state actions • Cross-reference all      document            │

│ • Loss of life        available sources   • Human review mandatory │

│ • Market-moving financial • Expert consultation      • Extended verification │

│ • National security      • Primary doc retrieval • Documented evidence │

│                                              │

│ LEVEL 4: HIGH           DEEP VERIFICATION        2+ independent reliable │
│ ────────────            ────────────────             sources                 │

│ • Policy changes        • Primary source check • Human review triggered │

│ • Major corporate actions • Cross-reference KG          if sources conflict              │

│ • Economic indicators     • Corroboration required                       │

│ • Election results                                        │

│                                                │

│ LEVEL 3: MODERATE          STANDARD VERIFICATION 1+ reliable source +                        │

│ ────────────────           ───────────────────── KG consistency check                            │

│ • Industry developments • Source check               • Autonomous if verified │

│ • Corporate announcements • KG cross-reference            • Flagged if uncertain │

│ • Sports results     • Corroboration preferred                       │

│                                                │

│ LEVEL 2: STANDARD         BASIC VERIFICATION           1 reliable source                 │

│ ────────────────           ─────────────────            sufficient                   │

│ • Routine announcements • Source check                 • Autonomous verification │

│ • Calendar events       • Plausibility check       • Spot-checked post-pub │

│ • Weather reports        • No contradiction                          │

│                                                │

│ LEVEL 1: MINOR          LIGHT VERIFICATION          Single source sufficient │

│ ─────────────            ─────────────────           with source reliability             │

│ • Event listings     • Source attribution check                      │

│ • Schedule changes       • Plausibility only       • Autonomous                  │

│ • Routine updates                                             │

│                                                │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘
```



VI.3 SOURCE RELIABILITY SCORING



VI.3.1 The Source Reliability Model



Every source used by the Truth Engine carries a dynamic reliability score that evolves with each
use:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           SOURCE RELIABILITY SCORING MODEL                          │

│                                             │

│ SCORE COMPONENTS (Weighted):                                  │

│ ────────────────────────────                                    │

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ HISTORICAL ACCURACY (35%)                                ││

│ │ • Verified claims / Total claims from this source             ││

│ │ • Higher weight to recent performance (last 90 days)                  ││

│ │ • Significant errors weighted more heavily than minor imprecisions         ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ CORROBORATION RATE (25%)                                      ││

│ │ • Claims confirmed by independent sources / Total claims                 ││

│ │ • Higher score if other reliable sources consistently agree             ││

│ │ • Lower score if source is frequently sole source for claims            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ INSTITUTIONAL AUTHORITY (20%)                                  ││

│ │ • Official sources (government, regulatory) start with high baseline         ││

│ │ • Academic/peer-reviewed sources rated highly                       ││

│ │ • Anonymous sources start at low baseline and must earn trust                 ││

│ │ • Corporate sources rated based on transparency history                  ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RECENCY & CONSISTENCY (10%)                                    ││

│ │ • More recent information weighted higher                          ││

│ │ • Consistency of reporting over time                          ││

│ │ • Penalty for contradictory statements without correction                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ TRANSPARENCY (10%)                                       ││

│ │ • Source clearly identifies itself and methodology             ││

│ │ • Conflicts of interest disclosed                        ││

│ │ • Corrections issued transparently when errors occur                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ SCORE INTERPRETATION:                                    ││

│ │ ─────────────────────                                     ││

│ │ 0.90 – 1.00: GOLD — Official primary sources, top-tier wire services     ││

│ │ 0.75 – 0.89: HIGH — Established media, verified expert sources           ││

│ │ 0.60 – 0.74: MODERATE — Generally reliable, occasional errors            ││

│ │ 0.40 – 0.59: CAUTION — Use with corroboration; human review recommended │ │

│ │ 0.20 – 0.39: LOW — Use only if essential; mandatory human review              ││

│ │ < 0.20: UNRELIABLE — Do not use without explicit human EIC authorisation │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

│ SCORE DYNAMICS:                                        │

│ • Scores recalculated weekly based on accumulated evidence                 │

│ • Immediate downgrade on verified false claim                     │

│ • Immediate downgrade to 0.1 if fabrication detected                  │

│ • Gradual recovery possible with sustained accurate reporting              │
│ • Human editors can override scores with documented rationale             │

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



VI.4 CLAIM EXTRACTION ENGINE



VI.4.1 How Claims Are Identified



The Claim Extraction Engine parses content to identify every factual assertion that requires
verification:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            CLAIM EXTRACTION ENGINE                          │

│                                            │

│ EXTRACTION PROCESS:                                     │

│ ──────────────────                                     │

│                                            │

│ INPUT: Draft content (text)                            │

│     │                                       │

│     ▼                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 1. SENTENCE SEGMENTATION                                  ││
│ │ • Parse content into individual sentences and clauses                 ││

│ │ • Identify quoted material separately                       ││

│ │ • Preserve context for each segment                         ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                          │

│     ▼                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 2. FACTUAL ASSERTION DETECTION                                  ││

│ │ • Identify sentences making truth claims                        ││

│ │ • Distinguish from:                                   ││

│ │       - Opinion statements ("arguably", "in my view")                ││

│ │       - Rhetorical devices                            ││

│ │       - Descriptive/narrative passages (not claims)             ││

│ │       - Previously established context (not new claims)              ││

│ │ • Flag ambiguous cases for human review                          ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                          │

│     ▼                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 3. CLAIM NORMALISATION                                     ││

│ │ • Convert each assertion to standard form:                       ││

│ │       "[ENTITY] [RELATIONSHIP] [VALUE/FACT] [TEMPORAL CONTEXT]"             ││

│ │ • Example: "The Bank of Ghana increased the policy rate to 30%"            ││
│ │       → ENTITY: Bank of Ghana                           ││

│ │       → ACTION: increased                               ││

│ │       → OBJECT: policy rate                         ││

│ │       → VALUE: 30%                                 ││

│ │       → TEMPORAL: August 7, 2026                             ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                         │

│     ▼                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 4. CLAIM CLASSIFICATION                                  ││

│ │ Assign each claim:                                 ││

│ │ • TYPE: Numerical | Attribution | Temporal | Causal |                  ││

│ │          Comparative | Predictive | Definitional              ││

│ │ • CRITICALITY: 1-5 (see Verification Ladder)                  ││

│ │ • STATED SOURCE: Source cited in content (if any)                  ││

│ │ • VERIFIABILITY: Directly verifiable | Requires inference |            ││

│ │               Unverifiable (opinion/speculation)             ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                         │

│     ▼                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 5. CLAIM LINKING                                   ││

│ │ • Link claims to entities in Knowledge Graph                      ││
│ │ • Link claims to sources in Source Graph                         ││

│ │ • Link related claims within the same story                      ││

│ │ • Identify if claim has been verified in a previous story              ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                            │

│     ▼                                                │

│ OUTPUT: Structured Claim Set (Claim ID, Normalised Text, Type, Criticality, │

│         Stated Source, KG Entity Links, Verifiability, Related Claims)       │

│                                                 │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



VI.5 CROSS-SOURCE CORRELATION



VI.5.1 Detecting Agreement and Disagreement



When multiple sources address the same claim, the Truth Engine must determine whether they
agree, disagree, or present different aspects:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              CROSS-SOURCE CORRELATION MATRIX                             │

│                                                 │

│ SOURCE A ──► CLAIM X                                          │
│ SOURCE B ──► CLAIM X                                      │

│     │                                      │

│     ▼                                          │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ CORRELATION ANALYSIS                                    ││

│ │                                          ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ MATCH TYPE        DESCRIPTION          CONFIDENCE IMPACT        │ ││

│ │ │ ──────────        ───────────          ─────────────────        │ ││

│ │ │ EXACT MATCH        Sources state identical HIGHEST confidence │ │ │

│ ││           fact with same values increase               │ ││

│ ││                          (+0.15 to claim)       │ ││

│ ││                                        │ ││

│ │ │ SUBSTANTIVE MATCH Sources agree on core HIGH confidence            │ ││

│ ││           fact; minor differences increase             │ ││

│ ││           in presentation        (+0.10 to claim)      │ ││

│ ││                                        │ ││

│ │ │ PARTIAL MATCH      Sources agree on some MODERATE confidence            │ ││

│ ││           aspects; differ on     impact             │ ││

│ ││           others            (+0.05 to claim)        │ ││

│ ││                                        │ ││

│ │ │ NO CORROBORATION       Only one source          NEUTRAL         │ ││

│ ││           addresses claim        (no change)           │ ││

│ ││                                        │ ││

│ │ │ PRESENTATIONAL      Sources disagree on        LOW confidence     │ │
│ │ │ DISCREPANCY          how to present same          reduction                │ │

│ ││              underlying fact        (-0.05 to claim)      │ ││

│ ││                                             │ ││

│ │ │ SUBSTANTIVE          Sources present           SIGNIFICANT confidence │ │ │

│ │ │ DISCREPANCY          meaningfully different reduction                      │ ││

│ ││              versions of fact      (-0.15 to claim)       │ ││

│ ││                                             │ ││

│ │ │ CONTRADICTION           Sources directly        CRITICAL confidence          │ ││

│ ││              contradict each other      reduction               │ ││

│ ││                              (-0.30 to claim;      │ ││

│ ││                              triggers escalation) │ │ │

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                │

│ RESOLUTION PROTOCOL FOR CONTRADICTIONS:                                              │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────                                             │

│ 1. Re-verify both sources                                    │

│ 2. Check source reliability scores                                 │

│ 3. Seek third independent source                                       │

│ 4. If contradiction persists:                              │

│   • Flag claim as DISPUTED                                     │

│   • Present both versions with source attribution in content                    │

│   • Reduce overall story confidence                                    │

│   • Escalate to human editor if claim is critical                          │

│                                                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



VI.6 CONFIDENCE SCORING FRAMEWORK



VI.6.1 From Claims to Confidence



The Truth Engine's outputs feed directly into the Editorial Confidence Engine. The transition
from verification results to confidence score is deterministic and auditable:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│         VERIFICATION-TO-CONFIDENCE CONVERSION                             │

│                                             │

│ CLAIM VERDICTS → FACTUAL ACCURACY SCORE                                   │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────                                   │

│                                             │

│ For each claim in the story:                             │

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ VERDICT      CLAIM SCORE WEIGHTED BY              CONTRIBUTION TO           ││

│ │ ───────      ─────────── ───────────             ───────────────            ││

│ │ VERIFIED     1.00       Criticality weight Full positive      ││

│ │ LIKELY TRUE 0.80         Criticality weight Strong positive        ││
│ │ UNCERTAIN      0.40       Criticality weight Weak positive                     ││

│ │ UNVERIFIED     0.20       Criticality weight Minimal positive                  ││

│ │ DISPUTED      0.00       Criticality weight No contribution                ││

│ │ FALSE       -0.50      Criticality weight Negative contribution │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                │

│ CRITICALITY WEIGHTING:                                       │

│ ─────────────────────                                        │

│ Level 5 claims: weight × 2.0 (extreme impact on score)                           │

│ Level 4 claims: weight × 1.5 (high impact)                           │

│ Level 3 claims: weight × 1.0 (standard impact)                           │

│ Level 2 claims: weight × 0.7 (moderate impact)                               │

│ Level 1 claims: weight × 0.4 (low impact)                            │

│                                                │

│ RAW FACTUAL ACCURACY = Σ(Claim Score × Criticality Weight) / Σ(Criticality Weights)│

│                                                │

│ EXAMPLE CALCULATION:                                         │

│ ────────────────────                                         │

│ Story with 12 claims:                                │

│ • 6 VERIFIED (Criticality: 2×L4, 2×L3, 2×L2)                     │

│ • 3 LIKELY TRUE (Criticality: 1×L3, 2×L2)                        │

│ • 2 UNCERTAIN (Criticality: 1×L3, 1×L1)                          │

│ • 1 UNVERIFIED (Criticality: L2)                             │

│                                                │

│ Weighted Claim Scores:                                   │
│ VERIFIED: (2×1.5×1.0) + (2×1.0×1.0) + (2×0.7×1.0) = 3.0 + 2.0 + 1.4 = 6.4│

│ LIKELY TRUE: (1×1.0×0.8) + (2×0.7×0.8) = 0.8 + 1.12 = 1.92           │

│ UNCERTAIN: (1×1.0×0.4) + (1×0.4×0.4) = 0.4 + 0.16 = 0.56                 │

│ UNVERIFIED: (1×0.7×0.2) = 0.14                               │

│                                              │

│ Total Weighted Score = 6.4 + 1.92 + 0.56 + 0.14 = 9.02               │

│ Total Weights = (2×1.5)+(2×1.0)+(2×0.7)+(1×1.0)+(2×0.7)+(1×1.0)+(1×0.4)+(1×0.7) =
3+2+1.4+1+1.4+1+0.4+0.7 = 10.9│

│                                              │

│ Raw Factual Accuracy = 9.02 / 10.9 = 0.827                       │

│                                              │

│ This feeds into the overall Confidence Score:                    │

│ Overall = (0.827 × 0.35) + (SourceRel × 0.20) + (EditQual × 0.20)            │

│       + (Style × 0.10) + (Ethics × 0.15)                 │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



VI.7 MISINFORMATION DETECTION



VI.7.1 The Hallucination and Misinformation Defence



The Truth Engine includes specific defences against both external misinformation and internal AI
hallucination:



```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           MISINFORMATION DETECTION FRAMEWORK                                     │

│                                              │

│ DEFENCE LAYER 1: KNOWN MISINFORMATION SOURCE FILTER                                          │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ • Maintain Misinformation Source Registry (MSR)                          │

│ • Sources flagged for: fabrication history, coordinated inauthenticity,              │

│ known disinformation campaigns, fact-check failures                      │

│ • Content from MSR sources: blocked from ingestion or flagged CRITICAL                       │

│ • MSR updated continuously from:                                 │

│ - Internal verification failures                        │

│ - External fact-check organisation databases                         │

│ - Platform trust and safety signals                         │

│ - Human editorial additions                                 │

│                                              │

│ DEFENCE LAYER 2: HALLUCINATION DETECTION                                     │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                            │

│ • Entity Grounding: Verify all named entities exist in Knowledge Graph                   │

│ • Quote Authenticity: Verify attributed quotes appear in source materials │

│ • Numerical Plausibility: Flag statistically improbable claims               │

│ • Temporal Logic: Verify event sequences are chronologically possible                    │

│ • Self-Consistency Check: Generate content twice; flag inconsistencies                   │

│ • Source-Content Alignment: Verify content is supported by cited sources                     │

│                                              │

│ DEFENCE LAYER 3: COORDINATED NARRATIVE DETECTION                                         │
│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                                  │

│ • Detect when multiple sources push identical narratives simultaneously           │

│ • Identify inauthentic coordination patterns                  │

│ • Cross-reference with known influence operations                     │

│ • Flag for enhanced verification and potential human review               │

│                                              │

│ DEFENCE LAYER 4: POST-PUBLICATION SURVEILLANCE                            │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                                   │

│ • Continuous re-verification of published claims                  │

│ • Monitor for new contradictory evidence                      │

│ • Track source recantations or corrections                    │

│ • Audience correction submissions processed                       │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

VI.11 VERIFICATION DECISION RECORDS



ADR ID Decision Rationale
VER-001 Verification depth scales with claim criticality, not story priority Ensures resource
efficiency while maintaining rigour for consequential claims

VER-002 Breaking news uses binary VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED verdicts with deferred full
verification Balances speed with integrity; full verification completes post-publish

VER-003 Source reliability scores are dynamic and degrade immediately on false claims Ensures
the platform's trust model responds quickly to source failures

VER-004 FALSE claim detection triggers immediate publication halt Prevents publication of
known falsehoods regardless of workflow stage

VER-005 Hallucination detection uses ensemble approach (entity grounding + self-consistency +
source alignment) Multiple detection methods provide defence in depth against AI errors

PART VII — CONTENT FACTORY



VII.1 THE CONTENT FACTORY: CONCEPTUAL FOUNDATION



VII.1.1 From Story to Content



The Content Factory is the production engine of the Agbofa Nexus AI newsroom. It transforms
verified Story Graph intelligence into platform-optimised content across every format and
channel the newsroom supports.



The Content Factory operates on a fundamental principle:



One canonical story. Many outputs. Consistent truth. Platform-appropriate presentation.
The Content Factory does not create new facts. It expresses the verified facts in the Story Graph
in formats optimised for each platform's audience, algorithm, and consumption patterns.

│ │ 2. HEADLINE SCORING                                        ││

│ │ ─────────────────                                           ││

│ │ Each variant scored on:                                   ││

│ │ • Accuracy (does it faithfully represent the story?)           (30%)        ││

│ │ • SEO potential (keyword inclusion, search intent)             (25%)        ││

│ │ • Engagement potential (click-through likelihood)              (25%)        ││

│ │ • Brand voice alignment                           (10%)      ││

│ │ • Length optimisation (platform-specific)                 (10%)    ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 3. PLATFORM-SPECIFIC SELECTION                                    ││

│ │ ──────────────────────────────                                         ││

│ │ Different headlines for different platforms:                      ││

│ │ • Web: SEO-optimised, up to 70 characters                              ││

│ │ • X: Concise, hashtaggable, ~100 characters                            ││
│ │ • Facebook: Engaging, conversational, ~40 characters                ││

│ │ • LinkedIn: Professional, industry-focused                 ││

│ │ • Newsletter: Personalised, benefit-focused                    ││

│ │ • Push notification: Urgent, action-oriented, ~30 characters         ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                      │

│     ▼                                          │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ 4. ENSEMBLE SELECTION (Enterprise)                         ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────                                  ││

│ │ Multiple models generate headlines; voting agent selects best.           ││

│ │ Human editor can review top candidates for critical stories.         ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                           │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

VII.12 CONTENT VERSIONING



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             CONTENT VERSIONING STRATEGY                              │

│                                               │

│ VERSION NUMBERING SCHEME: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH                                          │

│ ──────────────────────────────────────────                                       │

│                                               │

│ MAJOR version (X.0.0):                                  │

│ • Complete article rewrite or restructure                        │

│ • Significant new information that changes story narrative                   │

│ • Transition from breaking brief to full article                 │

│ • Major correction that substantially changes content                    │

│                                               │

│ MINOR version (0.X.0):                                  │

│ • Addition of new verified facts or context                      │

│ • Addition of expert commentary or analysis                          │

│ • Addition of multimedia elements                            │

│ • Minor updates to reflect developments                              │

│                                               │

│ PATCH version (0.0.X):                              │

│ • Typo corrections                                 │
│ • Minor clarifications                                 │

│ • Link updates                                     │

│ • Metadata adjustments                                     │

│ • Minor style adjustments                                  │

│                                               │

│ VERSION RETENTION:                                         │

│ • All versions permanently stored in Story Graph                       │

│ • Full diff available between any two versions                     │

│ • Version history visible to editorial team                    │

│ • Public version history for corrections (transparency)                │

│ • Rollback to any previous version supported                       │

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│ PUBLISH DECISION RECEIVED                              │

│ SCHEDULING OPTIMISATION:                                     │

│ ───────────────────────                                     │

VIII.4 RETRY STRATEGY & FAILURE RECOVERY



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│          DISTRIBUTION RETRY & FAILURE STRATEGY                     │

│                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RETRY POLICY (per platform)                            ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────                                 ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ ATTEMPT DELAY        STRATEGY                        │ ││

│ │ │ ─────── ─────        ────────                    │ ││

│ ││1       Immediate Initial publish attempt              │ ││

│ ││2       1 minute    Retry with same content             │ ││

│ ││3       5 minutes Retry; check platform status           │ ││

│ ││4       15 minutes Retry; notify ops team               │ ││

│ ││5       1 hour     Retry; escalate to human operator        │ ││

│ │ │ 6+    Manual      Dead-letter; human intervention required │ │ │

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ FAILURE HANDLING BY ERROR TYPE                                ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────────                                  ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ RATE LIMIT → Exponential backoff; queue for off-peak                   ││

│ │ AUTH ERROR → Immediate alert; check API credentials                     ││

│ │ CONTENT REJECTION → Log reason; adjust content; retry once                   ││

│ │ NETWORK TIMEOUT → Standard retry with backoff                           ││

│ │ PLATFORM UNAVAILABLE → Queue; retry when platform recovers                        ││

│ │ CONTENT POLICY VIOLATION → Escalate to human editor; do not retry                 ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ DEAD LETTER QUEUE                                     ││

│ │ ────────────────                                     ││

│ │ Content that fails all retry attempts enters the Dead Letter Queue.         ││

│ │ • Human operator reviews and determines action                     ││

│ │ • Options: manual retry, content adjustment, platform change, discard            ││

│ │ • DLQ items reviewed within 4 business hours                      ││

│ │ • Patterns of DLQ entries trigger platform health investigation         ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                          │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART IX — CONTINUOUS STORY MONITORING



IX.1 THE LIVING STORY LIFECYCLE



IX.1.1 Publication Is Not the End
In the Agbofa Nexus AI newsroom, publication marks the transition from content production to
content stewardship. Every published story enters a continuous monitoring phase that may last
days, months, or indefinitely — depending on the story's nature and ongoing relevance.



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           CONTINUOUS STORY MONITORING LIFECYCLE                        │

│                                            │

│ STORY PUBLISHED                                        │

│     │                                       │

│     ▼                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ ACTIVE MONITORING PHASE (First 7 days after publication)                 ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────                             ││

│ │                                          ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ MONITORING DIMENSION            FREQUENCY         TRIGGER ACTION         │ ││

│ │ │ ────────────────────           ─────────        ──────────────         │ ││

│ │ │                                        │ ││

│ │ │ Source Monitoring       Continuous      New source info →        │ ││

│ │ │ (Wire, social, web)               Update evaluation     │ ││

│ │ │                                        │ ││

│ │ │ Fact Re-verification   Daily        New contradictory     │ ││

│ │ │ (Critical claims)               evidence → Correction │ │ │
│ │ │                                            │ ││

│ │ │ Audience Engagement          Hourly         Anomalous patterns → │ │ │

│ │ │ (Metrics, sentiment)                  Editorial alert     │ ││

│ │ │                                            │ ││

│ │ │ Competitor Monitoring        Every 4 hours Competitor scoops →            │ ││

│ │ │ (Related coverage)                  Update consideration │ │ │

│ │ │                                            │ ││

│ │ │ Feedback Processing        Continuous        Reader correction →      │ ││

│ │ │ (Comments, corrections)                 Correction workflow        │ ││

│ │ │                                            │ ││

│ │ │ Social Signal Monitoring Continuous             Significant sharing → │ │ │

│ │ │ (Virality, narrative)              Distribution boost      │ ││

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                       │                         │

│                       ▼ (After 7 days or when velocity drops) │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PASSIVE MONITORING PHASE (7 days to 90 days)                           ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │                                              ││

│ │ • Monitoring frequency reduced (daily → weekly)                       ││

│ │ • Only critical claims re-verified                         ││

│ │ • Competitor monitoring continues                               ││

│ │ • Feedback still processed                                ││

│ │ • Significant new developments trigger return to Active phase               ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                     │                      │

│                     ▼ (After 90 days or when relevance fades)│

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ ARCHIVAL CANDIDATE (90+ days)                             ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────                                ││

│ │                                          ││

│ │ • Story assessed for archival                        ││

│ │ • If no updates in 90 days AND no ongoing relevance → Archive          ││

│ │ • If ongoing relevance (reference story, timeline piece) → Keep Passive │ │

│ │ • Archival: Story Graph preserved; content cold-stored            ││

│ │ • Archived stories can be reactivated if new developments occur        ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

IX.4 FOLLOW-UP STORY DETECTION



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           FOLLOW-UP STORY DETECTION WORKFLOW                          │

│                                             │

│ The Story Graph actively monitors for signals that a new story is a       │

│ follow-up to an existing story, enabling the newsroom to build narrative       │

│ continuity:                                      │

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ DETECTION SIGNALS                                       ││

│ │ ────────────────                                     ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ 1. ENTITY OVERLAP: New story shares significant entities with published │ │

│ │ story (≥40% entity overlap)                             ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ 2. TEMPORAL SEQUENCE: New story's event occurs after published story's │ │

│ │ event in a logical sequence                             ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ 3. CAUSAL CONNECTION: Language in new story indicates it is a               ││

│ │ consequence/response/reaction to the published story                ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ 4. TOPIC CONTINUITY: New story covers the same topic beat and references │ │

│ │ the earlier event                                  ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│     │                                       │

│     ▼                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RELATIONSHIP ASSIGNMENT                                     ││

│ │ ───────────────────────                                    ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ If follow-up detected, Story Graph relationship created:              ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ Published Story ←──FOLLOWS_UP── New Story                              ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ Actions:                                          ││

│ │ • Link both stories in Story Graph                         ││

│ │ • Add "Related Stories" section to both articles                 ││

│ │ • Update published story's "What's Next" section if applicable             ││

│ │ • Cross-reference in Knowledge Graph                            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



IX.5 STORY KNOWLEDGE GRAPH INTEGRATION
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│         STORY GRAPH ↔ KNOWLEDGE GRAPH INTEGRATION                            │

│                                           │

│ The Story Graph and Editorial Knowledge Graph are distinct but deeply        │

│ integrated structures:                             │

│                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ DATA FLOW BETWEEN GRAPHS                                   ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────                                  ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ STORY GRAPH ──────────────────────────────► KNOWLEDGE GRAPH                     ││

│ │ ───────────                     ──────────────          ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ • New entities discovered          • Entity nodes created/updated │ │

│ │ • New relationships observed          • Relationship edges added      ││

│ │ • Source reliability data        • Source scores updated        ││

│ │ • Claim verification outcomes        • Fact confidence updated       ││

│ │ • Event sequences observed           • Temporal relationships        ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ KNOWLEDGE GRAPH ──────────────────────────► STORY GRAPH                        ││

│ │ ──────────────                   ───────────            ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ • Entity resolution             • Entities grounded     ││

│ │ • Background facts               • Context enrichment        ││
│ │ • Relationship context             • Story relationships           ││

│ │ • Source reliability history       • Source evaluation             ││

│ │ • Topic classification           • Story categorisation        ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

IX.6 STORY ARCHIVING



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              STORY ARCHIVING WORKFLOW                            │

│                                            │

│ ARCHIVAL CRITERIA (All must be met):                             │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                      │

│ • Story published ≥ 90 days ago                              │

│ • No updates in ≥ 90 days                                │

│ • No ongoing active monitoring triggers                          │

│ • Not designated as permanent reference story                         │

│ • Not part of an active developing narrative                     │

│                                            │

│ ARCHIVAL PROCESS:                                     │

│ ────────────────                                     │
│                                               │

│ 1. ASSESSMENT: Archival criteria evaluated weekly by News Director Agent             │

│      │                                         │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 2. NOTIFICATION: Human EIC notified of pending archival (can override)           │

│      │                                         │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 3. CONTENT MIGRATION:                                    │

│     • Full article content → Cold storage (lower cost)           │

│     • Story Graph → Preserved in active graph database (permanent)           │

│     • Derivatives → Cold stored; URLs preserved                  │

│     • Media assets → Cold stored with metadata                   │

│      │                                         │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 4. STATE UPDATE: Story state → ARCHIVED                          │

│      │                                         │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 5. REACTIVATION CAPABILITY:                                  │

│     • Archived stories can be reactivated if new developments occur      │

│     • Reactivation restores to LIVE state                    │

│     • Content migrated back to warm storage                      │

│     • Full version history preserved                     │

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

X.2 CORRECTION WORKFLOW



```

│ │ │       accuracy or fairness         incorrect central fact │ │ │

│ │ │                                          │ ││

X.3 RETRACTION WORKFLOW



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             RETRACTION WORKFLOW                             │

│                                             │

│ RETRACTION TRIGGERS (Any one):                                  │

│ ──────────────────────────────                                      │
│ • Critical error that fundamentally undermines the story                          │

│ • Fabrication of sources, quotes, or facts detected                       │

│ • Legal requirement to remove content                                 │

│ • Ethical violation requiring content withdrawal                          │

│ • Human EIC determination that content should not remain published                        │

│                                              │

│ RETRACTION PROCESS:                                       │

│ ──────────────────                                        │

│                                              │

│ 1. IMMEDIATE HALT                                     │

│   • Story removed from active distribution                            │

│   • All platform content suspended                                │

│   • Social media posts flagged for removal                            │

│   • "This content has been retracted" placeholder published                           │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 2. INVESTIGATION (Expedited)                                      │

│   • Root cause analysis                               │

│   • Full editorial trail review                       │

│   • Agent behaviour review                                    │

│   • Impact assessment (how widely distributed?)                               │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 3. RETRACTION NOTICE DRAFTING                                         │

│   • Clear explanation of what was wrong and why                               │

│   • Apology if appropriate                                │
│   • Commitment to process improvement                                        │

│   • Duration of publication and distribution scope disclosed                     │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 4. EIC APPROVAL (MANDATORY)                                      │

│   • Human EIC must approve all retractions                               │

│   • Legal review if applicable                           │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 5. PUBLICATION & NOTIFICATION                                    │

│   • Retraction notice published in story location                        │

│   • Social media retraction posts                            │

│   • Audience notification (subscribers)                          │

│   • Source notification                              │

│   • Story state → RETRACTED                                  │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 6. ORGANISATIONAL LEARNING                                       │

│   • Full post-mortem                                 │

│   • Process improvement plan                                 │

│   • Agent retraining/behaviour update                                │

│   • Governance review                                    │

│   • Public transparency report (if appropriate)                          │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘
```

│ │ │ MONITOR │ │ EDITORIAL│ │GOVERNANCE│ │AUDIENCE │ │PLATFORM │           ││

│ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │              EVENT BUS                      │ ││

│ │ │ • Persistent, append-only log                      │ ││

│ │ │ • Publish-subscribe pattern                        │ ││

│ │ │ • Routes tasks to appropriate agents                  │ ││

│ │ │ • Handles timeouts, retries, escalations              │ ││

│ │ │ • Maintains workflow state independently of agents           │ ││
