│                                           │

XI.2 WORKFLOW ORCHESTRATION DESIGN



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│          WORKFLOW ORCHESTRATION DESIGN                          │

│                                           │

│ ORCHESTRATION PATTERNS:                                  │

│ ──────────────────────                                  │

│                                           │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PATTERN 1: SEQUENTIAL WORKFLOW (Standard Editorial)                   ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                           ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ SEED → ASSIGN → RESEARCH → DRAFT → REVIEW → FACT CHECK → STYLE →                ││

│ │ CONFIDENCE → PUBLISH → DISTRIBUTE → MONITOR                           ││

│ │                                         ││

│ │ Each stage must complete (with optional retry) before next begins.    ││

│ │ Checkpoint after each stage enables resume from any point.           ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PATTERN 2: PARALLEL EXECUTION (Content Factory)                       ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                             ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ After story is published:                             ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │            ┌──► Web Article Generation                     ││

│ │            │                                   ││

│ │ CANONICAL STORY ──┼──► Social Media Variant Generation                      ││

│ │            │                                   ││

│ │            ├──► Audio Brief Generation                      ││

│ │            │                                   ││

│ │            ├──► Newsletter Item Generation                      ││

│ │            │                                   ││

│ │            └──► Image/Thumbnail Generation                       ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ All executed in parallel; Distribution waits for all to complete.     ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PATTERN 3: EVENT-DRIVEN WORKFLOW (Breaking News)                           ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                                ││

│ │                                            ││
│ │ Breaking news is event-driven, not stage-gated:                 ││

│ │ • Detection event → Triggers declaration + initial draft         ││

│ │ • New source event → Triggers verification + update                  ││

│ │ • Stabilisation event → Triggers transition to standard          ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ Workflow Orchestrator listens for events and triggers appropriate          ││

│ │ agent actions rather than enforcing strict stage sequence.            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ PATTERN 4: HUMAN INTERRUPTION                                   ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────                                    ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ At defined points, workflow pauses for human input:                  ││

│ │ • Confidence score in review band → Pause; notify human editor             ││

│ │ • Ethics flag → Pause; escalate                            ││

│ │ • Correction approval → Pause; await human authorisation                  ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ Paused workflows maintain state and context.                     ││

│ │ Resume from exact pause point with full context.                 ││

│ │ Timeout on human response triggers re-escalation.                    ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



XI.3 CHECKPOINTING & RESUME



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           CHECKPOINTING & RESUME CAPABILITY                              │

│                                           │

│ CHECKPOINT STRATEGY:                                   │

│ ───────────────────                                    │

│                                           │

│ • Checkpoint created after every workflow stage completion                   │

│ • Checkpoint contains:                             │

│ - Story ID and current state                           ││

│ - Completed stages with timestamps                              │

│ - Agent outputs from completed stages                               ││

│ - All intermediate content versions                         │

│ - Pending tasks and assignments                             │

│ • Checkpoints persisted in Story Memory                             ││

│                                           │

│ RESUME SCENARIOS:                                      │

│ ────────────────                                   │

│                                           │
│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ SCENARIO               RESUME BEHAVIOUR                      ││

│ │ ────────             ────────────────                       ││

│ │ Agent failure          Reassign task to new agent of same type        ││

│ │                 New agent receives full context from checkpoint │ │

│ │                                            ││

│ │ Orchestrator restart      Load all active workflows from checkpoints       ││

│ │                 Resume each from last completed stage            ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ System maintenance         Pause all workflows gracefully             ││

│ │                 Create checkpoints for all in-flight work   ││

│ │                 Resume from checkpoints post-maintenance          ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ Infrastructure failure Restore from latest checkpoints                ││

│ │                 Replay any events since last checkpoint     ││

│ │                 Maximum data loss: events since last checkpoint │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



XI.4 RETRY POLICIES & DEAD LETTER QUEUES



```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            RETRY POLICIES & DEAD LETTER QUEUES                       │

│                                              │

│ RETRY POLICY (per task type):                               │

│ ────────────────────────────                                     │

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ TASK TYPE        MAX RETRIES BACKOFF STRATEGY DLQ TIMEOUT               ││

│ │ ─────────        ─────────── ──────────────── ───────────               ││

│ │ Content Generation 3             Exponential (1m, 24 hours         ││

│ │                      5m, 15m)                   ││

│ │ Fact-Checking        5        Exponential (30s, 4 hours       ││

│ │                      2m, 10m, 30m, 2h)               ││

│ │ Distribution     5           Exponential (1m, 1 hour          ││

│ │                      5m, 15m, 1h, 4h)               ││

│ │ Image Generation         3      Fixed (1m each) 12 hours           ││

│ │ Translation      3           Exponential (1m, 12 hours        ││

│ │                      5m, 15m)                   ││

│ │ Confidence Scoring 1 (no retry) N/A             Immediate alert │ │

│ │ (Critical — must not                                 ││

│ │ silently fail)                                 ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ DEAD LETTER HANDLING:                                       │
│ ─────────────────────                                   ││

│ • DLQ monitored by System Health Agent                         ││

│ • Alerts triggered for DLQ accumulation                      ││

│ • Human operator reviews DLQ items within SLA                       ││

│ • Patterns analysed for systemic issues                   ││

│ • DLQ items can be: replayed, modified and replayed, or discarded         ││

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



XI.5 WORKFLOW OBSERVABILITY



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

XII.5 ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS (ADRs)



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│        ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS — VOLUME 6                              │

│                                               │

│ ADR-V6-001: Verification Depth Scales with Claim Criticality             │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                │

│ Context: Full verification of every claim is resource-prohibitive        │

│ Decision: Verification depth (sources required, time allocated) scales           │

│       with claim criticality level (1-5)                   │

│ Rationale: Ensures resource efficiency while maintaining rigorous                │

│       verification for consequential claims                    │

│ Consequences: Critical claims receive disproportionate verification          │

│         resources; lower-criticality claims verified more lightly    │

│                                               │

│ ADR-V6-002: Breaking News Uses Deferred Full Verification                    │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                │

│ Context: Breaking news requires speed; full verification takes time              │

│ Decision: Breaking news publishes with rapid verification of critical        │

│       claims only; full verification runs post-publish in parallel   │
│ Rationale: Balances speed with integrity; any post-publish issues              │

│       trigger immediate correction                        │

│ Consequences: Potential for post-publish corrections higher for breaking               │

│         news; mitigated by DEVELOPING flag and rapid correction             │

│                                             │

│ ADR-V6-003: Content Derivatives Generated from Canonical Story Only                        │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                    │

│ Context: Multiple content formats risk factual divergence               │

│ Decision: All platform-specific content is generated as a derivative           │

│       of the canonical Story Graph, never independently created             │

│ Rationale: Ensures factual consistency across all platforms; single         │

│       source of truth for corrections                     │

│ Consequences: All derivatives must be refreshed when story updates;                    │

│         adds distribution complexity but ensures consistency           │

│                                             │

│ ADR-V6-004: Correction Severity Determines Approval Level                       │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ Context: Corrections range from typos to fundamental errors                    │

│ Decision: Correction approval authority scales with severity: Minor                │

│       (autonomous), Significant (Desk Editor), Major (Managing             │

│       Editor), Critical (EIC)                       │

│ Rationale: Balances efficiency with appropriate oversight for serious              │

│       errors                                    │

│ Consequences: Minor corrections processed quickly; major errors receive                    │

│         appropriate human scrutiny                          │

│                                             │
│ ADR-V6-005: Workflow State is External to Agents                     │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                                         │

│ Context: Agent failure should not lose workflow state                    │

│ Decision: Workflow state is persisted in the Workflow Orchestrator and               │

│      Story Memory, not in individual agent instances                 │

│ Rationale: Enables agent replacement without state loss; supports                │

│       workflow resume from any point                         │

│ Consequences: Agents must be designed as stateless workers; state                    │

│         retrieval adds latency per task but ensures resilience       │

│                                             │

│ ADR-V6-006: Human Override Always Available                              │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                    │

│ Context: Autonomous systems may make errors requiring human intervention                     │

│ Decision: Human editors can interrupt any workflow at any stage and                  │

│      override any AI decision with documented rationale                  │

│ Rationale: Maintains human supremacy principle; enables correction of                    │

│       AI errors before publication                      │

│ Consequences: Workflows must support pause/resume; human intervention                        │

│         introduces variability in processing times               │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

XII.8 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY



Volume 6 of the Agbofa Nexus AI enterprise architecture defines the complete operational
blueprint for the Autonomous AI Newsroom. Where Volume 5 specified what the AI agents are
and how they are architected, Volume 6 specifies how they operate — the workflows, pipelines,
decision frameworks, and operational practices that transform a collection of AI agents into a
coherent, self-directing media enterprise.



Key Architectural Achievements:



1. Complete Story Lifecycle Management — Every story progresses through a defined, auditable
lifecycle from discovery through verification, creation, publication, continuous monitoring, and
archival. The Story Graph maintains the canonical record; platform derivatives maintain
consistency.

2. The Truth Engine — A multi-stage verification pipeline that extracts claims, retrieves
evidence, correlates sources, assigns verdicts, and calculates confidence scores. Verification
depth scales with claim criticality, ensuring rigorous verification for consequential claims while
maintaining efficiency.

3. The Content Factory — One canonical story generates all platform outputs: long-form articles,
social media variants, audio briefs, video scripts, newsletters, and push notifications. Every
derivative is factually consistent because there is one source of truth.

4. Breaking News Architecture — A dedicated rapid pipeline that compresses verification
without eliminating it, publishes verified information within minutes, and continuously enriches
content as new information becomes available.
5. Correction & Retraction Framework — Comprehensive, severity-based correction workflows
with appropriate human oversight, full platform synchronisation, and organisational learning
integration.

6. Enterprise Workflow Orchestration — Event-driven architecture with checkpointing, retry
policies, dead letter queues, human interruption points, and full observability — ensuring
resilient, auditable, and recoverable operations.

7. Operational Maturity — Defined SLAs, monitoring dashboards, operational runbooks, disaster
recovery procedures, and a clear MVP→Growth→Enterprise evolution roadmap.



The Platform in Operation:



When fully realised, the Agbofa Nexus AI newsroom operates as follows: Monitoring agents
detect a potential story. The Event Detection Agent correlates signals and determines
newsworthiness. The Story Recognition Pipeline determines if this is new or an update. The
Truth Engine verifies claims against sources. The Content Factory generates the canonical story
and all platform derivatives. The Distribution Engine publishes to all configured platforms at
optimal times. The Monitoring systems watch for updates, errors, and audience feedback. The
Continuous Learning Engine analyses every outcome and improves the system.



Throughout this process, human editors are not bottlenecks — they are safety nets, reviewing
content when confidence is moderate, resolving escalations when AI agents disagree,
authorising corrections when errors occur, and setting the strategic direction that guides
autonomous operation.



This is not a content automation tool. This is an Autonomous AI Media Company Platform —
operational, scalable, and ready for implementation.



XII.9 KEY RECOMMENDATIONS



1. Implement the Truth Engine First — The verification pipeline is the foundation of editorial
integrity. Invest in its accuracy before expanding content volume.
2. Start with Human Review, Earn Autonomy — Begin with all content human-reviewed.
Gradually expand autonomous publication as confidence scores prove reliable.

3. Invest in the Story Graph Early — The Story Graph is the platform's most valuable asset. Its
quality determines the quality of every derivative and every update.

4. Build for Multi-Brand from Day One — Even if launching with one brand, implement brand
configuration architecture from the start to avoid costly migration.

5. Monitor Corrections as a Primary KPI — Correction rate is the most honest measure of
editorial quality. Track it relentlessly and investigate every trend.

6. Design Every Workflow for Interruption — Assume human editors will need to intervene at
any point. Build pause, resume, and override into every workflow.

7. Plan for Model Independence — The Multi-LLM Abstraction Layer is not optional. AI model
capabilities and costs will change; the platform must adapt without redesign.



XII.10 CONCLUSION



Volume 6 completes the operational architecture for the Agbofa Nexus AI Autonomous AI
Media Company Platform. Together with Volumes 1–5, it provides a complete blueprint for
designing, building, and operating an AI-first newsroom that can discover, verify, produce,
distribute, monitor, correct, and learn — all within deterministic governance boundaries and
with human editorial supremacy preserved.



The architecture is ready for implementation. The path from MVP through Growth to Enterprise
is defined. The operational practices, SLAs, monitoring frameworks, and recovery procedures
are specified. The platform's evolution from a single-brand newsroom to a global multi-tenant
media platform is architecturally supported without redesign.



What remains is execution — the translation of this architecture into working systems, deployed
infrastructure, and operational reality. That is the work of Volume 7: Implementation
Architecture, and the teams who will bring the Agbofa Nexus AI vision to life.

PART I — FRONTEND VISION & DESIGN PHILOSOPHY



I.1 UX VISION



I.1.1 The AI Operating System for Newsrooms



Agbofa Nexus AI is not a content management system with AI features added. It is an AI
operating system for running a modern autonomous newsroom. The frontend experience must
reflect this fundamental distinction.
Where traditional CMS platforms present users with forms, fields, and publish buttons, Agbofa
Nexus AI presents users with intelligence dashboards, agent workspaces, confidence indicators,
and editorial command centres. The user is not filling in content fields — they are overseeing an
AI workforce that discovers, verifies, produces, and distributes news.



The UX vision rests on four pillars:



1. Command, Not Control — Users direct AI agents rather than performing tasks themselves.
The interface surfaces decisions that require human judgment while automating routine
execution.

2. Confidence, Not Certainty — Every AI-generated output displays its confidence level. Users
make informed decisions about when to trust AI and when to intervene.

3. Visibility, Not Opacity — The AI newsroom's operations are fully visible. Users can inspect any
agent's reasoning, trace any story's provenance, and audit any decision.

4. Focus, Not Noise — The interface prioritises what needs human attention. Routine operations
happen automatically; exceptions surface prominently.

The Agbofa Nexus AI frontend operates on a Mission Control metaphor:

I.2 FRONTEND DESIGN PRINCIPLES
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            FRONTEND DESIGN PRINCIPLES                            │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 1: AI VISIBILITY                                 │

│ ────────────────────────                                        │

│ Every AI action is visible to the user. Agent activity is surfaced in            │

│ real-time. Confidence scores are displayed prominently. Users never                          │

│ wonder "what is the AI doing right now?"                             │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 2: PROGRESSIVE DISCLOSURE                                      │

│ ──────────────────────────────────                                           │

│ Complex AI capabilities are revealed progressively. The default view                     │

│ shows essential information. Users drill down for detail. Advanced                       │

│ features are discoverable but not overwhelming.                              │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 3: CONFIDENCE-FIRST INFORMATION HIERARCHY                                          │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────                                                  │

│ Content confidence level determines visual prominence. High-confidence                               │

│ content appears ready for action. Low-confidence content demands                                 │

│ attention. The user's eye is drawn to what needs their judgment.                         │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 4: ACTION-ORIENTED INTERFACES                                          │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                                 │

│ Every screen has a clear primary action. The interface reduces cognitive                     │
│ load by presenting the most relevant action prominently. Secondary                    │

│ actions are available but not competing.                      │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 5: CONSISTENT MENTAL MODEL                                  │

│ ──────────────────────────────────                                        │

│ The platform behaves consistently. Stories flow left to right through             │

│ pipeline stages. Confidence uses consistent colour semantics. Agent                   │

│ interactions follow consistent patterns. Users build one mental model.                │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 6: REAL-TIME BY DEFAULT                                 │

│ ────────────────────────────                                      │

│ The newsroom operates in real-time; the interface reflects this. Data             │

│ updates live. Notifications appear immediately. Story states change               │

│ before the user's eyes. The interface feels alive.                │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 7: KEYBOARD-DRIVEN EFFICIENCY                               │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ Power users operate the newsroom primarily via keyboard. Every action                     │

│ has a keyboard shortcut. The Command Palette provides universal access.                   │

│ Mouse is for exploration; keyboard is for execution.                  │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 8: ACCESSIBLE BY DESIGN                              │

│ ────────────────────────────                                      │

│ WCAG 2.2 AA compliance is not an add-on — it is a design constraint                   │

│ applied from the first wireframe. Every component meets accessibility                 │

│ standards. Every workflow is keyboard-navigable. Every visualisation                  │
│ has text alternatives.                               │

│                                            │

│ PRINCIPLE 9: RESPONSIVE FROM DESKTOP TO FIELD                           │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                                 │

│ The newsroom operates from desktop workstations, laptops in the field,          │

│ and mobile devices for on-the-go monitoring. Every critical workflow        │

│ functions at every breakpoint, with appropriate adaptations.            │

│                                            │

│ PRINCIPLE 10: BRAND-ADAPTIVE THEMING                                │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                   │

│ The platform supports light, dark, and system themes. Multi-tenant          │

│ deployments support tenant-specific branding (colours, logos, typography) │

│ while maintaining consistent interaction patterns.              │

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



I.3 AI-FIRST USER EXPERIENCE



I.3.1 The AI-First Paradigm



Traditional CMS: User → Form → Content → Publish

Agbofa Nexus AI: User → Direct AI Agents → Review AI Output → Approve/Publish



The AI-First UX manifests in every screen:
Traditional CMS Pattern AI-First Pattern

User writes headline AI proposes 5 headlines with scores; user selects or edits

User finds images AI generates images with prompts; user approves or adjusts

User checks facts AI verifies claims with sources; user reviews flagged items

User schedules posts AI recommends optimal schedule; user confirms or overrides

User monitors analytics AI surfaces anomalies and insights; user investigates



I.3.2 AI Presence in the Interface

│                                                │

│ 1. PROFESSIONAL AUTHORITY — The platform must inspire trust. Visual design │

│     communicates reliability, precision, and editorial integrity. Clean        │

│     lines, clear hierarchy, restrained colour palette.             │
│                                              │

│ 2. TECHNOLOGICAL SOPHISTICATION — The platform is AI-native. Subtle                    │

│     animations, glassmorphism accents, and intelligent use of motion           │

│                                              │

│ 3. OPERATIONAL CLARITY — The newsroom is complex. The interface reduces                    │

│     that complexity through clear information architecture, consistent         │

│     patterns, and progressive disclosure. Every pixel serves understanding. │

│                                              │

│ VISUAL REFERENCES:                                      │

│ • Notion: Clean typography, flexible layouts                   │

│ • Linear: Modern SaaS design, command palette                       │

│ GRID SYSTEM:                                           │

│ ───────────                                        │

│ • 12-column grid for page layouts                            │

│ • Column gap: 24px (desktop), 16px (tablet), 12px (mobile)                     │

│ • Max content width: 1440px (centred)                              │

│ • Full-width available for dashboards                          │

│ • Sidebar width: 240px (collapsed: 64px)                           │

│ • Context panel width: 360px                               │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



III.5 COMPONENT PRINCIPLES



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             COMPONENT DESIGN PRINCIPLES                            │

│                                             │

│ CARD SYSTEM:                                           │

│ ───────────                                        │

│ • Cards are the primary content container                          │

│ • Variants: Default, Elevated, Outlined, Interactive                   │

│ • Padding: 16px (default), 20px (large), 12px (compact)                    │

│ • Border radius: 12px (default cards), 8px (compact cards)                     │
│ • Background: bg-secondary with 1px border (light), subtle gradient (dark) │

│ • Hover: bg-tertiary, subtle shadow increase                             │

│ • Glassmorphism variant: backdrop-blur, semi-transparent bg                              │

│                                             │

│ FORM COMPONENTS:                                                 │

│ ───────────────                                          │

│ • Input height: 40px (default), 32px (compact), 48px (large)                         │

│ • Border radius: 8px                                 │

│ • Border: 1.5px, border-primary (default), brand-primary (focus)                         │

│ • Label: Above input, text-sm, text-secondary                            │

│ • Error state: Red border, error message below                               │

│ • Disabled: Reduced opacity (0.5), not-allowed cursor                            │

│ • All inputs support: normal, hover, focus, error, disabled, read-only                   │

│                                             │

│ BUTTON HIERARCHY:                                            │

│ ────────────────                                         │

│ • Primary: Solid brand colour, white text, for main actions                          │

│ • Secondary: Outlined, for secondary actions                             │

│ • Tertiary/Ghost: No border/bg, for subtle actions                           │

│ • Danger: Red, for destructive actions                               │

│ • Sizes: sm (32px), md (40px), lg (48px)                             │

│ • Icon-only variant: Square, for toolbar actions                         │

│ • Loading state: Spinner replaces text, button disabled                          │

│ • All buttons: Focus ring, keyboard activatable                          │

│                                             │

│ TABLE SYSTEM:                                        │
│ ────────────                                         │

│ • Header: Semi-bold, uppercase tracking, sticky on scroll                    │

│ • Rows: Alternating subtle background (optional), hover highlight                    │

│ • Sorting: Click column header to sort; indicator icon                   │

│ • Selection: Checkbox column; select all; bulk actions bar                   │

│ • Pagination: Bottom, with page size selector                        │

│ • Responsive: Horizontal scroll on mobile with sticky first column                   │

│ • Empty state: Illustration + message + action                       │

│                                              │

│ MODAL & DRAWER SYSTEM:                                           │

│ ──────────────────────                                       │

│ • Modal: Centred overlay, max-width 560px (default), 720px (large)                       │

│ • Drawer: Slides from right, width 480px (default), 640px (wide)                 │

│ • Backdrop: Semi-transparent overlay with blur                           │

│ • Close: X button (top-right), Esc key, click backdrop               │

│ • Focus trap: Tab cycles within modal/drawer                             │

│ • Scroll: Content scrolls if exceeds viewport; header/footer fixed               │

│                                              │

│ TOAST NOTIFICATIONS:                                     │

│ ───────────────────                                      │

│ • Position: Bottom-right (desktop), bottom-centre (mobile)                       │

│ • Duration: 5 seconds (info), 8 seconds (warning), persistent (error)                │

│ • Types: Success (green), Error (red), Warning (amber), Info (blue)              │

│ • Actions: Optional action button, dismiss button                        │

│ • Stacking: Newest at bottom, max 4 visible                          │

│ • Animation: Slide in from right, fade out                       │
│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



III.6 STATES & FEEDBACK



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              COMPONENT STATES & FEEDBACK                            │

│                                              │

│ EVERY INTERACTIVE COMPONENT MUST HANDLE:                                      │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                     │

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STATE       DESCRIPTION              VISUAL TREATMENT               ││

│ │ ─────       ───────────              ────────────────                 ││

│ │ Default     Resting state           Standard styling         ││

│ │ Hover       Mouse cursor over          Subtle bg change, cursor        ││

│ │ Focus       Keyboard focused          Visible focus ring (2px)      ││

│ │ Active      Being pressed/clicked      Darker bg, subtle scale        ││

│ │ Disabled     Not available           Reduced opacity (0.5)        ││

│ │ Loading      Processing             Skeleton or spinner        ││

│ │ Empty       No data available         Illustration + message        ││

│ │ Error      Something went wrong          Red indicator + message           ││
│ │ Success     Action completed             Green indicator + message │ │

│ │ Read-only    Viewable, not editable        No interactive indicators │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                               │

│ LOADING STATES:                                          │

│ ──────────────                                           │

│ • Skeleton screens: Mimic content layout with animated placeholders                   │

│ • Spinners: For actions < 2 seconds                           │

│ • Progress bars: For processes with known duration                        │

│ • Streaming text: For AI content generation (words appear progressively) │

│ • Pulsing dots: For AI "thinking" states                          │

│                                               │

│ EMPTY STATES:                                        │

│ ────────────                                         │

│ • Relevant illustration or icon                              ││

│ • Clear heading explaining the empty state                            │

│ • Descriptive subtext with guidance                               │

│ • Primary action button (where applicable)                            │

│ • Example: "No stories in review queue — All clear! Stories will appear           │

│ here when confidence scores require human review."                            │

│                                               │

│ ERROR STATES:                                        │

│ ────────────                                         │

│ • Clear error message (what happened)                                 │

│ • Actionable guidance (what to do about it)                           │
│ • Retry button (where applicable)                                 │

│ • Error reference code (for support)                              │

│ • Never show raw stack traces to users                                │

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



III.7 MOTION DESIGN



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              MOTION DESIGN PRINCIPLES                                 │

│                                            │

│ ANIMATION PHILOSOPHY:                                         │

│ ────────────────────                                          │

│ Motion serves purpose, never decoration. Animations communicate state                 │

│ changes, guide attention, and provide feedback. They are fast, subtle,            │

│ and respectful of user preferences.                               │

│                                            │

│ DURATION TOKENS:                                          │

│ ───────────────                                       │

│ • Instant (0ms): Layout changes, value updates                            │

│ • Micro (100ms): Button presses, icon state changes                           │

│ • Quick (200ms): Hover effects, tooltip appearance                            │

│ • Standard (300ms): Modal open/close, drawer slide, page transitions              │
│ • Slow (500ms): Complex transitions, celebratory animations                                │

│                                             │

│ EASING TOKENS:                                         │

│ ─────────────                                       │

│ • Default: ease-out (decelerating — natural feeling)                           │

│ • Entrance: ease-out (elements entering the screen)                                │

│ • Exit: ease-in (elements leaving the screen)                          │

│ • Bounce: cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) (celebratory)                     │

│                                             │

│ ANIMATION PATTERNS:                                            │

│ ──────────────────                                         │

│ • Page transitions: Fade + subtle slide (200ms)                        │

│ • List items: Staggered fade-in (50ms delay per item)                          │

│ • Modal: Scale + fade backdrop (300ms)                                 │

│ • Toast: Slide from right + fade (300ms)                           │

│ • AI content: Streaming text reveal (character by character)                           │

│ • Confidence change: Value counts up/down smoothly                                     │

│ • Agent activity: Subtle pulse on active agents                        │

│ • Breaking news: Attention-grabbing but not alarming animation                                     │

│                                             │

│ REDUCED MOTION:                                            │

│ ──────────────                                         │

│ • All animations respect prefers-reduced-motion                                │

│ • When reduced: Instant transitions, no movement, fades only                                   │

│ • No auto-playing animations over 5 seconds                                │

│                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

remaining key screens:



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

│                                                │

│                                              │

│ Each item: Story title, confidence score (colour + number), age,                     │

│ reason for review, assigned editor.                          │

│ Quick actions: "Review", "Assign to Me", "Reassign", "Quick Approve".                        │

│ Actions per platform: "Publish Now", "Schedule", "Edit Variant", "Skip". │

│ Bulk: "Publish to All", "Schedule All".                      │

│ Preview: Platform-specific preview on hover/click.                       │

│ Post-publish: Status updates, URL capture, engagement initial metrics.                       │

│                                              │

│ Features: Syntax highlighting, variable autocomplete, test run,                       │

PART V — DASHBOARD ARCHITECTURE



V.1 DASHBOARD DESIGN PRINCIPLES



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐
│            DASHBOARD ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES                              │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 1: INFORMATION HIERARCHY                                    │

│ Most critical information at top-left (F-pattern reading).                │

│ Breaking news and alerts → KPIs → Trends → Detail.                            │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 2: ACTIONABLE DATA                                  │

│ Every data point that requires action has a direct action link.               │

│ "Stories in Review: 8" → Click to open Review Queue.                          │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 3: REAL-TIME WHERE IT MATTERS                                   │

│ Breaking news, agent status, queue depth: real-time.                          │

│ Historical trends, audience data: near-real-time or periodic refresh.                 │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 4: CONFIGURABLE DENSITY                                 │

│ Users choose: Compact (maximum data), Comfortable (default), Relaxed.                     │

│ Density affects: card padding, chart size, font size.                │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 5: DRILL-DOWN CAPABILITY                                │

│ Every KPI card is clickable for detail. Every chart supports zoom.                │

│ Every metric has an "Explore" link to full analytics.                │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 6: CONSISTENT TIME CONTROLS                                     │

│ Global time range selector: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days,              │

│ This Month, Custom Range. Individual widgets can override.                        │

│                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART VI — USER WORKFLOWS



VI.1 CORE WORKFLOW PATTERNS
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              CORE WORKFLOW PATTERNS                          │

│                                              │

│ WORKFLOW 1: DISCOVER & VERIFY STORY                                  │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                    │

│                                              │

│ 1. User receives notification: "New story candidate detected"                │

│     │                                         │

│     ▼                                             │

│ 2. User opens Story Pipeline → Story in "Seed" column                    │

│     │                                         │

│     ▼                                             │

│ 3. User clicks story → Story Detail view                    │

│     │                                         │

│     ▼                                             │

│ 4. User reviews: AI-generated summary, source list, initial confidence           │

│     │                                         │

│     ├── Confidence ≥ 0.85: Story auto-assigned to Writer                 │

│     │                                         │

│     └── Confidence < 0.85: User decides:                    │

│         ├── "Assign" → Select agent or let AI assign             │

│         ├── "Research More" → Request additional research                    │

│         └── "Reject" → Story killed with reason              │

│                                              │
│ WORKFLOW 2: HUMAN REVIEW & APPROVAL                                             │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                            │

│                                            │

│ 1. User receives notification: "Story requires human review"                        │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 2. User opens Human Review Queue → Sorted by priority                                   │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 3. User clicks story → Editorial Workspace with Review Mode                             │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 4. User reviews:                                    │

│   • Content preview (as it will appear)                         │

│   • Confidence breakdown (all dimensions)                               │

│   • Fact-check results                                  │

│   • Source list with reliability scores                     │

│   • AI recommendations and rationale                                │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 5. User decides:                                    │

│   ├── "Approve" → Story published; confidence recorded                              │

│   ├── "Approve with Edits" → Opens Article Editor; then publish                         │

│   ├── "Request Changes" → Returns to AI with editor notes                           │

│   ├── "Reject" → Story returned to draft; reason required                       │

│   └── "Escalate" → Sent to Managing Editor or EIC                           │
│                                             │

│ WORKFLOW 3: BREAKING NEWS RESPONSE                                           │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                        │

│                                             │

│ 1. Breaking alert appears: Visual + Audio (if enabled) + Notification                │

│    │                                          │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 2. User clicks alert → Breaking News Centre                      │

│    │                                          │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 3. User reviews: Initial brief (AI-generated), sources, confidence               │

│    │                                          │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 4. User actions (rapid, one-click where possible):                   │

│   ├── "Publish Brief" → Initial version published immediately                    │

│   ├── "Hold for Verification" → Brief held; verification accelerated                 │

│   ├── "Edit Brief" → Quick edit then publish                     │

│   └── "Assign Coverage Team" → Multiple agents assigned                          │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 5. Continuous monitoring: Timeline updates live; user intervenes as needed │

│    │                                         │

│    ▼                                             │

│ 6. Story stabilises → "End Breaking" → Transitions to standard monitoring │

│                                             │

│ WORKFLOW 4: CORRECTION ISSUANCE                                      │
│ ───────────────────────────────                                        │

│                                               │

│ 1. Correction alert: AI detects error OR user/audience reports error           │

│      │                                        │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 2. User opens Corrections & Retractions → Reviews flagged issue                │

│      │                                        │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 3. User verifies: Compare original vs. corrected information               │

│      │                                        │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 4. User reviews AI-drafted correction notice                       │

│      │                                        │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 5. User approves/rejects based on severity:                        │

│     • Minor: Content Editor can approve                        │

│     • Significant: Desk Editor approval required                   │

│     • Major: Managing Editor approval required                         │

│     • Critical: EIC approval required                   │

│      │                                         │

│      ▼                                             │

│ 6. Correction published: Content updated; notice posted; derivatives synced │

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART VII — AI INTERACTION EXPERIENCE



VII.1 AI INTERACTION PATTERNS



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            AI INTERACTION PATTERNS                        │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 1: AI ASSISTANT PANEL (Contextual Sidebar)                    │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                               │

│ • Always-available panel (toggle with ⌘/)                     │

│ • Context-aware: Shows relevant AI insights for current screen            │

│ • Sections: AI Suggestions, Agent Status, Confidence Info, Quick Actions │

│ • User can ask questions: "Summarise this story", "Find related stories" │

│ • Responses appear in threaded conversation within panel                  │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 2: INLINE AI SUGGESTIONS                              │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                   │

│ • AI suggestions appear subtly in context                     │

│ • Article editor: Margin highlights for suggested improvements            │

│ • Dashboard: "AI Insight" callouts on anomalies                   │

│ • Verification: Suggested sources or contradictions flagged           │
│ • Visual treatment: Subtle blue glow or dotted underline                   │

│ • Hover: Preview suggestion; Click: Apply or expand                    │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 3: CONFIDENCE INDICATORS (Everywhere)                                  │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ • Appears on every AI-generated output                         │

│ • Visual: Colour bar (green/amber/red) + numeric score + icon                      │

│ • Position: Consistent location (top-right of content area)                │

│ • Click: Opens confidence breakdown panel                          │

│ • Breakdown: Per-dimension scores with contributing factors                        │

│ • Explainability: "Why this score?" shows agent reasoning                      │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 4: MULTI-AGENT CONVERSATION VIEW                                       │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                           │

│ • For complex tasks, user can observe agent collaboration                      │

│ • View: Chat-like interface showing agent-to-agent messages                        │

│ • Each message: Agent avatar, message content, timestamp                           │

│ • User can interject: "Suggest different angle" or "Ask FactCheck to verify"│

│ • User messages highlighted differently from agent messages                        │

│ • Transcript preserved for audit                           │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 5: FEEDBACK COLLECTION                                 │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                    │

│ • Every AI output has         feedback buttons                         │

│ • Thumbs down opens: Quick reason selector + optional comment                          │

│ • Reasons: "Inaccurate", "Poor quality", "Wrong tone", "Not relevant"                  │
│ • Feedback immediately logged; feeds Continuous Learning Engine             │

│ • User can see their feedback history on outputs                │

│                                             │

│ PATTERN 6: PROMPT VISIBILITY & EDITING                          │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                │

│ • "View Prompt" link on AI-generated content                    │

│ • Opens prompt viewer: System prompt + Context + Task prompt                │

│ • Read-only by default; editable with appropriate permissions           │

│ • "Test Changes" to see output with modified prompt                 │

│ • Version history tracked for all prompt edits              │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

│ ──────────────────────                                         │

│                                                │

│ LOADING:                                              │

│                                                │

│ • Service Worker for offline shell                                │

│ • API response caching (stale-while-revalidate)                               │

│ • IndexedDB for client-side data persistence                              │
│                                            │

│ OFFLINE & PWA:                                     │

│ • PWA-capable for mobile monitoring                        │

│ • Offline: Cached dashboards, queued actions                   │

XII.2 DESIGN DECISION RECORDS (DDRs)



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           DESIGN DECISION RECORDS                          │

│                                            │

│ DDR-001: Three-Panel Layout as Primary Desktop Pattern                     │

│ Decision: Primary workspace uses sidebar | content | context panel                 │

│ Rationale: Maximises information density while maintaining focus on content │

│ Context panel provides AI insights without leaving the workspace               │

│                                            │

│ DDR-002: Confidence-First Visual Hierarchy                         │

│ Decision: Confidence score determines visual prominence of AI content                  │

│ Rationale: Draws user attention to content requiring human judgment                    │

│ Colour + icon + number ensures accessibility for colour-blind users            │

│                                            │
│ DDR-003: Command Palette as Universal Interaction Pattern                      │

│ Decision: ⌘K activates searchable command palette for all actions                  │

│ Rationale: Power-user efficiency; reduces reliance on mouse navigation                 │

│ All platform actions accessible via keyboard through palette               │

│                                             │

│ DDR-004: Streaming AI Content Display                          │

│ Decision: AI-generated content appears progressively (character/word stream) │

│ Rationale: Communicates AI activity; allows early review; reduces perceived │

│ latency; distinguishes AI generation from static content               │

│                                            │

│ DDR-005: Glassmorphism for AI-Related UI Elements                          │

│ Decision: Subtle glassmorphism (backdrop-blur, semi-transparency) for AI               │

│ panels, suggestion cards, and confidence indicators                    │

│ Rationale: Creates visual distinction between human-managed and AI-managed │

│ interface elements; communicates technological sophistication                  │

│                                            │

│ DDR-006: Real-Time by Default, Configurable                        │

│ Decision: All dashboards and pipeline views update in real-time by default │

│ Rationale: Newsroom operations are time-sensitive; stale data risks missed │

│ stories; users can reduce refresh frequency for focus work                 │

│                                             │

│ DDR-007: Mobile as Monitoring and Approval Platform                        │

│ Decision: Mobile experience optimised for monitoring, alerts, and approvals │

│ rather than content creation                               │

│ Rationale: Content creation requires desktop-class screen and keyboard;                │

│ mobile serves the "on-call editor" use case for time-sensitive decisions           │
│                                          │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

XII.4 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY



Volume 7 of the Agbofa Nexus AI enterprise architecture defines the complete frontend
experience and user interface specification for the Autonomous AI Media Company Platform.
This document transforms the architectural specifications of Volumes 1–6 into a concrete,
implementable user experience blueprint.
Key Achievements:



1. AI-Native UX Paradigm — The platform is designed from the ground up as an AI operating
system for newsrooms, not a traditional CMS. AI presence permeates the interface through
confidence indicators, agent activity feeds, inline suggestions, and explainability panels.

2. Mission Control Metaphor — The three-panel desktop layout (Navigation | Content | AI
Context) provides a consistent mental model that scales from executive oversight to detailed
content editing.

3. Complete Screen Catalogue — 48 screens fully specified with layouts, components,
interactions, states, responsive behaviour, and accessibility requirements. Every screen is
documented to a level that enables independent implementation by AI coding agents.

4. Comprehensive Design System — Typography, colour, spacing, component, motion, and state
systems defined with design tokens. Light and dark themes. Multi-tenant branding support.
WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility embedded from foundation.

5. Confidence-First Information Architecture — The platform's most innovative UX pattern: AI-
generated content displays its confidence score prominently, drawing human attention to
decisions that require judgment while allowing high-confidence content to flow autonomously.

6. Responsive from Desktop to Field — Six breakpoints with appropriate adaptations. Desktop
for editorial work, tablet for monitoring, mobile for alerts and approvals. Every critical workflow
functions at every breakpoint.

7. Enterprise Governance — Design review process, component versioning, UX quality metrics,
continuous improvement framework, and architecture decision records ensure the frontend
evolves with discipline.



The Experience:



An editor-in-chief opens the Executive Dashboard each morning to review the AI newsroom's
overnight performance — stories published, confidence trends, agent activity, and any
escalations requiring attention. A managing editor works through the Human Review Queue,
approving high-confidence stories with a single click and providing feedback on stories requiring
revision. A content editor refines an AI-generated article in the Article Editor, accepting AI
suggestions for improved clarity and requesting additional context where needed. An on-call
editor receives a breaking news push notification on their phone, reviews the AI-generated
initial brief, and approves publication — all within 60 seconds of the alert.



Throughout this experience, AI is not a chatbot in the corner. It is the fabric of the platform —
visible, explainable, and accountable. The user is not operating a content management system.
They are commanding an AI newsroom.



This volume, together with the complete Agbofa Nexus AI enterprise architecture (Volumes 1–
7), provides the blueprint for building the world's leading autonomous AI media company
platform.

PART I — FRONTEND ENGINEERING STRATEGY



I.1 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES



The Agbofa Nexus AI frontend is not a website with AI features. It is an AI operating system for
newsrooms, delivered through a browser. This distinction drives every engineering decision.



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            FRONTEND ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES                             │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 1: AI-NATIVE RENDERING                               │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                      │

│ The frontend renders AI-generated content as a first-class data type.      │

│ Streaming AI responses appear progressively. Confidence scores update          │

│ in real-time. Agent activity streams as events. The rendering engine       │

│ treats AI outputs differently from static content — with loading states    │

│ optimised for variable-duration generation, progressive disclosure,        │

│ and inline confidence visualisation.                       │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 2: REAL-TIME BY DEFAULT                              │

│ ────────────────────────────                                       │

│ The newsroom operates in real-time. The frontend reflects this through         │

│ WebSocket connections for live data, Server-Sent Events for agent streams, │
│ and optimistic updates for user actions. Stale data is a bug, not a             │

│ feature. Every data display declares its freshness.                 │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 3: COMPOSABLE OVER MONOLITHIC                                     │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                        │

│ The application is composed of feature modules that can be developed,                       │

│ tested, and deployed independently. Each module owns its routes,                        │

│ components, state, and API interactions. Shared code is extracted                   │

│ upward, not duplicated across modules.                          │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 4: SERVER-FIRST RENDERING                                 │

│ ────────────────────────────────                                        │

│ Next.js App Router with React Server Components is the default rendering │

│ strategy. Client components are used only where interactivity requires                  │

│ them. This maximises performance, SEO, and initial load experience                      │

│ while maintaining rich interactivity where needed.                      │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 5: TYPE SAFETY THROUGHOUT                                     │

│ ────────────────────────────────                                        │

│ TypeScript strict mode across the entire codebase. API contracts are                │

│ typed end-to-end using shared type packages. No `any` types in                      │

│ production code. AI-generated content carries typed metadata.                       │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 6: OFFLINE-CAPABLE WHERE CRITICAL                                 │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────                                             │

│ The newsroom cannot stop because the network did. Critical monitoring,                      │
│ drafting, and approval workflows function offline. Actions queue and                        │

│ sync when connectivity returns. The offline experience is designed,                     │

│ not accidental.                                     │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 7: ACCESSIBILITY AS ARCHITECTURE                                  │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                            │

│ Accessibility is not tested in — it is architected in. Component                │

│ contracts include ARIA requirements. The design system enforces                         │

│ contrast ratios. Keyboard navigation is a first-class interaction               │

│ model. Automated testing catches regressions before merge.                          │

│                                              │

│ PRINCIPLE 8: OBSERVABLE BY DESIGN                                   │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                         │

│ Every user action, every API call, every render, every error is             │

│ observable. The frontend emits structured telemetry that feeds the                      │

│ platform's operational dashboards. Performance regressions are detected                         │

│ in CI, not discovered by users.                           │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



I.2 ENTERPRISE CODING STANDARDS



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐
│            ENTERPRISE CODING STANDARDS                             │

│                                              │

│ NAMING CONVENTIONS:                                            │

│ ──────────────────                                        │

│ • Files: kebab-case (story-pipeline.tsx, use-story-state.ts)               │

│ • Components: PascalCase (StoryPipeline, AgentMonitor)                             │

│ • Functions: camelCase (fetchStory, calculateConfidence)                       │

│ • Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS)                                         │

│ • Types/Interfaces: PascalCase, prefixed where disambiguating                      │

│ (Story, IStoryService, TStoryState)                            │

│ • Hooks: camelCase, prefixed with 'use' (useStory, useAgentStream)                     │

│ • Stores: camelCase, suffixed with 'Store' (storyStore, agentStore)                │

│                                              │

│ FILE ORGANISATION:                                       │

│ ─────────────────                                        │

│ • One component per file (except tightly coupled sub-components)                       │

│ • Co-located styles, tests, and types                          │

│ • Barrel exports (index.ts) for public module API                      │

│ • Internal utilities not exported from barrels                     │

│                                              │

│ TYPE SYSTEM:                                         │

│ ───────────                                          │

│ • TypeScript strict mode enabled                               │

│ • Explicit return types on all exported functions                      │

│ • Discriminated unions for state management                                │

│ • Branded types for identifiers (StoryId, AgentId, WorkspaceId)                    │
│ • Zod schemas for runtime validation of API boundaries                       │

│                                           │

│ CODE QUALITY:                                      │

│ ────────────                                      │

│ • ESLint with strict configuration                       │

│ • Prettier for formatting (no debates)                       │

│ • Husky pre-commit hooks (lint, format, type-check)                      │

│ • Commitlint for conventional commits                            │

│ • No console.log in production (use structured logger)                   │

│ • Maximum function complexity enforced (ESLint complexity rule)                  │

│                                           │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



I.3 FEATURE-BASED ARCHITECTURE



The application is organised around feature modules, not technical layers. Each feature module
is a self-contained unit that owns everything needed to deliver its functionality.



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            FEATURE-BASED ARCHITECTURE                            │

│                                           │

│ MODULE STRUCTURE (per feature):                                  │

│ ──────────────────────────────                                       │
│                                               │

│ modules/[feature]/                                         │

│ ├── components/            # Feature-specific components                                       │

│ │ ├── [Component].tsx                                              │

│ │ ├── [Component].test.tsx                                             │

│ │ └── [Component].stories.tsx                                          │

│ ├── hooks/           # Feature-specific hooks                                      │

│ │ ├── use[Feature].ts                                      │

│ │ └── use[Feature].test.ts                                     │

│ ├── stores/          # Feature-specific state (Zustand slices)                             │

│ │ └── [feature]-store.ts                                   │

│ ├── services/         # Feature-specific API calls                                 │

│ │ └── [feature]-service.ts                                 │

│ ├── types/           # Feature-specific types                                  │

│ │ └── index.ts                                         │

│ ├── utils/          # Feature-specific utilities                           │

│ │ └── [util].ts                                    │

│ ├── constants.ts       # Feature-specific constants                                    │

│ └── index.ts        # Public API (barrel export)                               │

│                                               │

│ FEATURE MODULES (Primary):                                                 │

│ ─────────────────────────                                                      │

│                                               │

│ modules/dashboard/          # AI Newsroom, Executive, Custom dashboards                                │

I.5 RELEASE STRATEGY



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│               RELEASE STRATEGY                          │

│                                            │

│ BRANCHING STRATEGY: Trunk-Based Development                                             │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                                   │

│ • main: Always deployable, protected                                    │

│ • Feature branches: Short-lived (< 2 days), merged via PR                           │

│ • Release branches: Created from main for versioned releases                                │

│ • Hotfix branches: From main, merged to main and release branch                                 │

│                                            │

│ CI/CD PIPELINE (GitHub Actions):                                    │

│ ────────────────────────────────                                            │

│                                            │
│ Pull Request:                                      │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ Lint → Type Check → Unit Tests → Component Tests → Build Check          ││

│ │ → Lighthouse Budget Check → Visual Regression → Preview Deploy          ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ Merge to Main:                                         │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ Full Test Suite → Integration Tests → E2E Tests (critical paths)   ││

│ │ → Production Build → Staging Deploy → Smoke Tests                  ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ Production Release:                                        │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ Manual Approval → Blue-Green Deploy → Health Check → Traffic Shift      ││

│ │ → Monitor (1 hour) → Full Traffic                            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ FEATURE FLAGS:                                         │

│ ─────────────                                          │

│ • All new features behind flags (LaunchDarkly or custom)             │

│ • Percentage rollouts for risk mitigation                       │
│ • Kill switches for emergency disable                    │

│ • A/B test support for UX experiments                        │

│                                              │

│ VERSIONING: Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH)                      │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                             │

│ • MAJOR: Breaking changes to user-facing behaviour                   │

│ • MINOR: New features, non-breaking                          │

│ • PATCH: Bug fixes, performance improvements                     │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```
