II.2 RENDERING STRATEGY



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│                RENDERING STRATEGY                            │

│                                              │

│ COMPONENT TYPE DECISION TREE:                                       │

│ ────────────────────────────                                       │

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ Does component need:                                   ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ • useState / useEffect?                       │ ││

│ │ │ • Browser-only APIs (localStorage, WebSocket, canvas)?                  │ ││

│ │ │ • Event listeners (onClick, onChange)?                       │ ││

│ │ │ • Custom hooks with state?                           │ ││
│ ││                                             │ ││

│ │ │ YES → Client Component ("use client")                       │ ││

│ │ │ NO → Server Component (default)                             │ ││

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                 │

│ RENDERING PATTERNS:                                     │

│ ──────────────────                                      │

│                                                 │

│ STATIC (Pre-rendered at build time):                            │

│ • Marketing pages, documentation, legal                             │

│ • Never changes without deployment                                  │

│                                                 │

│ DYNAMIC (Server-rendered per request):                              │

│ • Dashboards with initial data                              │

│ • Story pages (SSR with CDN caching where appropriate)                              │

│ • Settings pages (personalised)                             │

│                                                 │

│ STREAMING (Progressive server rendering):                               │

│ • AI-generated content (streamed as generated)                              │

│ • Large dashboards (shell immediate, data streams in)                           │

│ • Story Graph (complex visualisation loads progressively)                       │

│                                                 │

│ CLIENT-SIDE (SPA-like within shell):                            │

│ • Article Editor (rich text, AI suggestions)                    │
│ • Real-time dashboards (WebSocket updates)                         │

│ • Story Graph interactions (canvas manipulation)                   │

│                                            │

│ PARTIAL PRERENDERING (PPR) — Enterprise:                           │

│ • Static shell with dynamic holes for personalised content             │

│ • Combines instant navigation with fresh data                  │

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



II.3 STREAMING AI CONTENT



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            STREAMING AI CONTENT ARCHITECTURE                           │

│                                            │

│ AI-generated content is not fetched — it is streamed. The user sees        │

│ content appearing progressively, just as they would watching a human type. │

│                                            │

│ IMPLEMENTATION: React Suspense + Server Components + ReadableStream            │

│                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ SERVER COMPONENT (Streaming)                               ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────                                ││
│ │                                             ││

│ │ async function StoryContent({ storyId }: { storyId: string }) {              ││

│ │ // This server component streams AI content as it's generated                      ││

│ │ const stream = await ai.generateStoryContent(storyId);                        ││

│ │ return <StreamingContent stream={stream} />;                              ││

│ │ }                                           ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ // Wrapped in Suspense:                                       ││

│ │ <Suspense fallback={<ContentSkeleton />}>                                ││

│ │ <StoryContent storyId={storyId} />                                 ││

│ │ </Suspense>                                          ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                               │

│ STREAMING STATES:                                           │

│ ────────────────                                            │

│                                               │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ STATE         VISUAL                 DURATION                 ││

│ │ ─────          ──────                   ────────              ││

│ │ IDLE         Skeleton placeholder          —                   ││

│ │ CONNECTING          Pulsing indicator           < 500ms                 ││

│ │ STREAMING          Content appearing word-by-word Variable                        ││

│ │ PARTIAL         Partial content visible     Ongoing                 ││

│ │ COMPLETE          Full content rendered          —                  ││

│ │ ERROR          Error message + retry         —                     ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ CONFIDENCE STREAMING:                                        │

│ Confidence score updates alongside content. As verification completes,                   │

│ the score transitions from "calculating" to a specific value, with       │

│ smooth animation from previous score to new score.                       │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



II.4 SEO ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│               SEO ARCHITECTURE                           │

│                                              │

│ PUBLIC-FACING CONTENT (News articles, landing pages):                            │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────                                         │

│ • Full SSR with comprehensive metadata                           │

│ • Structured data (JSON-LD): Article, NewsArticle, BreadcrumbList                    │

│ • Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata                               │

│ • Dynamic sitemap generation (per workspace, per brand)                          │

│ • Canonical URLs with proper hreflang for multi-language                     │

│ • CDN caching with intelligent invalidation (on story update/correction) │
│                                             │

│ APPLICATION INTERIOR (Dashboards, editors, settings):                        │

│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────                                   │

│ • No indexing (X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow)                      │

│ • Authenticated routes return 403 for unauthenticated crawlers                   │

│ • Minimal metadata (title only for browser tab)                      │

│                                             │

│ METADATA ARCHITECTURE:                                       │

│ ─────────────────────                                    │

│ • generateMetadata() for dynamic routes                          │

│ • Shared metadata defaults in root layout                        │

│ • Per-page overrides for title, description, OG images                   │

│ • Template-based titles: "%s | Agbofa Nexus AI"                      │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART IV — COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE



IV.1 COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE STRATEGY



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE STRATEGY                               │

│                                              │

│ ATOMIC DESIGN (Adapted for AI-Native Application):                           │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────                                     │

│                                              │

│ ATOMS: Primitive, non-contextual UI elements                         │

│ ──────────────────────────────────────────                                       │

│ Button, Input, Badge, Icon, Avatar, Spinner, Skeleton, Divider               │

│ • Location: components/ui/                                  │

│ • No business logic                                    │

│ • Fully typed props                                    │

│ • All states handled (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading)          │
│ • Accessibility built-in (aria attributes, keyboard support)                   │

│                                              │

│ MOLECULES: Composed atoms with simple behaviour                                        │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                                  │

│ ConfidenceBadge, AgentAvatar, KpiCard, SearchInput, NotificationItem                               │

│ • Location: components/ai/, components/dashboard/, etc.                                │

│ • May contain simple hooks (useState, useCallback)                             │

│ • Storybook stories with all variants                          │

│                                              │

│ ORGANISMS: Complex composed sections                                       │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                               │

│ StoryPipelineCard, AgentActivityFeed, ConfidenceBreakdown,                                 │

│ PublishingChecklist, HumanReviewItem                                   │

│ • Location: modules/[feature]/components/                                  │

│ • Feature-specific business logic                              │

│ • May connect to stores or services                                │

│                                              │

│ TEMPLATES: Page-level layouts                                      │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                          │

│ DashboardLayout, EditorialLayout, SettingsLayout                               │

│ • Location: components/layout/                                     │

│ • Define page structure, not content                               │

│                                              │

│ PAGES: Route-level composition                                     │

│ ─────────────────────────────                                          │

│ • Location: app/ routes                                  │
│ • Compose templates + organisms into complete pages                          │

│ • Server Components where possible                                 │

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



IV.2 COMPONENT CONTRACTS



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              COMPONENT CONTRACTS                               │

│                                               │

│ Every shared component exports a strict contract:                      │

│                                               │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ // Button component contract                                ││

│ │ interface ButtonProps {                                ││

│ │ // Required                                       ││

│ │ children: ReactNode;                                   ││

│ │ onPress: (e: PressEvent) => void; // Keyboard + mouse unified              ││

│ │                                             ││

│ │ // Optional                                      ││

│ │ variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary' | 'danger' | 'ghost'; │ │

│ │ size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';                            ││
│ │ isLoading?: boolean;                                 ││

│ │ isDisabled?: boolean;                                ││

│ │ leftIcon?: ReactNode;                                ││

│ │ rightIcon?: ReactNode;                               ││

│ │ accessibilityLabel?: string; // Override auto-generated label             ││

│ │                                           ││

│ │ // DOM passthrough                                   ││

│ │ id?: string;                                   ││

│ │ className?: string;                                 ││

│ │ 'data-testid'?: string;                             ││

│ │}                                          ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ CONTRACT ENFORCEMENT:                                           │

│ ────────────────────                                        │

│ • TypeScript strict props (no spreading unknown objects)                    │

│ • Runtime prop validation with Zod in development                       │

│ • Storybook stories for every variant combination                   │

│ • Unit tests for every state (including error and edge cases)           │

│ • Accessibility tests using jest-axe                        │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



IV.3 AI COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE
```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           AI COMPONENT ARCHITECTURE                              │

│                                             │

│ AI-specific components handle the unique patterns of AI-generated content: │

│                                             │

│ CONFIDENCE INDICATOR:                                        │

│ ────────────────────                                         │

│ Displays AI confidence score with colour, icon, and numeric value.               │

│ Props: score (0-1), breakdown?: ConfidenceBreakdown, showLabel?: boolean │

│ States: high (≥0.85, green), medium (0.60-0.84, amber), low (<0.60, red), │

│     calculating (pulsing, neutral), unavailable (grey, "N/A")        │

│ Interaction: Click opens ConfidenceBreakdown panel                       │

│ Accessibility: aria-label="Confidence score: 85 percent. High confidence." │

│                                             │

│ STREAMING CONTENT:                                           │

│ ────────────────                                         │

│ Renders AI-generated content as it streams from the server.                  │

│ Props: stream: ReadableStream, onComplete?: () => void                       │

│ States: connecting, streaming, complete, error                       │

│ Behaviour: Content appears word-by-word; cursor blinks during streaming;             │

│       scrolls smoothly to follow content; confidence updates inline │

│                                             │

│ AGENT AVATAR:                                        │
│ ────────────                                            │

│ Displays which AI agent performed an action.                            │

│ Props: agent: AgentIdentity, size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg', showStatus?: bool │

│ States: active (pulsing border), idle (static), error (red indicator),      │

│      offline (grey)                                 │

│ Interaction: Click opens Agent Detail panel; hover shows agent name + task │

│                                                │

│ AI SUGGESTION CARD:                                         │

│ ─────────────────                                           │

│ Inline suggestion from AI that user can accept, modify, or dismiss.             │

│ Props: suggestion: AISuggestion, onAccept, onModify, onDismiss                      │

│ Visual: Subtle blue border, glassmorphism background, confidence indicator │

│ Interaction: "Apply" (primary), "Edit" (secondary), "Ignore" (tertiary)         │

│ Accessibility: aria-live="polite" for new suggestions                   │

│                                                │

│ EXPLAINABILITY PANEL:                                       │

│ ────────────────────                                            │

│ Shows why the AI made a specific decision.                              │

│ Props: decision: AIDecision                                 │

│ Content: Agent reasoning trace, sources considered, confidence breakdown, │

│       alternatives evaluated, timestamp                             │

│ States: loading, complete, unavailable                              │

│                                                │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART V — STATE MANAGEMENT ARCHITECTURE



V.1 STATE CATEGORIES



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│          STATE MANAGEMENT ARCHITECTURE                               │

│                                            │

│ STATE CATEGORIES:                                     │

│ ────────────────                                       │

│                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ CATEGORY         EXAMPLES              SOLUTION               ││

│ │ ────────         ────────             ────────               ││

│ │                                          ││

│ │ LOCAL UI STATE     Modal open/close          useState              ││

│ │            Form input values     useReducer (complex)             ││

│ │            Dropdown selections        Component-scoped             ││

│ │                                          ││

│ │ GLOBAL UI STATE Theme (light/dark)            Zustand store            ││

│ │            Sidebar collapsed     (ui-store)             ││

│ │            Active workspace                        ││
│ │          User preferences                                ││

│ │                                               ││

│ │ SERVER STATE    Story data              TanStack Query                  ││

│ │          Agent list            (React Query)              ││

│ │          Analytics data          Cache + background sync │ │

│ │          Settings data                               ││

│ │                                               ││

│ │ REAL-TIME STATE Breaking news alerts               WebSocket → Zustand             ││

│ │          Agent activity feed       (realtime-store)                ││

│ │          Story state changes                              ││

│ │          Queue depth updates                                  ││

│ │                                               ││

│ │ WORKFLOW STATE        Story lifecycle state        Zustand + XState           ││

│ │          Publishing workflow         (complex workflows)                ││

│ │          Verification pipeline                           ││

│ │                                               ││

│ │ OFFLINE STATE   Queued actions                Zustand (offline-store) │ │

│ │          Cached data             + IndexedDB                   ││

│ │          Sync status                                ││

│ │                                               │

│ │ AUTH STATE      User session            NextAuth.js + Zustand            ││

│ │          Permissions             (auth-store)              ││

│ │          Workspace role                                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



V.2 STATE MANAGEMENT COMPARISON



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│         STATE MANAGEMENT SOLUTION COMPARISON                                     │

│                                                │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ SOLUTION        STRENGTHS           WEAKNESSES              USE CASE       ││

│ │ ────────        ─────────          ──────────             ────────     ││

│ │                                              ││

│ │ useState/      Zero dependencies     Not for shared         Local UI      ││

│ │ useReducer      Simple mental model state                 state      ││

│ │           Built-in         Re-renders tree                ││

│ │                                              ││

│ │ React Context Built-in           Performance issues Low-frequency │

│ │           Good for providers    with high-frequency updates            ││

│ │           (theme, auth)        updates            Theme, Auth │ │

│ │                                              ││

│ │ Zustand       Tiny (1KB)        Less ecosystem        Global UI │ │

│ │           Simple API         than Redux           state        ││

│ │           No providers needed Fewer devtools              Workflow     ││
│ │           Great performance                                ││

│ │                                                ││

│ │ Redux Toolkit Mature ecosystem             Larger bundle         (Not        ││

│ │           Powerful devtools       More boilerplate         selected) │ │

│ │           Middleware support          Overkill for this          ││

│ │                           architecture              ││

│ │                                                ││

│ │ TanStack Query Best-in-class caching Only for server             Server       ││

│ │ (React Query) Background refetch            state           state       ││

│ │           Mutations + cache       Not for client                ││

│ │           Devtools            state                   ││

│ │                                                ││

│ │ XState       Formal state machines Learning curve               Complex      ││

│ │           Visual editor        Heavy for simple       workflows │ │

│ │           Guaranteed correctness state                (Enterprise)│ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                  │

│ ENTERPRISE RECOMMENDATION: Zustand + TanStack Query + XState (Enterprise) │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │

│                                                  │

│ Zustand: All client-side global state (UI, workflow, offline, real-time)        │

│ TanStack Query: All server state (caching, refetching, mutations)                   │

│ XState: Complex workflow state machines (Enterprise phase)                          │

│                                                  │

│ WHY NOT REDUX:                                               │
│ • Zustand provides equivalent capability with 1/10th the boilerplate            │

│ • Modern React patterns (Server Components, streaming) reduce client state │

│ • TanStack Query handles the most complex state (server cache) better               │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



V.3 STORE ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              STORE ARCHITECTURE                             │

│ ├── connected: boolean                                          │
│ ├── activeStories: Map<StoryId, StoryState>                                     │

│ └── actions: subscribe(), unsubscribe()                             │

│                                               │

│ stores/workflow-store.ts                                    │

│ ├── activeWorkflows: Map<StoryId, WorkflowState>                                        │

│ ├── reviewQueue: ReviewItem[]                                           │

│ └── actions: transitionState(), approve(), reject()                         │

│                                               │

│ FEATURE STORES (Module-scoped, loaded lazily):                                      │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                                               │

│ modules/pipeline/stores/pipeline-store.ts         # Pipeline filters, selection │

│ modules/editorial/stores/editor-store.ts      # Editor state, drafts                    │

│ modules/breaking-news/stores/breaking-store.ts # Breaking news state                            │

│                                               │

│ TANSTACK QUERY (Server state):                                      │

│ ────────────────────────────                                                │

│ Query keys follow convention: [domain, ...params]                                   │

│ • ['story', storyId]                                   │

│ • ['stories', { status, priority, page }]                       │

│ • ['agents', { engine, status }]                            │

│ • ['analytics', 'audience', { period }]                         │

│ • ['workspace', workspaceId, 'settings']                            │

│                                               │

│ MUTATIONS:                                              │

│ • useCreateStory()       • useUpdateStory()       • usePublishStory()                   │
│ • useApproveStory()     • useRejectStory()       • useCorrectStory()        │

│ • useAssignAgent()     • useUpdatePrompt()        • useUpdateSettings()             │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



V.4 OPTIMISTIC UPDATES



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             OPTIMISTIC UPDATE STRATEGY                          │

│                                              │

│ Optimistic updates are critical for newsroom responsiveness. When a user                │

│ approves a story, the UI updates immediately — not after the server                 │

│ responds.                                          │

│                                              │

│ IMPLEMENTATION (TanStack Query Mutations):                              │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────                                     │

│                                              │

│ Pattern:                                          │

│ 1. onMutate: Immediately update cache (optimistic)                      │

│ 2. onError: Roll back cache to previous state                       │

│ 3. onSettled: Invalidate queries to ensure consistency                  │

│                                              │

│ OPTIMISTIC OPERATIONS:                                      │
│ ─────────────────────                                             │

│ • Story approval/rejection                                    │

│ • Story assignment                                        │

│ • Breaking news declaration                                       │

│ • Correction application                                      │

│ • Agent task assignment                                       │

│ • Notification dismissal                                  │

│ • User preference changes                                         │

│                                              │

│ ROLLBACK UX:                                          │

│ ───────────                                          │

│ • Toast notification: "Failed to approve story. Retrying..."                  │

│ • Revert UI to previous state                                 │

│ • Option to retry manually                                        │

│ • Error logged for debugging                                      │

│                                              │

│ OPTIMISTIC vs. CONFIRMED:                                             │

│ ─────────────────────────                                                 │

│ • Confirmed: Financial operations, user deletion, retractions                     │

│ • Optimistic: Content approval, assignments, preferences                          │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART VI — API INTEGRATION LAYER



VI.1 API CLIENT ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            API INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE                      │

│                                            │

│ LAYERED API ARCHITECTURE:                               │

│ ────────────────────────                                │

│                                            │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 1: HTTP CLIENT (services/api-client.ts)              ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────                   ││

│ │ • Base fetch wrapper                            ││

│ │ • Automatic auth token injection                      ││

│ │ • Request/response interceptors                       ││

│ │ • Error normalisation                           ││

│ │ • Retry logic (exponential backoff)                  ││

│ │ • Rate limit handling (429 → queue + retry)                ││

│ │ • Request deduplication                          ││

│ │ • Response caching (stale-while-revalidate)                ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
│                       │                      │

│                       ▼                          │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 2: DOMAIN SERVICES (services/*-service.ts)                       ││

│ │ ───────────────────────────────────────────────                              ││

│ │ • Typed API functions per domain                             ││

│ │ • Request/response type validation (Zod)                          ││

│ │ • Business logic error handling                          ││

│ │ • Cache tag management for revalidation                           ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ story-service.ts:                                  ││

│ │ getStory(id) → Story                                ││

│ │ listStories(filters) → PaginatedResponse<Story>                    ││

│ │ createStory(data) → Story                               ││

│ │ updateStory(id, data) → Story                            ││

│ │ approveStory(id) → Story                                ││

│

│                       │                      │

│                       ▼                          │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 3: TANSTACK QUERY HOOKS (hooks/use-*.ts)                          ││

│ │ • useQuery for reads                               ││

│ │ • useMutation for writes                            ││

VI.2 REAL-TIME COMMUNICATION



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           REAL-TIME COMMUNICATION ARCHITECTURE                            │

│                                            │

│ TRANSPORT HIERARCHY:                                     │

│ ──────────────────                                   │

│                                            │

│ PRIMARY: WebSocket (Full-duplex, persistent)                      │

│ ───────────────────────────────────────────                                   │

│ • Single authenticated WebSocket connection per client                │

│ • Multiplexed channels: story-updates, agent-events, notifications, system │
│ • Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff                                  │

│ • Heartbeat/ping for connection health                                 │

│ • Message acknowledgements for critical events                                     │

│                                              │

│ SECONDARY: Server-Sent Events (AI Streaming)                                       │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────────                                               │

│ • AI content generation streams (unidirectional)                               │

│ • Agent reasoning streams (explainability)                             │

│ • Native browser EventSource API                                   │

│ • Automatic reconnection built-in                              │

│                                              │

│ TERTIARY: Server Actions (Mutations)                                   │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────                                                  │

│ • Form submissions, quick actions                                  │

│ • Progressive enhancement (works without JavaScript)                                   │

│ • Built-in CSRF protection                                 │

│                                              │

│ WEBSOCKET CHANNELS:                                            │

│ ──────────────────                                         │

│ • story.{storyId}.state      → Story state changes (real-time pipeline) │

│ • story.{storyId}.confidence → Confidence score updates                                │

│ • agent.{agentId}.activity     → Individual agent events                       │

│ • agents.all              → Aggregate agent status                 │

│ • breaking.active           → Active breaking news events                      │

│ • notifications.user.{userId} → User notifications                         │

│ • system.health             → Platform health metrics                      │
│ • queue.review           → Human review queue updates                             │

│                                            │

│ IMPLEMENTATION:                                           │

│ ──────────────                                        │

│ • Custom useWebSocket hook wrapping native WebSocket                                  │

│ • Channel subscription management                                 │

│ • Automatic cleanup on component unmount                                      │

│ • Message buffering during disconnection                              │

│ • Zustand store integration for reactive UI updates                       │

│                                            │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

PART VII — AUTHENTICATION & SECURITY



VII.1 AUTHENTICATION ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           AUTHENTICATION ARCHITECTURE                                 │

│                                            │

│ AUTHENTICATION FLOW:                                          │

│ ──────────────────                                        │
│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LOGIN FLOW                                       ││

│ │ ─────────                                        ││

│ │                                            ││

│ │ User → Email/Password → Server validates →                                ││

│ │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │

│ │ │ MFA Required?                                  │ ││

│ │ │ ├── NO → JWT issued → Session created → Redirect to dashboard                      │ ││

│ │ │ └── YES → MFA challenge sent → User enters code →                           │ ││

│ │ │      JWT issued → Session created → Redirect to dashboard                   │ ││

│ │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ SESSION MANAGEMENT:                                         │

│ ──────────────────                                      │

│ • NextAuth.js v5 (Auth.js) for session management                           │

│ • JWT-based sessions (stateless, scalable)                          │

│ • Access token: 15-minute expiry                            │

│ • Refresh token: 7-day expiry, rotating                         │

│ • Automatic token refresh in API client interceptor                     │

│ • Session synchronisation across tabs (BroadcastChannel)                        │

│ • Forced logout on security events (server push)                        │

│                                              │
│ RBAC (ROLE-BASED ACCESS CONTROL):                                      │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ • Roles: EIC, ManagingEditor, ContentEditor, PlatformAdmin, Viewer                     │

│ • Permissions: Granular, composable                            │

│ • Frontend: usePermission() hook for conditional rendering                         │

│ • Route protection: Middleware checks workspace role                               │

│ • API protection: Backend validates (never trust client)                   │

│                                             │

│ ENTERPRISE SSO (Growth/Enterprise):                                │

│ ──────────────────────────────────                                             │

│ • SAML 2.0 and OIDC support                                │

│ • Multi-tenant IdP configuration                           │

│ • Just-in-time user provisioning                           │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



VII.2 SECURITY ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            FRONTEND SECURITY ARCHITECTURE                                  │

│                                             │

│ DEFENCE LAYERS:                                      │

│ ──────────────                                       │
│                                              │

│ LAYER 1: CONTENT SECURITY POLICY (CSP)                                    │

│ • Strict CSP headers configured in next.config.ts                     │

│ • No inline scripts (nonce-based for necessary exceptions)                        │

│ • No 'unsafe-eval'                                    │

│ • Script sources whitelisted                              │

│ • Report-only mode during development                                 │

│                                              │

│ LAYER 2: XSS PREVENTION                                       │

│ • React's built-in XSS protection (JSX escaping)                      │

│ • dangerouslySetInnerHTML: banned (use sanitisation utility if essential) │

│ • DOMPurify for any HTML rendering (AI content previews)                              │

│ • Input validation on all user inputs (Zod schemas)                       │

│                                              │

│ LAYER 3: CSRF PROTECTION                                      │

│ • Next.js Server Actions: Built-in CSRF protection                    │

│ • API routes: SameSite=Strict cookies                             │

│ • Custom fetch: CSRF token header for mutations                               │

│                                              │

│ LAYER 4: SECURE HEADERS                                       │

│ • Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)                            │

│ • X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff                                 │

│ • X-Frame-Options: DENY (allow for previews if needed)                            │

│ • Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin                    │

│ • Permissions-Policy: restrictive defaults                        │

│                                              │
│ LAYER 5: SECURE STORAGE                                        │

│ • Tokens: httpOnly cookies (never localStorage)                            │

│ • User preferences: localStorage (non-sensitive)                           │

│ • Offline drafts: IndexedDB (encrypted if sensitive)                       │

│ • Session data: In-memory only                                 │

│                                             │

│ LAYER 6: AUDIT LOGGING                                     │

│ • All sensitive actions logged (frontend → backend)                            │

│ • Log: user, action, resource, timestamp, IP, user agent                       │

│ • Audit log viewer in Governance section                               │

│ • Tamper-evident log integrity                             │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

│ The newsroom does not stop because the network did. The offline                        │

│ • Draft editing (queued for sync)                                  │

│                                            │

│ GROWTH:                                            │

│ • Full editorial workflows offline                             │

│ • Breaking news alerts (via Push API)                                  │

│ • Offline publishing queue                                 │

│ • Conflict resolution UI                               │

│                                            │

│ ENTERPRISE:                                        │

│ • Near-full newsroom operation offline                                     │

│ • Multi-device sync                                    │

VIII.2 SERVICE WORKER ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           SERVICE WORKER ARCHITECTURE                                       │

│                                               │

│ CACHE STRATEGY (per resource type):                                     │

│ ───────────────────────────────────                                              │

│                                               │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RESOURCE             STRATEGY             MAX AGE         MAX ITEMS │ │

│ │ ────────            ────────             ───────         ───────── │ │

│ │ App Shell (HTML/CSS) Cache-First                7 days      50            ││

│ │ JavaScript bundles Cache-First (versioned) 30 days               100               ││

│ │ Fonts             Cache-First          365 days     20           ││

│ │ Images (UI)         Cache-First          30 days      500         ││

│ │ Images (Content)       Network-First         7 days        1000               ││

│ │ API (Stories)       Network-First         1 hour         500          ││

│ │ API (Agents)        Network-First         5 minutes 100                   ││

│ │ API (Analytics)      Network-First         1 hour        200          ││
│ │ API (Settings)    Stale-While-Revalidate 1 day         50     ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                            │

│ BACKGROUND SYNC:                                            │

│ ──────────────                                      │

│ • Sync API for queued actions (publish, approve, correct)               │

│ • Periodic background sync for content updates                      │

│ • Sync status indicator in UI                            │

│ • Conflict resolution when server state diverges                    │

│                                            │

│ PUSH NOTIFICATIONS:                                         │

│ ──────────────────                                          │

│ • Breaking news alerts                               │

│ • Human review required                                     │

│ • Corrections needed                                    │

│ • System health alerts                               │

│                                            │

─┘

VIII.3 OFFLINE SYNC ARCHITECTURE



```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│            OFFLINE SYNC ARCHITECTURE                                    │

│                                             │

│ SYNC QUEUE:                                             │

│ ──────────                                          │

│                                             │

│ 1. USER PERFORMS ACTION (while offline)                                     │

│   • UI updates optimistically                               │

│   • Action added to sync queue (IndexedDB)                                  │

│   • Sync status: "pending"                                  │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 2. CONNECTIVITY RESTORED                                            │

│   • Service Worker detects online event                                 │

│   • Sync queue processing begins                                │

│   • Actions processed in FIFO order (with priority overrides)                   │

│    │                                        │

│    ▼                                            │

│ 3. ACTION EXECUTED                                          │

│   ├── SUCCESS: Action removed from queue; UI confirms                               │

│   └── CONFLICT: Server state differs from optimistic update                     │

│        │                                    │

│        ▼                                        │

│ 4. CONFLICT RESOLUTION                                          │

│   • User notified of conflict                               │
│     • Side-by-side comparison: Local vs. Server                 │

│     • User chooses: Accept Server, Keep Local, Merge                    │

│     • Resolution applied; action removed from queue                     │

│                                              │

│ CONFLICT DETECTION:                                     │

│ ──────────────────                                      │

│ • Version vectors (client version vs. server version)               │

│ • Last-write-wins for simple data                           │

│ • Three-way merge for content (base, local, server)                 │

│ • Conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) for real-time collaboration │

│ (Enterprise — story co-editing)                             │

│                                              │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

│                                              │

│ BLUE-GREEN DEPLOYMENT (Zero-downtime):                            │

│ ──────────────────────────────────────                                │

│ 1. Deploy new version to inactive slot (blue/green)           │

│ 2. Run health checks against inactive slot                │
│ 3. Run smoke tests (critical user journeys)                             │

│ 4. Switch traffic to new slot (gradual: 10% → 50% → 100%)                           │

│ 5. Monitor error rates, performance, user metrics                           │

│ 6. If issues: Instant rollback to previous slot                     │

│ 7. If stable: Previous slot becomes inactive (ready for next deploy)                    │

│                                               │

│ ROLLBACK STRATEGY:                                      │

│ ────────────────                                       │

│ • Instant rollback via traffic switch (< 1 minute)                      │

│ • Database: Backward-compatible migrations (expand-contract pattern)                            │

│ • Static assets: Versioned, immutable, CDN-cached                               │

│ • Feature flags: Disable problematic features without rollback                          │

│                                               │

│ FEATURE FLAGS (LaunchDarkly / Custom):                                      │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                                │

│ • All new features behind flags                             │

│ • Kill switches for critical functionality                  │

│ • Percentage rollouts (0% → 10% → 50% → 100%)                                       │

│ • Targetable by: user, workspace, region, random percentage                                 │

│ • A/B experiment support                                    │

│                                               │

│ MONITORING (Production):                                    │

│ ───────────────────────                                         │

│ • Real-time error rate dashboard                                │

│ • Core Web Vitals trend dashboard                                   │

│ • API latency and error rate dashboard                              │
│ • User-facing performance dashboard                               │

│ • Alert thresholds: Error rate spike, latency degradation,                    │

│ feature flag anomaly, security event                          │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```



XII.2 FRONTEND ADRs



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│           FRONTEND ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS                                      │

│                                             │

│ ADR-FE-001: Next.js App Router as Foundation                              │

│ Decision: Use Next.js 15 App Router exclusively                       │

│ Rationale: Server Components reduce client JS; streaming enables AI content; │

│       built-in optimisations reduce engineering burden                    │

│                                             │

│ ADR-FE-002: Zustand over Redux for Client State                           │

│ Decision: Zustand for all client-side global state management                         │

│ Rationale: Minimal boilerplate, excellent TypeScript support, tiny bundle, │

│       no provider wrapping required                          │

│                                             │

│ ADR-FE-003: TanStack Query for Server State                           │

│ Decision: TanStack Query (React Query) for all server state                       │
│ Rationale: Best-in-class caching, background refetch, optimistic updates, │

│       devtools; handles the hardest state management problem                   │

│                                               │

│ ADR-FE-004: Feature-Based Module Organisation                              │

│ Decision: Organise codebase by feature modules, not technical layers                   │

│ Rationale: Enables independent development, testing, and deployment;                           │

│       reduces coupling; improves discoverability               │

│                                               │

│ ADR-FE-005: WebSocket for Real-Time, SSE for AI Streaming                      │

│ Decision: WebSocket for bidirectional real-time; SSE for AI streaming              │

│ Rationale: WebSocket provides full-duplex for dashboards; SSE is simpler                   │

│       for unidirectional AI content streams                │

│                                               │

│ ADR-FE-006: Offline-First with Background Sync                         │

│ Decision: Critical workflows function offline with background sync                 │

│ Rationale: Newsroom operations cannot stop for network issues; queued                          │

│       actions with conflict resolution provide seamless experience             │

│                                               │

│ ADR-FE-007: Streaming AI Content Display                           │

│ Decision: AI content streams progressively (word-by-word rendering)                    │

│ Rationale: Reduces perceived latency; provides early preview; communicates │

│       AI activity; allows early abort if quality is poor       │

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```
XII.3 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY



Volume 8 of the Agbofa Nexus AI enterprise architecture defines the complete frontend
engineering implementation blueprint. Where Volume 7 specified what the frontend experience
should be, Volume 8 specifies how it is engineered, organised, managed, and deployed.



Key Architectural Decisions:



1. Next.js 15 App Router as the foundational framework, leveraging React Server Components
as the default rendering strategy, with Client Components reserved for interactive elements.
This maximises performance, SEO, and developer experience while supporting the unique
requirements of an AI-native application — streaming content, real-time updates, and
progressive disclosure.

2. Feature-based module architecture that organises the codebase around business capabilities
(dashboard, pipeline, editorial, publishing, agents) rather than technical layers. Each module
owns its components, hooks, stores, services, and types. This enables independent
development and testing while maintaining clear boundaries.

3. Zustand + TanStack Query as the state management architecture. Zustand handles client-side
global state (UI, workflow, offline, real-time) with minimal boilerplate. TanStack Query handles
all server state with best-in-class caching, background refetching, and optimistic updates. XState
is reserved for complex workflow state machines in the Enterprise phase.

4. Layered API architecture with a base HTTP client providing authentication, retry logic, rate
limiting, and error normalisation; typed domain services providing business-logic API functions;
and TanStack Query hooks providing reactive data fetching with cache management.

5. Offline-first architecture using Service Workers for asset caching, IndexedDB for data
persistence, and a sync queue for offline actions. Critical workflows — story review, draft
editing, approval — function without connectivity, queuing actions for synchronisation when
the network returns.

6. Real-time by default using WebSocket connections for bidirectional communication (story
state changes, agent events, notifications) and Server-Sent Events for unidirectional AI content
streaming. The real-time store integrates with Zustand for reactive UI updates.
7. Comprehensive testing strategy spanning static analysis, unit tests, component tests,
integration tests, E2E tests, visual regression tests, accessibility audits, and performance budget
enforcement — all integrated into the CI/CD pipeline.

8. Blue-green deployment with feature flags, percentage rollouts, instant rollback capability, and
comprehensive production monitoring — ensuring the newsroom platform meets enterprise
reliability standards.



The Engineering Reality:



When implemented, the Agbofa Nexus AI frontend will be a high-performance, real-time,
offline-capable, AI-native application that delivers the Mission Control experience defined in
Volume 7. It will be built on a foundation of type safety, component isolation, and
comprehensive testing. It will deploy with zero downtime and degrade gracefully under adverse
conditions. It will be observable — every error, every performance regression, every user
interaction captured and actionable.



This volume, together with Volumes 1–7, provides the complete blueprint for building the
world's leading autonomous AI media company platform — from executive vision through AI
architecture, user experience, and frontend engineering implementation.

PART I — ENTERPRISE CLOUD STRATEGY



I.1 CLOUD VISION



Agbofa Nexus AI is not merely hosted in the cloud. It is architected as a cloud-native, globally
distributed, AI-optimised platform that can operate from a single virtual machine serving a
proof-of-concept newsroom to a multi-region Kubernetes fleet powering hundreds of
autonomous newsrooms across six continents.



The cloud vision rests on four pillars:



1. Progressive Infrastructure — The platform's infrastructure evolves with its business. MVP
runs on minimal, cost-optimised resources. Growth adds managed services and
containerisation. Enterprise achieves global distribution, multi-tenancy, and five-nines
availability. Each phase is a complete, functional deployment — not a partial implementation
awaiting future investment.

2. AI-Optimised Compute — The platform's workload is AI-heavy. Infrastructure decisions
prioritise GPU availability, model serving latency, vector database performance, and streaming
data throughput. Traditional web-hosting assumptions do not apply.

3. Vendor Awareness, Not Vendor Lock-in — The platform uses cloud-native services where they
provide clear advantage, but all critical paths have defined escape hatches. The Multi-LLM
Abstraction Layer extends to infrastructure: the platform can migrate between cloud providers
without architectural redesign.
4. Zero-Trust by Default — No component trusts any other component by default. Every service-
to-service communication is authenticated and encrypted. Every API call is authorised. Every
network boundary is defined and enforced. Security is not a perimeter — it is a property of
every component.



I.2 CLOUD PRINCIPLES



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│              CLOUD ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLES                         │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 1: INFRASTRUCTURE AS CODE (IaC)                              │

│ ─────────────────────────────────────────                                          │

│ Every infrastructure resource is defined in code (Terraform/Pulumi).                   │

│ No manual console changes. Infrastructure changes follow the same CI/CD                        │

│ pipeline as application changes. What is in version control is what exists. │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 2: IMMUTABLE INFRASTRUCTURE                                      │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                       │

│ Servers are never patched — they are replaced. New AMIs/container images │

│ are built, tested, and deployed. Running instances are never modified.                     │

│ This eliminates configuration drift and ensures reproducibility.               │

│                                             │

│ PRINCIPLE 3: HORIZONTAL SCALABILITY                                │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                      │

│ Every component scales horizontally by adding instances, not vertically                    │
│ by upgrading hardware. The platform is designed for distributed operation │

│ from day one — even if MVP runs on a single node.                            │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 4: DEFENCE IN DEPTH                                   │

│ ───────────────────────────                                          │

│ Security is layered. Network controls, identity management, encryption,                      │

│ application security, and monitoring each provide independent protection. │

│ Compromise of one layer does not compromise the platform.                                │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 5: OBSERVABILITY AS INFRASTRUCTURE                                     │

│ ────────────────────────────────────────                                             │

│ Logging, metrics, and tracing are not features — they are infrastructure                     │

│ services provisioned alongside compute and storage. Every component emits │

│ telemetry. Every deployment includes observability configuration.                        │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 6: COST-AWARE ARCHITECTURE                                      │

│ ────────────────────────────────────                                             │

│ Cost is a first-class architectural constraint. Every service selection          │

│ includes cost analysis. Auto-scaling is configured with cost boundaries.                 │

│ Idle resources are eliminated automatically. FinOps is operational,                  │

│ not retrospective.                                     │

│                                               │

│ PRINCIPLE 7: FAILURE IS EXPECTED                                 │

│ ───────────────────────────────                                          │

│ Every component is designed for failure. Retries, circuit breakers,                  │

│ graceful degradation, and automated recovery are not add-ons — they are                          │
│ fundamental to the architecture. Chaos engineering validates assumptions. │

│                                           │

│ PRINCIPLE 8: REGIONAL SOVEREIGNTY                               │

│ ─────────────────────────────────                                   │

│ Data residency requirements are respected by design. The platform can       │

│ deploy in any region with local data storage. Multi-region deployments      │

│ respect data sovereignty boundaries.                       │

│                                           │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

│ │ WebSocket       t3.medium+        HPA (Conn)    Real-time connections │ │

│ │ Background Workers t3.small+        HPA (Queue) Async processing          ││

│ │ System        t3.small+      Fixed (3)   Monitoring, logging │ │
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                               │

│ AUTO-SCALING CONFIGURATION:                                            │

│ ──────────────────────────                                         │

│ • Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) for all stateless services                       │

│ • Cluster Autoscaler for node group scaling                            │

│ • KEDA (Kubernetes Event-Driven Autoscaling) for queue-based scaling                               │

│ • Predictive scaling based on historical patterns (Enterprise)                         │

│ • Minimum replicas: 2 (production), 1 (staging/dev)                                │

│ • Maximum replicas: Configurable per service with cost caps                                │

│                                               │

│ GPU WORKLOAD MANAGEMENT:                                                   │

│ ───────────────────────                                        │

│ • Dedicated GPU node group with NVIDIA device plugin                                       │

│ • GPU time-slicing for multiple inference tasks per GPU                            │

│ • Spot instances for non-critical GPU workloads (80% cost savings)                             │

│ • On-demand fallback when spot unavailable                                     │

│ • GPU workload priority: Breaking news > Standard content > Batch processing│

│                                               │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

IV.2 CONTAINER STANDARDS



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             CONTAINER STANDARDS                                │

│                                              │

│ IMAGE STANDARDS:                                       │
│ ──────────────                                         │

│ • Base image: Distroless or Alpine (minimal attack surface)                        │

│ • Multi-stage builds (build dependencies not in final image)                       │

│ • Non-root user (SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot: true)                              │

│ • Read-only root filesystem where possible                                 │

│ • Image scanning in CI (Trivy or AWS ECR scanning)                             │

│ • Images tagged with git SHA and semantic version                              │

│ • No 'latest' tag in production                                │

│                                             │

│ RESOURCE MANAGEMENT:                                                   │

│ ──────────────────                                         │

│ • Every container has: requests and limits (CPU, memory)                               │

│ • Quality of Service: Guaranteed (critical), Burstable (standard)                  │

│ • LimitRange and ResourceQuota per namespace                                       │

│ • HPA configured with min/max replicas                                     │

│ • Pod Disruption Budgets for critical services                             │

│                                              │

│ SECURITY CONTEXT:                                          │

│ ────────────────                                           │

│ • privileged: false                                │

│ • allowPrivilegeEscalation: false                                  │

│ • readOnlyRootFilesystem: true (where possible)                                │

│ • runAsNonRoot: true                                       │

│ • seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault                                       │

│ • capabilities: drop ALL                               │

│                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

PART VI — ENTERPRISE SECURITY



VI.1 ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURE



```

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┐

│             ZERO TRUST ARCHITECTURE                               │

│                                               │
│ PRINCIPLES:                                        │

│ ─────────                                         │

│ • Never trust, always verify                                   │

│ • Least privilege access                                   │

│ • Assume breach                                            │

│ • Verify explicitly                                    │

│                                              │

│ IMPLEMENTATION LAYERS:                                             │

│ ─────────────────────                                           │

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 1: IDENTITY (AWS IAM + Cognito/Auth0)                                ││

│ │ ────────────────────────────────────────────                                         ││

│ │ • IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) for Kubernetes pods                     ││

│ │ • No long-lived credentials                                  ││

│ │ • MFA enforced for all human users                                   ││

│ │ • Just-in-time access for elevated privileges                         ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                              │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 2: NETWORK                                             ││

│ │ ──────────────                                           ││

│ │ • Security Groups: Least privilege, service-specific                      ││

│ │ • Network Policies (Kubernetes): Pod-to-pod micro-segmentation                       ││
│ │ • Private subnets for all workloads                        ││

│ │ • VPC endpoints for AWS services (no internet traversal)                  ││

│ │ • NAT Gateways for controlled egress                            ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 3: TRANSPORT (mTLS)                                  ││

│ │ ─────────────────────────                                   ││

│ │ • TLS 1.3 minimum for all external traffic                  ││

│ │ • mTLS between all internal services (Istio)                    ││

│ │ • Certificate management via cert-manager + AWS ACM                        ││

│ │ • Automatic certificate rotation                       ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 4: APPLICATION                                 ││

│ │ ───────────────────                                    ││

│ │ • API authentication: JWT with short expiry                      ││

│ │ • API authorisation: RBAC per endpoint                          ││

│ │ • Rate limiting per user/tenant/IP                         ││

│ │ • Input validation on all endpoints                        ││

│ │ • CSP headers, XSS protection (see Volume 8)                         ││
│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ LAYER 5: DATA                                     ││

│ │ ─────────────                                          ││

│ │ • Encryption at rest: All databases, S3, EBS volumes              ││

│ │ • Encryption in transit: TLS everywhere                      ││

│ │ • Envelope encryption: KMS for key management                      ││

│ │ • Key rotation: Automatic (AWS KMS)                          ││

│ │ • Database encryption: AES-256                              ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘

```

│ ──────────────                                               │

│                                                   │

│ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│

│ │ RESOURCE           METHOD              FREQUENCY RETENTION                        ││

│ │ ────────          ──────            ───────── ─────────                      ││

│ │ Aurora (SQL)       Automated snapshots Every 6 hrs 30 days (rolling) │ │

│ │ Neo4j          Native backups        Daily       90 days               ││

│ │ DynamoDB           Point-in-time       Continuous 35 days                    ││

│ │ S3           Cross-region repl. Continuous Policy-based                     ││

│ │ EKS Config        etcd snapshots       Daily        90 days             ││

│ │ Terraform State      Versioned in S3     Per-apply All versions               ││

│ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│

│                                                   │
│ DISASTER RECOVERY SCENARIOS:                                     │

│ ──────────────────────────                                       │

│                                             │

│ SCENARIO 1: SINGLE AZ FAILURE                                │

│ • Automatic: Multi-AZ services fail over within RTO                          │

│ • Impact: None (designed for this)                           │

│                                             │

│ SCENARIO 2: SINGLE REGION FAILURE                                    │

│ • DNS failover to DR region (Route 53 health checks)                         │

│ • Aurora Global Database promoted to primary                                 │

│ • DynamoDB Global Tables: automatic                                  │

│ • EKS: Deploy from Terraform in DR region                            │

│ • Traffic shifted via Route 53 or Global Accelerator                     │

│                                             │

│ SCENARIO 3: DATA CORRUPTION                                      │

│ • Point-in-time recovery from Aurora backups                             │

│ • DynamoDB point-in-time restore                                 │

│ • S3 versioning for object recovery                          │

│                                             │

│ SCENARIO 4: AI PROVIDER OUTAGE                                       │

│ • Multi-LLM Abstraction Layer routes to alternative provider                         │

│ • Self-hosted models (Llama/Mistral) activated as fallback                       │

│ • Quality may degrade; operations continue                               │

│                                             │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
─┘
```
