5.1 Zero Trust Architecture



```yaml

zero_trust:

 identity:
 provider: SPIFFE/SPIRE

 spiffe_trust_domain: agbofa-nexus.internal

 node_attestation: AWS IID



 workload_identity:

  format: "spiffe://agbofa-nexus.internal/ns/{{.Namespace}}/sa/{{.ServiceAccount}}"

  automatic_rotation: true

  rotation_interval: 1h



authentication:

 user_to_service:

  protocol: OAuth 2.0 + OIDC

  provider: Auth0 Enterprise

  token_type: JWT (RS256)

  token_lifetime: 15 minutes

  refresh_token_lifetime: 7 days



 service_to_service:

  protocol: mTLS (SPIFFE)

  min_tls_version: "1.3"

  cipher_suites:

   - TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

   - TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256



authorization:

 policy_engine: Open Policy Agent (OPA)
policy_distribution: OPA Bundles via S3



default_policy: DENY # Zero trust — deny by default



policies:

 - name: service_to_service

  description: Allow only authorized service-to-service communication

  rego: |

   package agbofa.authz

   default allow = false

   allow {

       input.source.namespace == "content-factory"

       input.destination.namespace == "distribution"

       input.destination.path == "/publish"

   }



 - name: tenant_isolation

  description: Ensure tenant-level data isolation

  rego: |

   package agbofa.authz

   allow {

       input.source.tenant_id == input.destination.tenant_id

   }



network:

segmentation:
       vpc: private subnets only for workloads

       service_mesh: Istio Ambient (L4 + L7)

       network_policies:

        default_deny: true

        allowed_egress:

         - monitoring namespace

         - vault namespace

         - external: AWS APIs only via VPC endpoints



      api_gateway:

       waf: AWS WAF with managed rules

       ddos_protection: AWS Shield Advanced

       rate_limiting: Per-IP, per-tenant, per-endpoint

```

  oplog: 7 days

       - ephemeral_volumes

6.2 Disaster Recovery Plan



```yaml

disaster_recovery:

 rpo_targets:

      postgresql: 5 minutes

      neo4j: 1 hour

      mongodb: 15 minutes
 kafka: 5 minutes (cross-region mirroring)

 redis: 24 hours (cache — acceptable to lose)

 clickhouse: 1 hour (replayable from Kafka)



rto_targets:

 total_platform: 1 hour

 critical_services: 15 minutes

 breaking_news_capability: 5 minutes (failover to secondary region)



scenarios:

 single_az_failure:

  impact: None (HA across 3 AZs)

  action: Automatic failover

  notification: Info only



 single_region_failure:

  impact: Service degradation for that region

  rto: 15 minutes (DNS failover to healthy region)

  action:

   - Route 53 health check detects failure

   - DNS weighted routing shifts traffic

   - Aurora promotes secondary region to primary

   - Neo4j read replicas promoted

   - Services scale up in healthy region

  notification: PagerDuty SEV1
complete_platform_outage:

 impact: Full platform unavailable

 rto: 1 hour

 action:

  - Incident commander declared

  - War room activated

  - Restore from latest backups in new region

  - Infrastructure provisioned via Terraform

  - Data restored in priority order:

   1. PostgreSQL (user data, source registry)

   2. Kafka (event streaming)

   3. Neo4j (story graph)

   4. MongoDB (content drafts)

   5. ClickHouse (analytics — replayable)

notification: PagerDuty SEV1 + Executive escalation



ransomware_attack:

 impact: Potential data corruption

 rto: 4 hours

 action:

  - ISOLATE affected systems immediately

  - Activate clean-room recovery environment

  - Restore from last known good backups

  - Validate backup integrity before restore

  - Engage incident response team

  - Notify legal and compliance
       notification: PagerDuty SEV1 + CISO + Legal



      data_corruption:

       impact: Partial data loss

       rto: 2 hours

       action:

        - Identify corruption scope

        - Point-in-time recovery for PostgreSQL

        - Replay Kafka events to rebuild state

        - Validate data integrity

       notification: PagerDuty SEV1



 recovery_testing:

      frequency:

       tabletop_exercise: quarterly

       az_failover_test: monthly

       region_failover_test: quarterly

       full_recovery_test: annually



      success_criteria:

       rto_met: yes/no

       rpo_met: yes/no

       data_integrity_validated: yes/no

       all_critical_services_operational: yes/no

```

PART X — ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS



```markdown

## ADR-OPS-001: Multi-Region Active-Active
**Decision:** Three-region active-active deployment

**Rationale:** 99.99% availability, data sovereignty, global audience

**Consequences:** Higher cost, replication complexity



## ADR-OPS-002: Istio Ambient Mesh

**Decision:** Istio Ambient (sidecar-less) for service mesh

**Rationale:** 40-60% resource savings vs sidecar model

**Consequences:** Requires K8s 1.29+, newer technology



## ADR-OPS-003: GitOps with Flux CD

**Decision:** Flux CD for continuous delivery

**Rationale:** GitOps audit trail, disaster recovery, rollback

**Consequences:** Git discipline required



## ADR-OPS-004: Tiered Storage Lifecycle

**Decision:** Automatic data tiering (Kafka → S3 → Glacier)

**Rationale:** 60-70% storage cost reduction

**Consequences:** Complex lifecycle management



## ADR-OPS-005: OpenTelemetry for Observability

**Decision:** OpenTelemetry as single observability framework

**Rationale:** Vendor-neutral, CNCF standard, unified collection

**Consequences:** Migration from existing tools if any



## ADR-OPS-006: SPIFFE/SPIRE for Workload Identity

**Decision:** SPIFFE/SPIRE for service identity in Zero Trust
**Rationale:** Cryptographically verifiable identity, automatic rotation

**Consequences:** Additional infrastructure component



## ADR-OPS-007: Aurora Global Database for PostgreSQL

**Decision:** AWS Aurora Global Database for primary relational store

**Rationale:** <1s replication lag, <60s cross-region failover

**Consequences:** AWS lock-in, but best-in-class for PostgreSQL



## ADR-OPS-008: Canary Deployments with Argo Rollouts

**Decision:** Progressive canary deployments with automated analysis

**Rationale:** Reduced blast radius, automated rollback on metric deviation

**Consequences:** More complex deployment configuration



## ADR-OPS-009: FinOps with Automated Optimization

**Decision:** Implement FinOps framework with automated cost optimization

**Rationale:** AI workloads highly variable; manual optimization insufficient

**Consequences:** Initial setup investment, significant ongoing savings



## ADR-OPS-010: Immutable Infrastructure

**Decision:** All infrastructure changes through Terraform; no manual changes

**Rationale:** Reproducibility, disaster recovery, audit compliance

**Consequences:** Slower emergency changes, but essential for reliability

```

ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORDS (ADR)



ADR-ENG-001: Monorepo with Domain-Based Structure



Decision: Single monorepo with domain-based directory structure, shared libraries, and
independent service deployment.
Rationale: 60+ microservices require shared types, protobuf definitions, and utilities. Monorepo
enables atomic changes across services, consistent versioning, and simplified dependency
management.

Alternatives Considered: Polyrepo per service (rejected — coordination overhead too high for
60+ services); hybrid with shared libraries as separate repos (rejected — versioning complexity).

Consequences: Larger clone size, but tooling (Bazel/Nx) mitigates build impact.



ADR-ENG-002: Trunk-Based Development with Short-Lived Feature Branches



Decision: Trunk-based development on main branch. Feature branches live maximum 2 days.
Release branches created for production stabilization only.

Rationale: AI-assisted development generates code rapidly. Long-lived branches create merge
conflicts with AI-generated code. Trunk-based development ensures continuous integration.

Alternatives Considered: GitFlow (rejected — too heavyweight for rapid AI development);
GitHub Flow (adopted with modifications).

Consequences: Requires high test coverage and feature flags for incomplete features.



ADR-ENG-003: AI-First Development Workflow



Decision: AI coding agents are first-class contributors. All AI-generated code must pass same CI
checks as human code. AI pull requests follow identical review process.

Rationale: Platform designed for AI-assisted development. Formalizing AI contribution workflow
ensures quality and auditability.

Consequences: CI must handle higher PR volume; review process must be efficient.



ADR-ENG-004: Contract-First API Development



Decision: All services define APIs in Protobuf/OpenAPI before implementation. API contracts are
reviewed and approved before coding begins.
Rationale: 60+ services require clear contracts. Contract-first prevents integration issues and
enables parallel development.

Consequences: Upfront API design effort, but significant reduction in integration issues.

1.1 Engineering Philosophy

AGBOFA NEXUS AI — ENGINEERING PHILOSOPHY:

1.2 Domain-Driven Development Standards



```yaml

ddd_standards:

 bounded_contexts:

      naming: PascalCase, matches Volume names

      examples:

       - ContentOrigination

       - TruthEngine

       - ContentFactory

       - ComplianceGatekeeper

       - DistributionEngine



      directory_convention: |

       domain/{bounded-context}/

        ├── api/          # Protobuf/OpenAPI definitions

        ├── cmd/           # Service entry points

        ├── internal/

        │ ├── domain/ # Domain models, aggregates, value objects

        │ ├── application/ # Use cases, application services

        │ ├── infrastructure/ # Database, messaging, external APIs

        │ └── interfaces/ # gRPC/REST handlers

        ├── pkg/          # Public shared packages

        └── test/       # Integration and contract tests
ubiquitous_language:

 enforcement: Code must use domain terms from Volumes 11-19

 prohibited: Generic terms like "data", "info", "process", "handle"

 examples:

  correct: "VerifyClaim", "PublishStory", "LockFacts"

  incorrect: "ProcessData", "HandleRequest", "DoStuff"



aggregate_design:

 rules:

  - One aggregate root per transaction boundary

  - Reference other aggregates by ID only

  - Eventual consistency across aggregates

  - Domain events for cross-aggregate communication



 example: |

  // CORRECT: Aggregate root with ID references

  type Story struct {

      ID       string      // Aggregate root

      Claims     []Claim      // Part of aggregate

      Sources     []SourceRef // Reference by ID

      AuthorID string         // Reference by ID

  }



  // INCORRECT: Direct object references

  type Story struct {
            Author Author        // DO NOT DO THIS

       }

```



1.3 Clean Architecture Rules



```yaml

clean_architecture:

 layer_dependencies:

      rule: Dependencies point inward. Outer layers depend on inner layers.



      layers:

       domain:

           description: Enterprise business rules

           dependencies: NONE (pure Go/Python)

           contains: Entities, Value Objects, Domain Services, Repository Interfaces

           rules:

            - No framework imports

            - No database imports

            - No HTTP/gRPC imports

            - Pure business logic only



       application:

           description: Application use cases

           dependencies: domain

           contains: Use Cases, Application Services, DTOs, Ports
   rules:

    - Orchestrates domain objects

    - Implements application-specific logic

    - No infrastructure concerns



  infrastructure:

   description: Technical implementations

   dependencies: domain, application

   contains: Repository implementations, API clients, Message brokers

   rules:

    - Implements interfaces defined in inner layers

    - Contains all framework-specific code

    - Database queries, HTTP clients, etc.



  interfaces:

   description: External APIs

   dependencies: application, infrastructure

   contains: gRPC handlers, HTTP handlers, Event consumers

   rules:

    - Thin layer, delegates to application services

    - Request/Response mapping only

    - Authentication/Authorization enforcement



dependency_injection:

 tool: Uber FX (Go), dependency-injector (Python)

 pattern: Constructor injection
      anti_pattern: Service locator, global state

```



1.4 Twelve-Factor Application Standards



```yaml

twelve_factor_compliance:

 factor_1_codebase:

      rule: One codebase per service, tracked in monorepo

      compliance:      Monorepo with domain-based structure



 factor_2_dependencies:

      rule: Explicitly declare and isolate dependencies

      go: go.mod with version pinning

      python: pyproject.toml with locked dependencies

      container: All dependencies in container image

      anti_pattern: System-level dependencies assumed



 factor_3_config:

      rule: Store config in environment variables

      implementation: |

       # CORRECT

       DB_HOST=${DB_HOST}

       KAFKA_BROKERS=${KAFKA_BROKERS}



       # INCORRECT
  DB_HOST=localhost # Hardcoded

 config_sources:

  - Environment variables (Kubernetes ConfigMap/Secrets)

  - HashiCorp Vault (secrets only)

  - Never: Config files in repository



factor_4_backing_services:

 rule: Treat backing services as attached resources

 implementation: Connection strings from environment

 services: PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB, Redis, Kafka, S3



factor_5_build_release_run:

 rule: Strictly separate build and run stages

 pipeline: Build → Test → Containerize → Deploy

 immutable: Container images never modified after build



factor_6_processes:

 rule: Execute as stateless processes

 state: All state in backing services (databases, caches)

 sticky_sessions: Never



factor_7_port_binding:

 rule: Export services via port binding

 implementation: Services bind to $PORT environment variable



factor_8_concurrency:
      rule: Scale out via process model

      implementation: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling in Kubernetes



 factor_9_disposability:

      rule: Fast startup, graceful shutdown

      startup_time: <10 seconds

      shutdown: SIGTERM handling, drain connections, finish in-flight requests

      health_checks: Readiness and liveness probes



 factor_10_dev_prod_parity:

      rule: Development, staging, production as similar as possible

      implementation: Same container images, different configs

      gap: Time (fast feedback), personnel (devs can deploy), tools (same stack)



 factor_11_logs:

      rule: Treat logs as event streams

      implementation: stdout/stderr, structured JSON logging

      aggregation: OpenTelemetry → Loki



 factor_12_admin_processes:

      rule: Run admin tasks as one-off processes

      implementation: Kubernetes Jobs, same codebase, same config

```

PART III — CODING STANDARDS



3.1 Go Coding Standards



```yaml

go_standards:

 version: "1.22+"



 style:

      formatter: gofumpt (stricter than gofmt)

      linter: golangci-lint

      imports: goimports



      naming:
  packages: lowercase, single word, no underscores

  interfaces: Single-method: Reader, Writer; Multi-method: Repository, Service

  structs: PascalCase

  functions: PascalCase (exported), camelCase (unexported)

  variables: camelCase

  constants: PascalCase (exported), camelCase (unexported)

  acronyms: ID, URL, HTTP, JSON (all caps or all lowercase based on context)



conventions:

 error_handling: |

  // CORRECT: Wrap errors with context

  if err != nil {

      return fmt.Errorf("failed to verify claim %s: %w", claimID, err)

  }



  // INCORRECT: Bare error return

  if err != nil {

      return err

  }



  // CORRECT: Custom error types

  var ErrClaimNotFound = errors.New("claim not found")



  // CORRECT: Error checking

  if errors.Is(err, ErrClaimNotFound) { ... }
context_propagation: |

 // CORRECT: Context always first parameter

 func (s *Service) VerifyClaim(ctx context.Context, claimID string) error



 // INCORRECT: Missing context

 func (s *Service) VerifyClaim(claimID string) error



concurrency: |

 // Use errgroup for parallel operations

 g, ctx := errgroup.WithContext(ctx)

 g.Go(func() error { return s.verifySource(ctx, id) })

 g.Go(func() error { return s.verifyClaim(ctx, id) })

 if err := g.Wait(); err != nil { ... }



 // Use context for cancellation

 // Never use time.Sleep for synchronization



interfaces: |

 // Define interfaces where they're used (consumer side)

 // Keep interfaces small (1-3 methods preferred)

 type ClaimVerifier interface {

     Verify(ctx context.Context, claim *Claim) (*VerificationResult, error)

 }



performance:

- Use sync.Pool for frequently allocated objects
 - Pre-allocate slices when size is known

 - Use strings.Builder for string concatenation

 - Avoid reflection in hot paths

 - Profile before optimizing



testing:

 framework: testify (assertions), go-mock (mocking)

 patterns:

  - Table-driven tests

  - Parallel tests with t.Parallel()

  - Test helpers with t.Helper()



 example: |

  func TestVerifyClaim(t *testing.T) {

    t.Parallel()



    tests := []struct {

         name string

         claim *Claim

         want Verdict

         wantErr bool

    }{

         {

             name: "verified true claim",

             claim: &Claim{Text: "Earth is round"},

             want: VerdictTrue,
                   wantErr: false,

              },

              // ... more cases

          }



          for _, tt := range tests {

              tt := tt

              t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {

                   t.Parallel()

                   svc := NewService(mockVerifier)

                   got, err := svc.VerifyClaim(context.Background(), tt.claim)

                   if tt.wantErr {

                       require.Error(t, err)

                       return

                   }

                   require.NoError(t, err)

                   assert.Equal(t, tt.want, got.Verdict)

              })

          }

      }

```



3.2 Python Coding Standards



```yaml

python_standards:
version: "3.12+"



style:

 formatter: black (line length 100)

 linter: ruff

 type_checker: mypy (strict mode)

 import_sorter: isort



 naming:

  classes: PascalCase

  functions: snake_case

  variables: snake_case

  constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE

  private: _leading_underscore



conventions:

 type_hints: |

  # CORRECT: All functions must have type hints

  async def verify_claim(

     self,

     claim: Claim,

     context: VerificationContext,

  ) -> VerificationResult:

     ...



  # INCORRECT: Missing type hints
 def verify_claim(self, claim, context):

   ...



async_io: |

 # Use async/await for I/O-bound operations

 # LLM calls, database queries, HTTP requests

 async def generate_article(self, story: EnrichedStory) -> GeneratedArticle:

   outline = await self.generate_outline(story)

   sections = await asyncio.gather(*[

         self.generate_section(story, sec) for sec in outline.sections

   ])

   return self.assemble(outline, sections)



error_handling: |

 # CORRECT: Specific exceptions

 try:

   result = await self.llm.generate(prompt)

 except LLMRateLimitError as e:

   await self.handle_rate_limit(e)

 except LLMTimeoutError as e:

   raise RetryableError(f"LLM timeout: {e}") from e



 # INCORRECT: Bare except

 try:

   result = await self.llm.generate(prompt)

 except:
       pass



 pydantic_models: |

  from pydantic import BaseModel, Field



  class ClaimVerification(BaseModel):

       claim_id: str = Field(..., description="UUID of the claim")

       verdict: Verdict

       confidence: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)

       evidence: list[Evidence] = Field(default_factory=list)



testing:

 framework: pytest + pytest-asyncio

 fixtures: conftest.py at each level

 mocking: pytest-mock, unittest.mock



 example: |

  @pytest.mark.asyncio

  async def test_generate_article_success(

       mock_llm_gateway,

       sample_enriched_story,

  ):

       mock_llm_gateway.generate.return_value = sample_response

       generator = ArticleGenerator(mock_llm_gateway)



       article = await generator.generate_article(
             sample_enriched_story,

             ArticleConfig(archetype="BREAKING_NEWS"),

         )



         assert article.word_count > 0

         assert len(article.headlines) >= 3

         mock_llm_gateway.generate.assert_called()

```



3.3 gRPC & Protobuf Standards



```yaml

protobuf_standards:

 version: proto3



 file_structure:

      naming: |

       api/{domain}/v{version}/{service}.proto

       Example: api/truth_engine/v1/verification.proto



      header: |

       syntax = "proto3";

       package truth_engine.v1;

       option go_package = "github.com/agbofa/nexus-api/truth_engine/v1";



 naming:
 services: PascalCase + "Service" suffix

 rpcs: PascalCase, VerbNoun pattern

 messages: PascalCase

 fields: snake_case

 enums: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE for values



 examples: |

  service ClaimVerificationService {

      rpc VerifyClaim(VerifyClaimRequest) returns (VerifyClaimResponse);

      rpc BatchVerifyClaims(BatchVerifyClaimsRequest) returns (stream ClaimVerification);

  }



  message VerifyClaimRequest {

      string tenant_id = 1;

      string claim_id = 2;

      VerificationOptions options = 3;

      string idempotency_key = 4;

  }



conventions:

 field_numbers: Never reuse deleted field numbers

 reserved: Mark deleted fields as reserved

 breaking_changes: Never change field types or numbers

 non_breaking_changes: Adding new fields (with appropriate defaults)



 validation: |
       Use buf.validate for proto validation

       message VerifyClaimRequest {

           string tenant_id = 1 [(buf.validate.field).string.uuid = true];

           string claim_id = 2 [(buf.validate.field).string.uuid = true];

       }



 code_generation:

      tool: buf (replaces protoc)

      configuration: buf.gen.yaml



      generated_code_location: |

       api/gen/

       ├── go/

       │ └── truth_engine/v1/

       │      ├── verification.pb.go

       │      └── verification_grpc.pb.go

       └── python/

           └── truth_engine/v1/

             └── verification_pb2.py

3.4 Error Handling Standards



```yaml

error_handling:

 principles:
 - Errors are values, not exceptions (Go)

 - Always add context when propagating errors

 - Never swallow errors silently

 - Log errors at service boundaries only

 - Use structured error types with error codes



error_codes:

 format: "DOMAIN-SUBSYSTEM-NUMBER"

 examples:

  - "TRUTH-VERIFY-001": Claim verification failed

  - "DIST-PUB-002": Platform publishing timeout

  - "COMPLY-COPY-003": Copyright check unavailable



 implementation: |

  type ErrorCode string



  const (

      ErrClaimVerificationFailed ErrorCode = "TRUTH-VERIFY-001"

      ErrSourceTimeout          ErrorCode = "TRUTH-SRC-002"

  )



  type ServiceError struct {

      Code   ErrorCode `json:"code"`

      Message string `json:"message"`

      Cause error      `json:"-"`

      Retryable bool    `json:"retryable"`
            Severity string `json:"severity"`

    }



    func (e *ServiceError) Error() string {

            return fmt.Sprintf("[%s] %s", e.Code, e.Message)

    }



gRPC_error_mapping: |

func MapToGRPC(err error) error {

        var svcErr *ServiceError

        if errors.As(err, &svcErr) {

             switch {

             case svcErr.Code.IsNotFound():

                 return status.Error(codes.NotFound, svcErr.Message)

             case svcErr.Code.IsInvalidArgument():

                 return status.Error(codes.InvalidArgument, svcErr.Message)

             case svcErr.Code.IsUnauthenticated():

                 return status.Error(codes.Unauthenticated, svcErr.Message)

             case svcErr.Code.IsRateLimited():

                 return status.Error(codes.ResourceExhausted, svcErr.Message)

             default:

                 return status.Error(codes.Internal, svcErr.Message)

             }

        }

        return status.Error(codes.Internal, "internal error")

}
```



3.5 Logging Standards



```yaml

logging:

 format: JSON structured logging



 levels:

      DEBUG: Development only, verbose diagnostic information

      INFO: Normal operations, business events (service started, story published)

      WARN: Retryable errors, degraded operations, approaching limits

      ERROR: Service failures, data loss risks, failed operations

      FATAL: Unrecoverable errors, service cannot continue



 required_fields:

      - timestamp: RFC3339 format

      - level: DEBUG/INFO/WARN/ERROR/FATAL

      - service: Service name

      - trace_id: OpenTelemetry trace ID

      - span_id: OpenTelemetry span ID

      - tenant_id: Tenant identifier (if applicable)

      - message: Human-readable message

      - error: Error details (if applicable)



 go_implementation: |
import "github.com/rs/zerolog"



func NewLogger(service string) zerolog.Logger {

    return zerolog.New(os.Stdout).

      With().

      Str("service", service).

      Timestamp().

      Logger()

}



// Usage

logger.Info().

    Str("story_id", storyID).

    Str("action", "publish").

    Msg("Story published successfully")



logger.Error().

    Err(err).

    Str("claim_id", claimID).

    Msg("Claim verification failed")



python_implementation: |

import structlog



logger = structlog.get_logger()
      # Usage

      await logger.info(

          "story_published",

          story_id=story_id,

          platform="twitter",

          duration_ms=elapsed_ms,

      )



      await logger.error(

          "verification_failed",

          claim_id=claim_id,

          error=str(err),

          exc_info=True,

      )



 anti_patterns:

      - NO: Logging sensitive data (PII, credentials, tokens)

      - NO: Using print() or fmt.Println() for logging

      - NO: Logging at every function call (use tracing for that)

      - NO: Inconsistent log formats between services

```

4.4 Hallucination Prevention Standards



```yaml

hallucination_prevention:

 mandatory_patterns:

  fact_locking: |

   // ALWAYS lock facts before passing to LLM

   lockedFacts := factLocker.LockFacts(ctx, storyID)

   // Pass locked facts, not raw story, to LLM

   response := llm.Generate(ctx, prompt, lockedFacts)



  constraint_injection: |

   // ALWAYS inject constraints into prompts

   prompt := fmt.Sprintf(`

    %s



    CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:

    - Only use facts from the provided fact set

    - Do not invent or embellish any details

    - If information is not in the fact set, say "information not available"

    - Quotes must be VERBATIM from: %s

   `, basePrompt, lockedQuotes)



  output_validation: |

   // ALWAYS validate LLM output against facts
       response := llm.Generate(ctx, prompt)

       violations := factValidator.Validate(response, lockedFacts)

       if len(violations) > 0 {

           // Regenerate with stricter constraints

           response = regenerateWithCorrections(ctx, prompt, violations)

       }



 testing:

      automated: |

       # Run hallucination detection test suite daily

       make test-hallucination



      metrics:

       - Hallucination rate per model

       - Hallucination rate per content type

       - Regeneration success rate



      thresholds:

       critical: 0% hallucination rate (breaking news, legal)

       standard: <0.1% hallucination rate

       non_critical: <0.5% hallucination rate

```

PART V — GIT & COLLABORATION
5.1 Branching Strategy



```

TRUNK-BASED DEVELOPMENT:



main

├── feature/TICKET-123-verify-claim         (max 2 days)

├── feature/TICKET-124-add-source-check         (max 2 days)

├── feature/TICKET-125-fix-headline-bug        (max 2 days)

│

├── release/v1.0.0                 (stabilization only)

├── release/v1.1.0

│

└── hotfix/TICKET-999-critical-security   (emergency only)



RULES:

1. All development on short-lived feature branches

2. Merge to main at least daily

3. main is always deployable

4. Feature flags protect incomplete features

5. Release branches for stabilization (max 2 days)

6. Hotfix branches for critical production issues

7. Delete branches after merge

```
5.2 Commit Standards



```yaml

commit_conventions:

 format: "type(scope): description"



 types:

  feat: New feature

  fix: Bug fix

  refactor: Code restructuring without behavior change

  test: Adding or updating tests

  docs: Documentation changes

  chore: Maintenance, dependencies, tooling

  perf: Performance improvements

  security: Security fixes

  ai: AI model or prompt changes



 scopes:

  - truth-engine

  - content-factory

  - distribution

  - compliance

  - analytics

  - infrastructure

  - api

  - ai-prompts
 examples:

      - "feat(truth-engine): add cross-source validation for breaking news"

      - "fix(content-factory): correct headline truncation on mobile"

      - "security(infrastructure): rotate TLS certificates"

      - "ai(prompts): update article generation prompt v1.2.0"

      - "test(distribution): add integration tests for Twitter connector"



 requirements:

      - Maximum 72 characters for subject line

      - Body explains WHAT and WHY (not HOW)

      - Reference ticket/issue number

      - Breaking changes marked with "BREAKING CHANGE:"

```

5.4 Versioning Strategy



```yaml

versioning:

 strategy: Semantic Versioning (SemVer)
format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH



rules:

 MAJOR:

  - Breaking API changes

  - Database schema migrations that are not backward compatible

  - Changes to Kafka event schemas (field removal/type change)



 MINOR:

  - New features (backward compatible)

  - New API endpoints

  - New event types

  - Database additions (new tables, new columns with defaults)



 PATCH:

  - Bug fixes

  - Performance improvements

  - Security patches

  - Documentation updates



release_cadence:

 PATCH: As needed (hotfixes)

 MINOR: Weekly (every Wednesday)

 MAJOR: Quarterly (planned, with migration guides)



changelog:
      format: Keep a Changelog (https://keepachangelog.com)

      location: CHANGELOG.md at repo root

      generation: Automated from conventional commits

```

7.1 CI/CD Pipeline



```yaml

ci_cd_pipeline:

 pull_request:

      triggers:

       - opened

       - synchronize

       - reopened



      jobs:

       lint:

        runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        steps:

         - checkout

         - golangci-lint (Go services)

         - ruff (Python services)

         - buf lint (protobuf)
 test:

  runs-on: ubuntu-latest

  strategy:

   matrix:

    service: ${{ steps.changed-services.outputs.list }}

  steps:

   - checkout

   - setup-go / setup-python

   - run: make test SERVICE=${{ matrix.service }}



 security:

  runs-on: ubuntu-latest

  steps:

   - trufflehog (secrets scan)

   - semgrep (SAST)

   - dependency-review



 contract-test:

  runs-on: ubuntu-latest

  steps:

   - buf breaking (API compatibility)

   - run: make contract-test



merge_to_main:

triggers:
 - push to main



jobs:

 build:

  strategy:

   matrix:

    service: ${{ steps.changed-services.outputs.list }}

  steps:

   - checkout

   - build container image

   - trivy scan

   - syft SBOM generation

   - cosign image signing

   - push to ECR



 deploy-staging:

  needs: build

  steps:

   - flux reconcile

   - wait for rollout

   - smoke tests



 deploy-production:

  needs: deploy-staging

  environment: production

  steps:
         - approval gate (for MAJOR/MINOR)

         - canary deployment (10% → 50% → 100%)

         - metric validation

         - auto-rollback on failure

```

13.2 Final Engineering Recommendations



1. Start with Foundation: Deploy infrastructure and foundation services first. Everything
depends on them.

2. Contract-First Development: Define all API contracts before coding. This enables parallel team
work.

3. AI as Accelerator: Use AI coding agents for initial implementation, but always with human
review.

4. Ship Incrementally: Deploy each service as it's ready. Don't wait for the full platform.

5. Monitor from Day One: Don't defer observability. Every service must emit metrics and traces
from the start.

6. Test in Production (Safely): Use canary deployments and feature flags to validate in
production.

7. Document as You Go: Documentation is code. Review it, version it, keep it current.

8. Security is Continuous: Integrate security scanning in CI/CD. Never defer security to a later
phase.

9. Own Your Services: Service teams own development, deployment, and operations.

10. Measure and Improve: Use SLOs to drive decisions. Continuously improve based on data.

---



REPOSITORY DECISION RECORDS (RDR)



RDR-001: Monorepo with Domain-Based Structure



Decision: Single monorepo containing all services, shared libraries, infrastructure, AI modules,
and documentation. Domains organized by bounded context from Volumes 11-19.

Why: 60+ microservices require extensive code sharing. Monorepo enables atomic refactoring,
consistent versioning, simplified dependency management, and unified CI/CD. Domain-based
structure maps directly to architecture.

Alternatives: Polyrepo (rejected — coordination overhead for 60+ repos); Hybrid with separate
library repos (rejected — versioning hell with rapid AI development).

Trade-offs: Larger clone size (mitigated by sparse checkout), but significant gains in developer
velocity and consistency.



RDR-002: Go Workspaces + Python Monorepo Tools



Decision: Go workspaces (go.work) for Go services, Pants build system for Python monorepo
management, pnpm workspaces for frontend/Node.js packages.
Why: Each language ecosystem has different monorepo tooling maturity. Go workspaces are
native and stable. Pants provides Python monorepo support at scale. pnpm is the standard for
Node.js monorepos.

Alternatives: Bazel (rejected — too complex for initial phases, may adopt later); Nx (rejected —
JavaScript-centric, Go/Python support limited).

Trade-offs: Three build tools instead of one, but each is best-in-class for its ecosystem.



RDR-003: Contract-First with Centralized API Definitions



Decision: All API definitions (Protobuf, OpenAPI, JSON Schema, AsyncAPI) live in /api/ at
repository root. Code generation produces language-specific clients. Breaking changes detected
in CI.

Why: APIs are the contracts between services. Centralized definitions ensure consistency,
enable parallel development, and provide single source of truth for code generation.

Alternatives: API definitions in each service (rejected — scattered, inconsistent, hard to
discover).

Trade-offs: Requires discipline to update central definitions first, but eliminates integration
surprises.



RDR-004: Template-Based Service Scaffolding



Decision: Every service created from standardized templates using cookiecutter (Python) and
custom Go templates. Templates enforce Clean Architecture, observability, and security
patterns.

Why: 60+ services must be consistent. Templates eliminate boilerplate decisions and ensure
every service follows standards from Volume 21.

Alternatives: Manual service creation (rejected — inconsistent, error-prone at scale).

Trade-offs: Template maintenance overhead, but essential for consistency across 60+ services.

1.2 Monorepo Strategy
```yaml

monorepo_strategy:

 organization: Domain-based with shared infrastructure



 boundaries:

  api/: API contracts (single source of truth)

  services/: Business logic services (by bounded context)

  libs/: Shared libraries (cross-cutting concerns)

  ai/: AI models, prompts, datasets

  infrastructure/: IaC, Kubernetes, Terraform

  docs/: Documentation, ADRs

  tests/: E2E, integration, performance tests

  tools/: Developer tooling, scripts



 dependency_flow:

  direction: |

   services/ ──depends on──         libs/

   services/ ──depends on──         api/ (generated code)

   ai/ ──depends on──       libs/

   infrastructure/ ──independent── (references service images)

   tests/ ──depends on──       services/ (integration tests)



  rule: |

   Services CAN depend on shared libraries

   Services CANNOT depend on other services
       Services communicate ONLY via APIs and events

       Libraries CANNOT depend on services



 ownership:

      model: CODEOWNERS per domain directory

      example: |

       /services/truth-engine/ @agbofa/truth-engine-team

       /services/content-factory/ @agbofa/content-factory-team

       /libs/go/          @agbofa/platform-team

       /infrastructure/     @agbofa/platform-team

```



1.3 Development Principles



```yaml

development_principles:

 onboarding:

      time_to_productivity: <30 minutes

      single_command_startup: "make dev-up"

      comprehensive_readme: Every directory



 consistency:

      automated_enforcement: Linting, formatting, testing in CI

      template_based_creation: All new services from templates

      naming_conventions: Strict, documented, enforced
 quality:

      test_coverage_minimum: 80%

      linting_zero_warnings: Required for merge

      security_scan_clean: No CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities



 velocity:

      fast_builds: Incremental builds, caching

      parallel_execution: Independent services build in parallel

      local_first: Everything runs locally



 ai_compatibility:

      structured_directories: Predictable locations

      explicit_conventions: Documented in .cursorrules

      comprehensive_templates: AI agents use templates

      contract_definitions: Machine-readable API specs

```

2.2 Key Directory Explanations



```yaml

directory_explanations:

 api/:

      purpose: "Single source of truth for all API contracts"

      contents: "Protobuf, OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, JSON Schema"

      generation: "Code generated to api/gen/ via CI"

      consumers: "All services, SDKs, documentation"



 services/:

      purpose: "Business logic microservices"

      organization: "By bounded context (matching Volumes 11-19)"

      independence: "Each service independently buildable and deployable"

      template: "Created from tools/templates/"



 libs/:

      purpose: "Shared code across services"

      go/: "Go shared libraries (events, auth, observability, etc.)"
 python/: "Python shared libraries (LLM, NLP, prompts, etc.)"

 node/: "Node.js/TypeScript shared packages (UI, utils, API client)"

 rule: "Libraries have NO business logic; pure infrastructure concerns"



ai/:

 purpose: "AI-specific resources, versioned separately from code"

 prompts/: "Prompt templates with semantic versioning"

 models/: "Fine-tuning scripts and evaluation results"

 datasets/: "Training and evaluation datasets (sampled/synthetic)"



infrastructure/:

 purpose: "Everything needed to deploy and operate"

 terraform/: "Cloud infrastructure (EKS, RDS, MSK, etc.)"

 kubernetes/: "Kubernetes manifests (Flux CD GitOps)"

 helm/: "Helm charts for standardized deployments"



docs/:

 purpose: "All project documentation"

 adr/: "Architecture Decision Records (immutable history)"

 runbooks/: "Operational procedures"

 guides/: "Developer onboarding and contribution guides"



tests/:

 purpose: "Cross-service tests that don't belong to any single service"

 integration/: "End-to-end workflow tests"

 contract/: "Pact contract tests between services"
      performance/: "k6 load testing scenarios"



 tools/:

      purpose: "Developer productivity tools"

      dev-environment/: "Docker Compose for local development"

      scripts/: "Automation scripts"

      templates/: "Service scaffolding templates (cookiecutter)"

```

PART IV — SHARED ENGINEERING LIBRARIES



4.1 Go Shared Library Design



```go

// libs/go/pkg/events/types.go

// Package events defines all Kafka event types and provides standardized

// producer/consumer implementations used by all services.

package events



// EventType represents a unique event type identifier
type EventType string



const (

  // Foundation Events

  EventTenantProvisioned EventType = "foundation.tenant.provisioned"

  EventUserCreated         EventType = "foundation.user.created"

  EventUserAuthenticated EventType = "foundation.user.authenticated"



  // Content Origination Events

  EventStoryDetected        EventType = "content_origination.story.detected"

  EventSourceUpdated          EventType = "content_origination.source.updated"



  // Truth Engine Events

  EventClaimVerified       EventType = "truth_engine.claim.verified"

  EventConfidenceCalculated EventType = "truth_engine.confidence.calculated"

  EventStoryVerified       EventType = "truth_engine.story.verified"

  EventMisinfoDetected        EventType = "truth_engine.misinfo.detected"



  // Content Factory Events

  EventArticleGenerated      EventType = "content_factory.article.generated"

  EventContentPackaged        EventType = "content_factory.content.packaged"

  EventTranslationCompleted EventType = "content_factory.translation.completed"



  // Compliance Events

  EventComplianceChecked EventType = "compliance.checked"

  EventRightsViolation      EventType = "compliance.rights.violation"
    // Distribution Events

    EventPublicationQueued EventType = "distribution.publication.queued"

    EventPublicationCompleted EventType = "distribution.publication.completed"

    EventPublicationFailed EventType = "distribution.publication.failed"



    // Analytics Events

    EventMetricsCollected    EventType = "analytics.metrics.collected"

    EventOptimizationSignal EventType = "analytics.optimization.signal"

)



// Event is the base interface for all domain events

type Event interface {

    EventType() EventType

    EventID() string

    Timestamp() time.Time

    TenantID() string

}



// BaseEvent provides common event fields

type BaseEvent struct {

    ID     string `json:"event_id"`

    Type    EventType `json:"event_type"`

    Timestamp time.Time `json:"timestamp"`

    TenantID string `json:"tenant_id"`

}

```go

// libs/go/pkg/events/producer.go

package events



import (

      "context"

      "encoding/json"

      "fmt"



      "github.com/IBM/sarama"

      "go.opentelemetry.io/otel"

)



// Producer provides standardized Kafka event publishing

type Producer struct {

      client sarama.SyncProducer

      tracer trace.Tracer

      metrics *ProducerMetrics

}



// ProducerConfig configures the event producer

type ProducerConfig struct {

      Brokers     []string

      ClientID    string
    Acks         sarama.RequiredAcks // WaitForAll for critical events

    EnableTracing bool

}



// NewProducer creates a new standardized event producer

func NewProducer(config ProducerConfig) (*Producer, error) {

    saramaConfig := sarama.NewConfig()

    saramaConfig.Producer.RequiredAcks = config.Acks

    saramaConfig.Producer.Return.Successes = true

    saramaConfig.Producer.Idempotent = true

    saramaConfig.Producer.Compression = sarama.CompressionSnappy

    saramaConfig.ClientID = config.ClientID



    client, err := sarama.NewSyncProducer(config.Brokers, saramaConfig)

    if err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("create kafka producer: %w", err)

    }



    return &Producer{

        client: client,

        tracer: otel.Tracer("events/producer"),

        metrics: NewProducerMetrics(),

    }, nil

}



// Publish publishes an event to Kafka with tracing and metrics
func (p *Producer) Publish(ctx context.Context, event Event) error {

  ctx, span := p.tracer.Start(ctx, "events.Publish")

  defer span.End()



  // Serialize event

  payload, err := json.Marshal(event)

  if err != nil {

      return fmt.Errorf("marshal event: %w", err)

  }



  // Determine topic from event type

  topic := p.eventTypeToTopic(event.EventType())



  // Build Kafka message

  msg := &sarama.ProducerMessage{

      Topic: topic,

      Key: sarama.StringEncoder(event.EventID()),

      Value: sarama.ByteEncoder(payload),

      Headers: []sarama.RecordHeader{

           {Key: []byte("event_type"), Value: []byte(event.EventType())},

           {Key: []byte("tenant_id"), Value: []byte(event.TenantID())},

      },

  }



  // Inject tracing headers

  otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Inject(ctx, NewKafkaHeaderCarrier(&msg.Headers))
      // Publish

      partition, offset, err := p.client.SendMessage(msg)

      if err != nil {

          p.metrics.RecordError(event.EventType())

          return fmt.Errorf("publish event: %w", err)

      }



      span.SetAttributes(

          attribute.String("kafka.topic", topic),

          attribute.Int64("kafka.partition", int64(partition)),

          attribute.Int64("kafka.offset", offset),

      )



      p.metrics.RecordSuccess(event.EventType())

      return nil

}

4.2 Python Shared Library Design



```python

# libs/python/agbofa/llm/client.py

"""

LLM Gateway Client — Standardized interface for all LLM interactions.
All services use this client to interact with LLMs. It provides:

- Model routing (cost-optimized tiering)

- Automatic retries with exponential backoff

- Response caching

- Token usage tracking

- Prompt template rendering

"""



from dataclasses import dataclass

from typing import Optional, Any

import structlog



logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)




@dataclass

class LLMRequest:

  """Standardized LLM request."""

  prompt: str

  model: str = "claude-3-sonnet"

  temperature: float = 0.4

  max_tokens: int = 4000

  response_format: Optional[str] = None # "json" for structured output

  cache_ttl: int = 3600 # Cache duration in seconds
@dataclass

class LLMResponse:

  """Standardized LLM response."""

  text: str

  model: str

  tokens_used: int

  cost_usd: float

  cached: bool = False

  latency_ms: float = 0.0




class LLMClient:

  """

  Standardized LLM client for all Agbofa services.



  Usage:

    client = LLMClient(default_model="claude-3-sonnet")

    response = await client.generate(LLMRequest(

         prompt="Generate a headline for...",

         temperature=0.4,

    ))

  """



  def __init__(self, default_model: str = "claude-3-sonnet"):

    self.default_model = default_model

    self._cache = {} # In-memory cache (use Redis in production)
  self._token_tracker = TokenTracker()



async def generate(self, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse:

  """

  Generate LLM response with automatic retries and caching.

  """

  # Check cache

  if request.cache_ttl > 0:

    cache_key = self._cache_key(request)

    if cache_key in self._cache:

        logger.debug("llm_cache_hit", model=request.model)

        return self._cache[cache_key]



  # Route to appropriate model

  model = request.model or self.default_model



  # Generate with retries

  for attempt in range(3):

    try:

        response = await self._call_llm(model, request)



        # Track token usage

        self._token_tracker.record(response.tokens_used, response.cost_usd)



        # Cache response

        if request.cache_ttl > 0:
          self._cache[cache_key] = response



      logger.info(

          "llm_generated",

          model=model,

          tokens=response.tokens_used,

          cost=response.cost_usd,

          latency_ms=response.latency_ms,

      )



      return response



    except Exception as e:

      logger.warning(

          "llm_retry",

          model=model,

          attempt=attempt + 1,

          error=str(e),

      )

      if attempt == 2:

          raise

      await asyncio.sleep(2 ** attempt)



async def _call_llm(self, model: str, request: LLMRequest) -> LLMResponse:

  """Internal LLM call — routes to appropriate provider."""

  # Implementation routes to Claude, GPT, etc. via gateway
      ...

```

5.2 Go Service Main Entry Point Template
```go

// cmd/server/main.go — Service Entry Point Template

package main



import (

    "context"

    "fmt"

    "net"

    "os"

    "os/signal"

    "syscall"



    "go.uber.org/fx"

    "google.golang.org/grpc"

    "google.golang.org/grpc/health/grpc_health_v1"



    "github.com/agbofa/nexus-ai/libs/go/pkg/observability"

    "github.com/agbofa/nexus-ai/libs/go/pkg/config"

)



func main() {

    // Load configuration

    cfg, err := config.Load[ServiceConfig]()

    if err != nil {

      fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to load config: %v\n", err)
     os.Exit(1)

}



// Initialize observability

shutdown, err := observability.Initialize(observability.Config{

     ServiceName: cfg.ServiceName,

     ServiceVersion: cfg.ServiceVersion,

     Environment: cfg.Environment,

     OTLPEndpoint: cfg.OTLPEndpoint,

})

if err != nil {

     fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to initialize observability: %v\n", err)

     os.Exit(1)

}

defer shutdown()



// Build dependency graph

app := fx.New(

     fx.Supply(cfg),

     fx.Provide(

       NewPostgresConnection,

       NewKafkaProducer,

       NewKafkaConsumer,

       NewRepository,

       NewDomainService,

       NewApplicationService,
           NewGRPCHandler,

           NewHealthChecker,

      ),

      fx.Invoke(RegisterGRPCServer),

      fx.Invoke(StartKafkaConsumer),

  )



  // Start application

  ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)

  defer cancel()



  if err := app.Start(ctx); err != nil {

      fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to start application: %v\n", err)

      os.Exit(1)

  }



  // Wait for shutdown signal

  <-ctx.Done()



  // Graceful shutdown

  shutdownCtx, shutdownCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(),
30*time.Second)

  defer shutdownCancel()



  if err := app.Stop(shutdownCtx); err != nil {

      fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "failed to stop application: %v\n", err)
          os.Exit(1)

      }

}

      │

           │

           ▼

    infrastructure/          # Deployment manifests

           │

           ▼

    staging deployment

           │

           ▼

    production deployment



BUILD ORDER:

1. Generate API code (make api-gen)

2. Build shared libraries

3. Build services in dependency order:

 a. Foundation (no dependencies)
  b. Content Origination (depends on foundation)

  c. Truth Engine (depends on foundation)

  d. Content Factory (depends on truth engine)

  e. Compliance (depends on content factory)

  f. Distribution (depends on compliance)

  g. Analytics (depends on distribution)

      services: kebab-case (tenant-identity, story-detection)

      domains: kebab-case matching Volume names



 files:

      go: snake_case (user_service.go, claim_verifier.go)

      python: snake_case (user_service.py, claim_verifier.py)

      protobuf: snake_case (tenant_identity.proto)

      kubernetes: kebab-case (deployment.yaml, service-account.yaml)

      terraform: snake_case (main.tf, variables.tf)



 go_packages:

      format: lowercase, no underscores

      examples: "tenantidentity" (not "tenant_identity")
 protobuf_packages:

      format: domain.v1

      examples: "truth_engine.v1", "content_factory.v1"



 kafka_topics:

      examples: "truth_engine.claim.verified", "distribution.publication.completed"



 docker_images:

      format: registry/domain-service:tag

      examples: "ecr.aws/truth-engine-claim-verifier:v1.2.3"



 branches:

      feature: feature/TICKET-123-short-description

      bugfix: fix/TICKET-456-short-description

      hotfix: hotfix/TICKET-789-critical-fix

      release: release/v1.2.0



 commits:

      format: "type(scope): description"

      types: feat, fix, refactor, test, docs, chore, perf, security, ai

PART XII — FOUNDATION DECISION RECORDS



```markdown

## RDR-001: Monorepo with Domain-Based Structure

**Decision:** Single monorepo with bounded context organization

**Rationale:** 60+ services, shared code, atomic refactoring
**Trade-offs:** Clone size vs. development velocity



## RDR-002: Go Workspaces + Pants + pnpm

**Decision:** Three build tools, each best-in-class for ecosystem

**Rationale:** Go workspaces native, Pants for Python scale, pnpm standard

**Trade-offs:** Three tools vs. one, but optimal per ecosystem



## RDR-003: Contract-First API Development

**Decision:** Centralized API definitions, code generation

**Rationale:** Single source of truth, parallel development

**Trade-offs:** Upfront API design vs. iteration speed



## RDR-004: Template-Based Service Scaffolding

**Decision:** Cookiecutter templates for all services

**Rationale:** Consistency across 60+ services

**Trade-offs:** Template maintenance vs. consistency gains



## RDR-005: Docker Compose for Local Development

**Decision:** Full local environment via Docker Compose

**Rationale:** Identical dependencies to production

**Trade-offs:** Resource usage vs. environment fidelity



## RDR-006: Trunk-Based Development

**Decision:** Short-lived branches, continuous integration

**Rationale:** Rapid AI-assisted development

**Trade-offs:** Branch discipline vs. merge conflict reduction
```

SERVICE DECISION RECORDS (SDR)



SDR-001: Argon2id for Password Hashing



Decision: Use Argon2id with calibrated parameters (time=3, memory=65536, threads=4) for all
password hashing.

Rationale: Argon2id is the OWASP-recommended algorithm, resistant to GPU and side-channel
attacks. Calibrated parameters provide ~500ms hashing time, balancing security and user
experience.

Alternatives: bcrypt (rejected — less memory-hard, more vulnerable to GPU attacks); scrypt
(rejected — less studied than Argon2id).

Trade-offs: Higher memory usage per hash, but acceptable for authentication service scale.
SDR-002: JWT with Asymmetric Signing (Ed25519)



Decision: Sign all JWTs using Ed25519 asymmetric keys, with key rotation every 30 days via
Vault.

Rationale: Ed25519 provides 128-bit security with small signatures and fast verification.
Asymmetric signing allows any service to verify tokens without sharing secrets.

Alternatives: RS256 (rejected — larger keys and signatures); HS256 (rejected — symmetric,
requires secret sharing).

Trade-offs: Key management complexity, but significantly better security posture.



SDR-003: Row-Level Security for Multi-Tenancy



Decision: Enforce tenant isolation at the database level using PostgreSQL Row-Level Security
(RLS) policies, with application-level tenant context injection.

Rationale: Defense in depth — even if application logic fails, database prevents cross-tenant
data access. RLS is more reliable than application-level filtering alone.

Alternatives: Separate databases per tenant (rejected — operational complexity); application-
level only (rejected — insufficient isolation).

Trade-offs: Slight query overhead, but essential for multi-tenant security.



SDR-004: SPIFFE/SPIRE for Service Identity



Decision: All service-to-service authentication uses SPIFFE/SPIRE-issued X.509 certificates with
mTLS, enforced by Istio Ambient Mesh.

Rationale: SPIFFE provides cryptographically verifiable workload identity without manual
certificate management. Automatic rotation eliminates certificate expiry risks.

Alternatives: Manual certificate management (rejected — operational burden); API keys
(rejected — weaker security model).
Trade-offs: SPIRE infrastructure overhead, but essential for zero-trust architecture.

PART II — TENANT & IDENTITY SERVICE



2.1 Service Overview



Service ID: SVC-FND-TIS

Runtime: Golang 1.22+

gRPC Port: 9091
Health Port: 9090

Metrics Port: 9092



The Tenant & Identity Service is the root trust domain for all human and non-human actors in
the Agbofa Nexus AI platform. It manages the complete lifecycle of tenants, users,
authentication, and session management.



2.2 Domain Model



```go

// internal/domain/model.go

package domain



import (

    "time"

    "github.com/google/uuid"

)



// Tenant represents a customer organization

type Tenant struct {

    ID       uuid.UUID `json:"id"`

    Name       string    `json:"name"`

    Slug     string     `json:"slug"`    // URL-safe identifier

    Status TenantStatus `json:"status"`

    Tier     TenantTier `json:"tier"`      // FREE, PRO, ENTERPRISE

    Config TenantConfig `json:"config"`

    CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
    UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updated_at"`

}



type TenantStatus string

const (

    TenantStatusActive         TenantStatus = "ACTIVE"

    TenantStatusSuspended TenantStatus = "SUSPENDED"

    TenantStatusDeleted TenantStatus = "DELETED"

    TenantStatusTrial         TenantStatus = "TRIAL"

)



type TenantTier string

const (

    TierFree    TenantTier = "FREE"

    TierPro     TenantTier = "PRO"

    TierEnterprise TenantTier = "ENTERPRISE"

)



// TenantConfig stores tenant-specific configuration

type TenantConfig struct {

    MaxUsers            int          `json:"max_users"`

    MaxStoriesPerDay           int       `json:"max_stories_per_day"`

    AllowedAuthProviders []AuthProvider          `json:"allowed_auth_providers"`

    DefaultRegion        string         `json:"default_region"`

    SSOConfig           *SSOConfig        `json:"sso_config,omitempty"`

    MFAPolicy           MFAPolicy        `json:"mfa_policy"`
    SessionTimeoutMinutes int             `json:"session_timeout_minutes"`

    AllowedDomains       []string      `json:"allowed_domains"`

    CustomBranding       *BrandingConfig `json:"custom_branding,omitempty"`

}



type AuthProvider string

const (

    AuthProviderEmail AuthProvider = "EMAIL"

    AuthProviderGoogle AuthProvider = "GOOGLE"

    AuthProviderGitHub AuthProvider = "GITHUB"

    AuthProviderSAML     AuthProvider = "SAML"

    AuthProviderOIDC     AuthProvider = "OIDC"

)



type MFAPolicy string

const (

    MFAPolicyOptional MFAPolicy = "OPTIONAL"

    MFAPolicyRequired MFAPolicy = "REQUIRED"

    MFAPolicyAdminOnly MFAPolicy = "ADMIN_ONLY"

)



// User represents a platform user

type User struct {

    ID         uuid.UUID `json:"id"`

    TenantID      uuid.UUID `json:"tenant_id"`

    Email       string   `json:"email"`
    EmailVerified bool           `json:"email_verified"`

    DisplayName       string      `json:"display_name"`

    AvatarURL        string     `json:"avatar_url,omitempty"`

    Status        UserStatus `json:"status"`

    Roles         []string    `json:"roles"`

    MFAEnabled        bool        `json:"mfa_enabled"`

    MFAVerified      bool        `json:"mfa_verified"`

    LastLoginAt      *time.Time `json:"last_login_at"`

    CreatedAt       time.Time `json:"created_at"`

    UpdatedAt        time.Time `json:"updated_at"`

    DeactivatedAt *time.Time `json:"deactivated_at,omitempty"`

}



type UserStatus string

const (

    UserStatusActive            UserStatus = "ACTIVE"

    UserStatusPendingVerification UserStatus = "PENDING_VERIFICATION"

    UserStatusPasswordReset           UserStatus = "PASSWORD_RESET_REQUIRED"

    UserStatusDisabled            UserStatus = "DISABLED"

    UserStatusSuspended             UserStatus = "SUSPENDED"

)



// Session represents an authenticated user session

type Session struct {

    ID       uuid.UUID `json:"id"`

    UserID        uuid.UUID `json:"user_id"`
      TenantID      uuid.UUID `json:"tenant_id"`

      RefreshTokenHash string `json:"-"`

      DeviceInfo    DeviceInfo `json:"device_info"`

      IPAddress     string    `json:"ip_address"`

      UserAgent      string    `json:"user_agent"`

      IsTrusted    bool       `json:"is_trusted"`

      CreatedAt     time.Time `json:"created_at"`

      ExpiresAt     time.Time `json:"expires_at"`

      RevokedAt      *time.Time `json:"revoked_at,omitempty"`

}



type DeviceInfo struct {

      DeviceID string `json:"device_id"`

      DeviceName string `json:"device_name"`

      DeviceType string `json:"device_type"` // MOBILE, DESKTOP, TABLET

      OS     string `json:"os"`

      Browser string `json:"browser"`

}

```



2.3 Authentication Flow Sequence



```

AUTHENTICATION FLOW (Password Login):



Client             API Gateway        Tenant-Identity   PostgreSQL   Redis   Kafka
│           │             │          │               │           │

│──POST /auth/login──      │             │               │               │               │

2.5 JWT Token Structure



```go

// internal/domain/token.go

package domain
import (

    "crypto/ed25519"

    "time"



    "github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5"

)



// TokenClaims represents the JWT claims structure

type TokenClaims struct {

    jwt.RegisteredClaims



    // Tenant context

    TenantID string `json:"tenant_id"`

    TenantSlug string `json:"tenant_slug"`



    // User context

    UserID       string `json:"user_id"`

    Email    string `json:"email"`

    DisplayName string `json:"display_name"`



    // Authorization

    Roles    []string `json:"roles"`

    Permissions []string `json:"permissions,omitempty"`



    // Session
    SessionID string `json:"session_id"`



    // Security

    TokenID        string `json:"jti"`

    IssuedAt int64 `json:"iat"`

    ExpiresAt int64 `json:"exp"`

    NotBefore int64 `json:"nbf"`

}



// TokenService manages JWT creation and validation

type TokenService struct {

    privateKey ed25519.PrivateKey

    publicKey ed25519.PublicKey

    keyID       string

    issuer      string

    ttl       time.Duration

}



// NewTokenService creates a token service with key rotation support

func NewTokenService(vaultClient VaultClient) (*TokenService, error) {

    // Fetch current signing key from Vault

    key, err := vaultClient.GetSigningKey(context.Background())

    if err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("get signing key: %w", err)

    }
    return &TokenService{

       privateKey: key.Private,

       publicKey: key.Public,

       keyID:        key.ID,

       issuer:       "agbofa-nexus",

       ttl:        15 * time.Minute, // Access token: 15 minutes

    }, nil

}



// CreateAccessToken generates a new JWT access token

func (ts *TokenService) CreateAccessToken(user *User, session *Session) (string, error) {

    now := time.Now()



    claims := &TokenClaims{

       RegisteredClaims: jwt.RegisteredClaims{

             Issuer: ts.issuer,

             Subject: user.ID.String(),

             Audience: jwt.ClaimStrings{"agbofa-nexus"},

             ExpiresAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now.Add(ts.ttl)),

             NotBefore: jwt.NewNumericDate(now),

             IssuedAt: jwt.NewNumericDate(now),

             ID:     uuid.NewV7().String(),

       },

       TenantID: user.TenantID.String(),

       UserID:        user.ID.String(),

       Email:        user.Email,
        DisplayName: user.DisplayName,

        Roles:        user.Roles,

        SessionID: session.ID.String(),

    }



    token := jwt.NewWithClaims(jwt.SigningMethodEdDSA, claims)

    token.Header["kid"] = ts.keyID



    signed, err := token.SignedString(ts.privateKey)

    if err != nil {

        return "", fmt.Errorf("sign token: %w", err)

    }



    return signed, nil

}



// ValidateAccessToken validates and parses a JWT access token

func (ts *TokenService) ValidateAccessToken(tokenString string) (*TokenClaims, error) {

    token, err := jwt.ParseWithClaims(tokenString, &TokenClaims{},

        func(token *jwt.Token) (interface{}, error) {

          // Verify signing algorithm

          if _, ok := token.Method.(*jwt.SigningMethodEd25519); !ok {

              return nil, fmt.Errorf("unexpected signing method: %v", token.Header["alg"])

          }



          // Verify key ID matches current key
               if token.Header["kid"] != ts.keyID {

                   // Could be rotated — check Vault for previous key

                   return ts.getKeyByID(token.Header["kid"].(string))

               }



               return ts.publicKey, nil

          },

          jwt.WithLeeway(30*time.Second), // 30 second clock skew tolerance

      )



      if err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse token: %w", err)

      }



      claims, ok := token.Claims.(*TokenClaims)

      if !ok || !token.Valid {

          return nil, ErrInvalidToken

      }



      return claims, nil

}

```



2.6 Refresh Token Rotation



```go
// internal/domain/refresh_token.go

package domain



import (

    "crypto/rand"

    "crypto/sha256"

    "encoding/hex"

    "time"

)



// RefreshTokenService manages opaque refresh tokens with rotation

type RefreshTokenService struct {

    store RefreshTokenStore

}



// GenerateRefreshToken creates a new cryptographically random refresh token

func (rts *RefreshTokenService) GenerateRefreshToken() (string, error) {

    // 256-bit random token

    bytes := make([]byte, 32)

    if _, err := rand.Read(bytes); err != nil {

        return "", fmt.Errorf("generate random: %w", err)

    }



    // URL-safe base64 encoding

    token := base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(bytes)

    return token, nil
}



// StoreRefreshToken hashes and stores the refresh token

func (rts *RefreshTokenService) StoreRefreshToken(

    ctx context.Context,

    token string,

    sessionID uuid.UUID,

    expiresAt time.Time,

) error {

    // Hash the token with SHA-256 before storage

    hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(token))

    tokenHash := hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])



    return rts.store.Store(ctx, &StoredRefreshToken{

         TokenHash: tokenHash,

         SessionID: sessionID,

         ExpiresAt: expiresAt,

         CreatedAt: time.Now(),

    })

}



// RotateRefreshToken implements token rotation:

// 1. Validate old token

// 2. Revoke old token

// 3. Issue new token

// This prevents refresh token replay attacks
func (rts *RefreshTokenService) RotateRefreshToken(

  ctx context.Context,

  oldToken string,

) (*TokenRotation, error) {



  // 1. Hash the old token

  oldHash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(oldToken))

  oldTokenHash := hex.EncodeToString(oldHash[:])



  // 2. Find and validate the stored token

  stored, err := rts.store.FindByHash(ctx, oldTokenHash)

  if err != nil {

      return nil, ErrInvalidRefreshToken

  }



  // 3. Check expiration

  if time.Now().After(stored.ExpiresAt) {

      return nil, ErrRefreshTokenExpired

  }



  // 4. Check if already revoked (replay attack detection)

  if stored.RevokedAt != nil {

      // Token reuse detected — revoke ALL tokens for this user

      rts.store.RevokeAllForUser(ctx, stored.UserID)

      return nil, ErrTokenReuseDetected

  }
      // 5. Revoke old token

      if err := rts.store.Revoke(ctx, oldTokenHash); err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("revoke old token: %w", err)

      }



      // 6. Generate new token

      newToken, err := rts.GenerateRefreshToken()

      if err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("generate new token: %w", err)

      }



      // 7. Store new token with same session

      newExpiresAt := time.Now().Add(7 * 24 * time.Hour) // 7 days

      if err := rts.StoreRefreshToken(ctx, newToken, stored.SessionID, newExpiresAt); err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("store new token: %w", err)

      }



      return &TokenRotation{

          NewToken: newToken,

          SessionID: stored.SessionID,

          ExpiresAt: newExpiresAt,

      }, nil

}

```
2.7 Password Management



```go

// internal/domain/password.go

package domain



import (

    "crypto/subtle"

    "fmt"



    "golang.org/x/crypto/argon2"

)



// Argon2id parameters (OWASP recommended)

const (

    argon2Time = 3      // Number of iterations

    argon2Memory = 65536 // 64 MB

    argon2Threads = 4    // Number of threads

    argon2KeyLen = 32 // 256-bit key

    argon2SaltLen = 16 // 128-bit salt

)



// PasswordService manages password hashing and verification

type PasswordService struct{}



// HashPassword hashes a password using Argon2id
func (ps *PasswordService) HashPassword(password string) (string, error) {

  // Generate random salt

  salt := make([]byte, argon2SaltLen)

  if _, err := rand.Read(salt); err != nil {

      return "", fmt.Errorf("generate salt: %w", err)

  }



  // Hash password with Argon2id

  hash := argon2.IDKey(

      []byte(password),

      salt,

      argon2Time,

      argon2Memory,

      argon2Threads,

      argon2KeyLen,

  )



  // Encode as: $argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=4$<salt>$<hash>

  encoded := fmt.Sprintf(

      "$argon2id$v=19$m=%d,t=%d,p=%d$%s$%s",

      argon2Memory,

      argon2Time,

      argon2Threads,

      base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(salt),

      base64.RawStdEncoding.EncodeToString(hash),

  )
    return encoded, nil

}



// VerifyPassword verifies a password against its hash using constant-time comparison

func (ps *PasswordService) VerifyPassword(password, encodedHash string) (bool, error) {

    // Parse encoded hash

    params, salt, hash, err := ps.decodeHash(encodedHash)

    if err != nil {

        return false, fmt.Errorf("decode hash: %w", err)

    }



    // Recompute hash with same parameters

    computedHash := argon2.IDKey(

        []byte(password),

        salt,

        params.iterations,

        params.memory,

        params.threads,

        params.keyLen,

    )



    // Constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks

    return subtle.ConstantTimeCompare(hash, computedHash) == 1, nil

}
// ValidatePasswordStrength enforces password policies

func (ps *PasswordService) ValidatePasswordStrength(password string) error {

  if len(password) < 8 {

      return ErrPasswordTooShort

  }



  if len(password) > 128 {

      return ErrPasswordTooLong

  }



  hasUpper := false

  hasLower := false

  hasDigit := false

  hasSpecial := false



  for _, ch := range password {

      switch {

      case 'A' <= ch && ch <= 'Z':

          hasUpper = true

      case 'a' <= ch && ch <= 'z':

          hasLower = true

      case '0' <= ch && ch <= '9':

          hasDigit = true

      case isSpecialChar(ch):

          hasSpecial = true

      }
      }



      if !hasUpper {

          return ErrPasswordNoUppercase

      }

      if !hasLower {

          return ErrPasswordNoLowercase

      }

      if !hasDigit {

          return ErrPasswordNoDigit

      }

      if !hasSpecial {

          return ErrPasswordNoSpecial

      }



      return nil

}

PART III — TENANT MANAGEMENT



3.1 Tenant Lifecycle State Machine



```
TENANT LIFECYCLE:



                 ┌──────────┐

                 │ CREATED │

                 └────┬─────┘

                   │

                 ┌────▼─────┐

                 │ TRIAL │ (14-day trial)

                 └────┬─────┘

                   │

          ┌──────────┼──────────┐

          │         │      │

        ┌────▼─────┐ ┌──▼───┐ ┌───▼──────┐

        │ ACTIVE │ │EXPIRED│ │CONVERTED │

        └────┬─────┘ └──────┘ └──────────┘

          │

    ┌─────────┼─────────┐

    │        │      │

┌───▼───┐ ┌──▼───┐ ┌───▼──────┐

│SUSPEND│ │DELETE│ │UPGRADE │

│       ││       │ │TIER   │

└───┬───┘ └──────┘ └──────────┘

    │

┌───▼───┐

│ACTIVE │ (reactivate)

└───────┘
TRANSITIONS:

    CREATED → TRIAL:      Automatic on tenant creation

    TRIAL → ACTIVE:      Payment confirmed

    TRIAL → EXPIRED:     14 days without payment

    ACTIVE → SUSPENDED:      Payment failure, TOS violation

    SUSPENDED → ACTIVE:      Issue resolved

    ACTIVE → DELETED:      Account deletion (30-day grace period)

    ACTIVE → UPGRADE:       Tier change (FREE → PRO → ENTERPRISE)

```



3.2 Tenant Isolation Implementation



```go

// internal/infrastructure/persistence/postgres.go

package persistence



import (

      "context"

      "fmt"



      "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5"

)



// TenantContext carries tenant information for database operations

type TenantContext struct {
    TenantID uuid.UUID

}



// SetTenantContext sets the tenant context for the current database session

// This enables Row-Level Security (RLS) to automatically filter queries

func (r *PostgresRepository) SetTenantContext(ctx context.Context, tc TenantContext) error {

    _, err := r.pool.Exec(ctx,

         "SELECT set_config('app.current_tenant_id', $1, true)",

         tc.TenantID.String(),

    )

    if err != nil {

         return fmt.Errorf("set tenant context: %w", err)

    }

    return nil

}



// Example query — RLS automatically adds "WHERE tenant_id =
current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')"

func (r *PostgresRepository) ListUsers(ctx context.Context) ([]*User, error) {

    // RLS ensures only users from the current tenant are returned

    rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, `

         SELECT id, tenant_id, email, display_name, status, roles, created_at

         FROM users

         ORDER BY created_at DESC

    `)

    // ... row scanning
}

3.3 Row-Level Security Policies



```sql

-- migrations/000002_tenant_rls.up.sql



-- Enable RLS on all multi-tenant tables

ALTER TABLE tenants ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

ALTER TABLE users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

ALTER TABLE sessions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

ALTER TABLE api_keys ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;



-- Tenants: Users can only see their own tenant

CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON tenants

      FOR ALL

      USING (id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))

      WITH CHECK (id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true));



-- Users: Filtered by tenant

CREATE POLICY user_tenant_isolation ON users

      FOR ALL

      USING (tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))

      WITH CHECK (tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true));
-- Sessions: Filtered by tenant through user relationship

CREATE POLICY session_tenant_isolation ON sessions

  FOR ALL

  USING (

       user_id IN (

           SELECT id FROM users

           WHERE tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)

       )

  );



-- API Keys: Filtered by tenant

CREATE POLICY apikey_tenant_isolation ON api_keys

  FOR ALL

  USING (tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))

  WITH CHECK (tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true));



-- Admin bypass policy for platform operators

CREATE POLICY admin_bypass ON users

  FOR ALL

  USING (current_setting('app.is_platform_admin', true) = 'true');



-- Create function to set tenant context

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_tenant_context(tenant_id UUID)

RETURNS void AS $$

BEGIN

  PERFORM set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenant_id::text, true);
END;

$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER;

```

// internal/domain/authorization.go

package domain



// AuthorizationService evaluates access policies

type AuthorizationService struct {

      opaClient *opa.Client

      policyStore PolicyStore

      cache     *redis.Client

}



// AuthorizationRequest represents an access check

type AuthorizationRequest struct {
    Subject Subject `json:"subject"`

    Action string `json:"action"`

    Resource Resource `json:"resource"`

    Context Context `json:"context"`

}



type Subject struct {

    UserID string `json:"user_id"`

    TenantID string `json:"tenant_id"`

    Roles    []string `json:"roles"`

}



type Resource struct {

    Type     string `json:"type"`      // "story", "article", "source", "tenant"

    ID      string `json:"id"`      // Resource identifier

    TenantID string `json:"tenant_id"` // Owning tenant

    Attributes map[string]interface{} `json:"attributes,omitempty"`

}



type Context struct {

    IPAddress string `json:"ip_address"`

    UserAgent string `json:"user_agent"`

    Timestamp int64 `json:"timestamp"`

    IsEmergency bool `json:"is_emergency,omitempty"`

}
// AuthorizationResponse represents the authorization decision

type AuthorizationResponse struct {

    Allowed bool      `json:"allowed"`

    Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`

  Obligations []string `json:"obligations,omitempty"` // Required actions (e.g., "LOG_AUDIT",
"NOTIFY_ADMIN")

}



// CheckAuthorization evaluates whether a subject can perform an action on a resource

func (as *AuthorizationService) CheckAuthorization(

    ctx context.Context,

    req *AuthorizationRequest,

) (*AuthorizationResponse, error) {



    // Check cache first

    cacheKey := as.cacheKey(req)

    if cached, err := as.cache.Get(ctx, cacheKey); err == nil {

        var resp AuthorizationResponse

        json.Unmarshal([]byte(cached), &resp)

        return &resp, nil

    }



    // Evaluate OPA policy

    input := map[string]interface{}{

        "subject": req.Subject,

        "action": req.Action,
          "resource": req.Resource,

          "context": req.Context,

      }



      result, err := as.opaClient.Evaluate(ctx, "data.agbofa.authz.allow", input)

      if err != nil {

          return nil, fmt.Errorf("opa evaluation: %w", err)

      }



      resp := &AuthorizationResponse{

          Allowed: result.Allowed,

          Reason: result.Reason,

      }



      if result.Allowed && len(result.Obligations) > 0 {

          resp.Obligations = result.Obligations

      }



      // Cache decision (short TTL for real-time policy updates)

      as.cache.Set(ctx, cacheKey, resp, 30*time.Second)



      return resp, nil

}

```



4.2 OPA Policy Definitions
```rego

# infrastructure/kubernetes/base/opa/policies/authz.rego

package agbofa.authz



import future.keywords.if

import future.keywords.in



# Default deny

default allow := false



# --- Role-Based Access Control ---



# Tenant Admin has full access within their tenant

allow if {

    "TENANT_ADMIN" in input.subject.roles

    input.resource.tenant_id == input.subject.tenant_id

}



# Editor can create and edit content

allow if {

    "EDITOR" in input.subject.roles

    input.resource.tenant_id == input.subject.tenant_id

    input.action in [

      "content:read",

      "content:create",
        "content:update",

        "story:read",

        "story:update",

        "headline:create",

        "media:upload",

    ]

}



# Viewer can only read

allow if {

    "VIEWER" in input.subject.roles

    input.resource.tenant_id == input.subject.tenant_id

    input.action in [

        "content:read",

        "story:read",

        "analytics:read",

    ]

}



# AI Agent permissions

allow if {

    "AI_AGENT" in input.subject.roles

    input.resource.tenant_id == input.subject.tenant_id

    input.action in [

        "story:read",

        "story:detect",
        "content:generate",

        "headline:generate",

        "source:read",

    ]

}



# --- Emergency Override ---



# Emergency access bypass (requires MFA verification)

allow if {

    input.context.is_emergency == true

    input.context.mfa_verified == true

    "EMERGENCY_ACCESS" in input.subject.roles

    # Must log audit event

    obligations := ["LOG_AUDIT", "NOTIFY_SECURITY"]

}



# --- Platform Admin (cross-tenant) ---



allow if {

    "PLATFORM_ADMIN" in input.subject.roles

    # Platform admins have access to all tenants

    obligations := ["LOG_AUDIT"]

}



# --- API Key Access ---
allow if {

      input.subject.type == "API_KEY"

      input.resource.tenant_id == input.subject.tenant_id

      # API key permissions are scoped

      input.action in input.subject.api_key_permissions

}



# --- Resource Ownership ---



# Story authors can manage their own stories

allow if {

      input.action in ["story:update", "story:delete"]

      input.resource.author_id == input.subject.user_id

}



# --- Rate Limiting Obligation ---



obligations["LOG_AUDIT"] if {

      not input.action in ["health:check", "metrics:read"]

}

```
