// tests/chaos/truth_engine/resilience_test.go

package chaos



import (

      "context"

      "testing"

      "time"



      "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

      "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)



func TestTruthEngine_Chaos_ExternalAPIFailure(t *testing.T) {

    ctx := context.Background()



    t.Run("factcheck_api_unavailable", func(t *testing.T) {

      // Setup services

      claimVerifier := setupClaimVerifier(t)



      // Inject failure: block external API

      apiBlocker := NewNetworkBlocker("external-factcheck-api:443")

      apiBlocker.Block()

      defer apiBlocker.Unblock()



      // Verify a claim — should degrade gracefully

      claim := createTestClaim()



      result, err := claimVerifier.VerifyClaim(ctx, claim, testStory)

      require.NoError(t, err, "Should not fail completely when API is down")



      // Should still produce a result using other methods

      assert.NotEmpty(t, result.Verdict)

      assert.Less(t, result.Confidence, 1.0,

        "Confidence should be lower with missing method")

      assert.Contains(t, result.MethodResults, "knowledge_graph",

        "Should fall back to knowledge graph")
     assert.Contains(t, result.MethodResults, "source_analysis",

         "Should fall back to source analysis")

})



t.Run("database_connection_failure", func(t *testing.T) {

     // Setup with circuit breaker

     cb := NewCircuitBreaker(CircuitBreakerConfigs["postgresql"])

     sourceIntel := setupSourceIntelligence(t)



     // Inject failure: kill database connection

     dbBlocker := NewPortBlocker("postgres:5432")

     dbBlocker.Block()

     defer dbBlocker.Unblock()



     // Execute multiple operations to trigger circuit breaker

     for i := 0; i < 5; i++ {

         _, err := sourceIntel.GetSourceReputation(ctx, testSourceID)

         if err != nil {

             // Expected after circuit opens

             assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "circuit breaker")

             break

         }

     }



     // Verify circuit is open

     assert.Equal(t, CircuitOpen, cb.State())
     // Restore database

     dbBlocker.Unblock()

     time.Sleep(15 * time.Second) // Wait for half-open timeout



     // Try again — should recover

     _, err := sourceIntel.GetSourceReputation(ctx, testSourceID)

     require.NoError(t, err, "Should recover after database restored")



     assert.Equal(t, CircuitClosed, cb.State())

})



t.Run("kafka_broker_failure", func(t *testing.T) {

     // Setup

     eventProducer := setupEventProducer(t)



     // Inject failure: kill Kafka broker

     kafkaBlocker := NewPortBlocker("kafka:9092")

     kafkaBlocker.Block()

     defer kafkaBlocker.Unblock()



     // Try to publish events

     event := createTestEvent()



     // Should retry and eventually succeed or fail gracefully

     err := eventProducer.PublishWithRetry(ctx, event)
           // Either succeeds (if retry worked) or fails gracefully

           if err != nil {

               assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "max retries")

           }



           // Verify no data loss: events should be queued

           pendingEvents := eventProducer.GetPendingEventCount(ctx)

           t.Logf("Pending events after Kafka failure: %d", pendingEvents)



           // Restore Kafka

           kafkaBlocker.Unblock()

           time.Sleep(10 * time.Second)



           // Pending events should be delivered

           err = eventProducer.FlushPending(ctx, 30*time.Second)

           require.NoError(t, err, "Pending events should be delivered after recovery")

      })

}

17.8 AI Validation Testing



```go

// tests/ai_validation/truth_engine/accuracy_test.go

package ai_validation
import (

    "context"

    "testing"



    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

)



// TestClaimVerification_Accuracy validates AI verification against known dataset

func TestClaimVerification_Accuracy(t *testing.T) {

    ctx := context.Background()



    // Load labeled test dataset

    dataset, err := LoadLabeledDataset("testdata/verified_claims.jsonl")

    require.NoError(t, err)



    claimVerifier := setupClaimVerifier(t)



    var truePositives, trueNegatives int

    var falsePositives, falseNegatives int



    for _, sample := range dataset {

      claim := sample.ToClaim()



      result, err := claimVerifier.VerifyClaim(ctx, claim, sample.Story)
    require.NoError(t, err)



    predicted := result.Verdict == VerdictTrue || result.Verdict == VerdictMostlyTrue

    actual := sample.IsTrue



    if predicted && actual {

        truePositives++

    } else if !predicted && !actual {

        trueNegatives++

    } else if predicted && !actual {

        falsePositives++

    } else {

        falseNegatives++

    }

}



total := len(dataset)

accuracy := float64(truePositives+trueNegatives) / float64(total)

precision := float64(truePositives) / float64(truePositives+falsePositives)

recall := float64(truePositives) / float64(truePositives+falseNegatives)

f1Score := 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)



t.Logf("AI Validation Results:")

t.Logf(" Total samples: %d", total)

t.Logf(" Accuracy: %.2f%%", accuracy*100)

t.Logf(" Precision: %.2f%%", precision*100)
    t.Logf(" Recall: %.2f%%", recall*100)

    t.Logf(" F1 Score: %.2f", f1Score)

    t.Logf(" True Positives: %d, False Positives: %d", truePositives, falsePositives)

    t.Logf(" True Negatives: %d, False Negatives: %d", trueNegatives, falseNegatives)



    // Quality thresholds

    assert.Greater(t, accuracy, 0.95, "Accuracy should exceed 95%")

    assert.Greater(t, precision, 0.90, "Precision should exceed 90%")

    assert.Greater(t, recall, 0.95, "Recall should exceed 95%")

    assert.Less(t, float64(falsePositives)/float64(total), 0.01,

      "False positive rate should be under 1%")

}



// TestHallucinationDetection validates hallucination detection accuracy

func TestHallucinationDetection(t *testing.T) {

    ctx := context.Background()



    hallucinationDetector := setupHallucinationDetector(t)



    // Load test dataset with known hallucinations

    dataset, err := LoadLabeledDataset("testdata/hallucination_samples.jsonl")

    require.NoError(t, err)



    correct := 0

    total := len(dataset)
      for _, sample := range dataset {

          assessment, err := hallucinationDetector.Assess(

              ctx, sample.Content, sample.Claims, sample.Verifications, sample.SourceInfo,

          )

          require.NoError(t, err)



          detected := assessment.OverallRisk == MisinfoRiskLevelHigh ||

                 assessment.OverallRisk == MisinfoRiskLevelCritical



          if detected == sample.ContainsHallucination {

              correct++

          }

      }



      accuracy := float64(correct) / float64(total)

      t.Logf("Hallucination Detection Accuracy: %.2f%%", accuracy*100)



      assert.Greater(t, accuracy, 0.90, "Hallucination detection accuracy should exceed 90%")

}

 migration_from_mvp:

SERVICE DECISION RECORDS (SDR)
SDR-CF-001: Fact-Locking Before Generation



Decision: All verified facts, quotes, and statistics are extracted into an immutable LockedFactSet
before any content generation begins. All generation prompts include the locked facts as
constraints with explicit "DO NOT MODIFY" instructions.

Rationale: Prevents AI hallucination and ensures factual consistency across all content variants.
The LockedFactSet serves as the single source of truth for all generation.

Alternatives: Real-time fact verification during generation (rejected — latency, inconsistency);
post-generation fact checking (rejected — higher revision cost).

Trade-offs: Additional preprocessing step, but eliminates hallucination risk.



SDR-CF-002: Multi-Pass Generation Pipeline



Decision: Content generation uses a three-pass architecture: structural outline (Pass 1), full draft
(Pass 2), editorial refinement (Pass 3). Each pass is scored by an editorial quality model before
proceeding.

Rationale: Single-pass generation produces inconsistent quality. Multi-pass allows early
detection of structural issues and progressive refinement.

Alternatives: Single-pass generation (rejected — quality issues); iterative human-AI
collaboration (rejected — not scalable).

Trade-offs: Higher token usage (3x), but significantly higher quality output.



SDR-CF-003: Platform-Native Generation (Not Translation)



Decision: Platform-specific content (social posts, video scripts) is generated natively using
platform-aware prompts rather than generating once and adapting.

Rationale: True platform-native content requires different narrative structures, tones, and
conventions. Translation/adaptation produces inferior results.
Alternatives: Generate canonical version, then adapt (partially adopted for efficiency in breaking
news MVP).

Trade-offs: More LLM calls, but significantly better platform engagement.



SDR-CF-004: Model Tiering for Cost Optimization



Decision: Route generation tasks to models based on content criticality: Claude-3-Opus for full
articles and sensitive content, Claude-3-Sonnet for standard generation, Claude-3-Haiku for
headlines/SEO/social posts.

Rationale: Full articles require highest quality; headlines and social posts can use faster, cheaper
models. Tiering reduces costs by 40-60% without quality degradation.

Alternatives: Single model for everything (rejected — cost prohibitive at scale); open-source
only (rejected — quality gap).

Trade-offs: Multiple model management, but significant cost savings.

```

CONTENT GENERATION LIFECYCLE:



                   ┌──────────┐

                   │ STORY │ Verified story received

                   │ RECEIVED │ from Truth Engine

                   └────┬─────┘

                     │

               ┌─────────▼─────────┐

               │ FACT LOCKING │ Extract immutable facts

               └────────┬──────────┘

                     │

               ┌────────▼────────┐

               │ PLANNING       │ Determine content types, formats

               └────────┬────────┘

                     │
   ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐

   │           │           │

┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌──────▼──────┐

│ ARTICLE │ │ MULTIMEDIA │ │ PLATFORM │

│ GENERATION │ │ GENERATION │ │ ADAPTATION │

└──────┬──────┘ └──────┬──────┘ └──────┬──────┘

   │           │           │

   └───────────────────┼───────────────────┘

               │

           ┌────────▼────────┐

           │ QUALITY CHECK │

           └────────┬────────┘

               │

       ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐

       │       │       │

  ┌──────▼──────┐ ┌─────▼─────┐ ┌─────▼─────┐

  │ PASSED │ │ RETRY │ │ REJECTED │

  └──────┬──────┘ └─────┬─────┘ └───────────┘

       │       │

       │   ┌────────▼────────┐

       │   │ AUTO-CORRECT │──    Regenerate failed sections

       │   └─────────────────┘

       │

  ┌──────▼──────┐

  │ PACKAGING │

  └──────┬──────┘
          │

      ┌──────▼──────┐

      │ DISTRIBUTION│──   Distribution Engine (Vol 17)

      │ HANDOFF │

      └─────────────┘



STATES:

 STORY_RECEIVED → FACT_LOCKING → PLANNING → GENERATING → QUALITY_CHECK

 → PASSED | RETRYING | REJECTED → PACKAGING → READY → DISTRIBUTED



RETRY LOGIC:

 QUALITY_CHECK failed → RETRYING (max 3 attempts)

 RETRYING → Auto-correct specific issues → QUALITY_CHECK

 After 3 failures → REJECTED (human review required)

```

2.2 Fact Locker Implementation



```go

// services/content-factory/content-assembler/internal/domain/fact_locker.go

package domain



// FactLocker extracts and cryptographically seals all verified facts

type FactLocker struct {

      truthEngine TruthEngineClient

      storyGraph StoryGraphClient
}



// LockFacts creates an immutable fact set for generation

func (fl *FactLocker) LockFacts(ctx context.Context, storyID uuid.UUID) (*LockedFactSet, error) {



    // 1. Retrieve verified story from Truth Engine

    verifiedStory, err := fl.truthEngine.GetVerifiedStory(ctx, storyID)

    if err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("get verified story: %w", err)

    }



    // 2. Verify story has passed Truth Engine verification

    if verifiedStory.VerificationStatus != "VERIFIED" {

        return nil, ErrStoryNotVerified

    }



    locked := &LockedFactSet{

        LockID: uuid.NewV7().String(),

        StoryID: storyID,

        LockedAt: time.Now(),

    }



    // 3. Extract core facts (5W1H)

    locked.CoreFacts = fl.extractCoreFacts(verifiedStory)



    // 4. Lock verified claims — MUST NOT be altered
locked.VerifiedClaims = fl.lockClaims(verifiedStory.VerifiedClaims)



// 5. Lock quotes VERBATIM

locked.AttributedQuotes = fl.lockQuotes(verifiedStory.Quotes)



// 6. Lock statistics with exact values

locked.Statistics = fl.lockStatistics(verifiedStory.Statistics)



// 7. Lock entity references with canonical names

locked.Entities = fl.lockEntities(verifiedStory.Entities)



// 8. Lock timeline events in chronological order

locked.Timeline = fl.lockTimeline(verifiedStory.Timeline)



// 9. Lock source attributions

locked.SourceAttributions = fl.lockAttributions(verifiedStory.Sources)



// 10. Generate required attributions based on sources

locked.RequiredAttributions = fl.generateRequiredAttributions(verifiedStory)



// 11. Generate forbidden phrases (clickbait, sensationalism)

locked.ForbiddenPhrases = fl.generateForbiddenPhrases(verifiedStory)



// 12. Calculate cryptographic hash for integrity verification

locked.Hash = fl.calculateHash(locked)
      return locked, nil

}



func (fl *FactLocker) lockQuotes(quotes []VerifiedQuote) []LockedQuote {

      locked := make([]LockedQuote, len(quotes))

      for i, q := range quotes {

          locked[i] = LockedQuote{

              QuoteID:        q.ID,

              QuoteText:      q.Text,    // VERBATIM — exact text preserved

              AttributedTo:    q.AttributedTo,

              Attribution:    q.Attribution, // Exact attribution preserved

              CannotBeParaphrased: true,         // CRITICAL: quotes cannot be paraphrased

          }

      }

      return locked

}



func (fl *FactLocker) calculateHash(facts *LockedFactSet) string {

      // Create canonical representation for hashing

      data, _ := json.Marshal(facts.CoreFacts)

      data = append(data, []byte(facts.LockedAt.String())...)



      hash := sha256.Sum256(data)

      return hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])

}

// CreatePlan generates a content generation plan for a story

func (gp *GenerationPlanner) CreatePlan(

    ctx context.Context,

    story *VerifiedStory,

    lockedFacts *LockedFactSet,

    overrides *PlanOverrides,

) (*GenerationPlan, error) {
// Determine story archetype

archetype := gp.classifyArchetype(story)



// Get archetype rules

rules := ArchetypeRulesConfig[archetype]



plan := &GenerationPlan{

    PlanID:        uuid.NewV7(),

    StoryID:       story.ID,

    StoryArchetype: archetype,

    ContentTypes: rules.DefaultContentTypes,

    TargetPlatforms: rules.DefaultPlatforms,

    TargetLanguages: []string{story.Language}, // Source language default

    ToneProfile:     rules.RecommendedTone,

    ModelTier:       rules.ModelTier,

    Priority:      rules.Priority,

    CreatedAt:       time.Now(),

}



// Apply overrides

if overrides != nil {

    if len(overrides.AdditionalContentTypes) > 0 {

        plan.ContentTypes = append(plan.ContentTypes, overrides.AdditionalContentTypes...)

    }

    if len(overrides.TargetLanguages) > 0 {
            plan.TargetLanguages = append(plan.TargetLanguages, overrides.TargetLanguages...)

        }

        if overrides.ModelTier != "" {

            plan.ModelTier = overrides.ModelTier

        }

    }



    // For breaking news, add translation if global story

    if archetype == ArchetypeBreakingNews && story.GeographicScope == "GLOBAL" {

        plan.TargetLanguages = append(plan.TargetLanguages, "es", "fr", "ar", "zh")

    }



    return plan, nil

}



func (gp *GenerationPlanner) classifyArchetype(story *VerifiedStory) StoryArchetype {

    switch {

    case story.State == "BREAKING" && time.Since(story.CreatedAt) < 2*time.Hour:

        return ArchetypeBreakingNews

    case story.State == "DEVELOPING":

        return ArchetypeDevelopingStory

    case story.Category == "EXPLAINER" || story.Category == "SCIENCE":

        return ArchetypeExplainer

    case story.Category == "INVESTIGATIVE":

        return ArchetypeInvestigative

    case story.Category == "HUMAN_INTEREST":
          return ArchetypeHumanInterest

      case story.IsLiveBlog:

          return ArchetypeLiveBlog

      default:

          return ArchetypeFeatureAnalysis

      }

}

// services/content-factory/content-assembler/internal/application/orchestrator.go

package application



// ContentOrchestrator coordinates the entire content generation pipeline

type ContentOrchestrator struct {

      factLocker     *domain.FactLocker

      planner       *domain.GenerationPlanner

      articleGen     ArticleGeneratorClient

      headlineGen      HeadlineGeneratorClient

      summaryGen        SummaryGeneratorClient

      seoEngine       SEOEngineClient

      multimediaFactory MultimediaFactoryClient

      socialGen      SocialContentGeneratorClient

      translationSvc TranslationServiceClient
    brandVoice       BrandVoiceClient

    qualityAssurance QualityAssuranceClient

    packager        ContentPackagerClient

    jobRepo         JobRepository

    eventBus        EventBus

}



// ProcessStory orchestrates the full content generation pipeline

func (co *ContentOrchestrator) ProcessStory(

    ctx context.Context,

    storyID uuid.UUID,

    overrides *domain.PlanOverrides,

) (*domain.ContentJob, error) {



    startTime := time.Now()



    // Create job

    job := &domain.ContentJob{

        JobID: uuid.NewV7(),

        StoryID: storyID,

        Status: domain.JobStatusReceived,

        CreatedAt: time.Now(),

    }



    co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)
// Phase 1: Lock Facts

lockedFacts, err := co.factLocker.LockFacts(ctx, storyID)

if err != nil {

    job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

    co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("fact locking: %w", err)

}

job.LockedFacts = lockedFacts



// Phase 2: Create Generation Plan

plan, err := co.planner.CreatePlan(ctx, storyID, lockedFacts, overrides)

if err != nil {

    job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

    co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("planning: %w", err)

}

job.GenerationPlan = plan

job.Status = domain.JobStatusPlanning

co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)



// Phase 3: Parallel Generation

job.Status = domain.JobStatusGenerating

co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)



content := &domain.ContentPackage{

    PackageID: uuid.NewV7(),
    StoryID: storyID,

}



// Launch all generation tasks in parallel

var wg sync.WaitGroup

var mu sync.Mutex

errors := make(chan error, len(plan.ContentTypes))



for _, ct := range plan.ContentTypes {

    wg.Add(1)

    go func(contentType domain.ContentType) {

      defer wg.Done()



      result, err := co.generateContent(ctx, contentType, storyID, lockedFacts, plan)

      if err != nil {

            errors <- fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", contentType, err)

            return

      }



      mu.Lock()

      co.mergeContent(content, contentType, result)

      mu.Unlock()

    }(ct)

}



wg.Wait()
close(errors)



// Check for errors

var genErrors []error

for err := range errors {

    genErrors = append(genErrors, err)

}



if len(genErrors) > 0 && len(genErrors) == len(plan.ContentTypes) {

    // All generation failed

    job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

    co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("all generation failed: %v", genErrors)

}



job.ContentPackage = content



// Phase 4: Quality Assurance

job.Status = domain.JobStatusQualityCheck

co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)



qaResult, err := co.qualityAssurance.RunFullQA(ctx, content, lockedFacts)

if err != nil {

    job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

    co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

    return nil, fmt.Errorf("QA failed: %w", err)
}



if !qaResult.Passed {

    // Retry failed components

    if qaResult.RetryableIssues > 0 {

        job.Status = domain.JobStatusRetrying

        co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)



        // Auto-correct and retry

        content, err = co.autoCorrectAndRetry(ctx, content, qaResult, lockedFacts, plan)

        if err != nil {

            job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

            co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

            return nil, fmt.Errorf("retry failed: %w", err)

        }

    } else {

        job.Status = domain.JobStatusRejected

        co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("QA critical issues: %v", qaResult.CriticalIssues)

    }

}



// Phase 5: Packaging

job.Status = domain.JobStatusPackaging

packagedContent, err := co.packager.Package(ctx, content, plan)

if err != nil {
           return nil, fmt.Errorf("packaging: %w", err)

      }

      job.ContentPackage = packagedContent



      job.Status = domain.JobStatusReady

      job.CompletedAt = timePtr(time.Now())

      co.jobRepo.Save(ctx, job)



      // Publish event

      co.eventBus.Publish(ctx, &ContentReadyEvent{

           JobID:     job.JobID,

           StoryID:   storyID,

           PackageID: packagedContent.PackageID,

           ContentTypes: plan.ContentTypes,

           Duration: time.Since(startTime),

           GeneratedAt: time.Now(),

      })



      return job, nil

}

```

3.1 Multi-Pass Article Generation



```python

# services/content-factory/article-generator/src/generator/pipeline.py

"""

Multi-Pass Article Generation Pipeline.

Pass 1: Structure & Outline

Pass 2: Full Draft

Pass 3: Editorial Refinement

"""



from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any

from enum import Enum

import structlog



logger = structlog.get_logger(__name__)




class ArticleArchetype(Enum):

  BREAKING_NEWS = "BREAKING_NEWS"

  FEATURE_ANALYSIS = "FEATURE_ANALYSIS"
  EXPLAINER = "EXPLAINER"

  INVESTIGATIVE = "INVESTIGATIVE"

  HUMAN_INTEREST = "HUMAN_INTEREST"

  LIVE_BLOG = "LIVE_BLOG"




@dataclass

class ArticleOutline:

  """Generated article structure."""

  headline_candidates: List[str]

  sections: List[SectionPlan]

  key_takeaways: List[str]

  flow: str # Narrative flow description



@dataclass

class SectionPlan:

  section_id: str

  heading: str

  purpose: str # What this section should accomplish

  key_facts_to_include: List[str]

  quotes_to_include: List[str]

  target_word_count: int

  order: int




@dataclass
class GeneratedArticle:

  """Complete generated article."""

  article_id: str

  story_id: str

  archetype: ArticleArchetype

  headlines: List[str]

  summary: str

  sections: List[ArticleSection]

  word_count: int

  reading_time_minutes: int

  quotes_included: List[str]

  sources_cited: List[str]

  generation_metadata: Dict[str, Any]

  quality_scores: Dict[str, float]




class ArticleGenerationPipeline:

  """Three-pass article generation system."""



  def __init__(self, llm_gateway, prompt_library, quality_scorer, brand_voice):

    self.llm = llm_gateway

    self.prompts = prompt_library

    self.scorer = quality_scorer

    self.brand_voice = brand_voice



  async def generate_article(
  self,

  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

  plan: GenerationPlan,

  config: ArticleConfig,

) -> GeneratedArticle:

  """

  Generate article using three-pass architecture.

  """



  article_id = str(uuid.uuid4())



  # ============================================================

  # PASS 1: Generate Structure & Outline

  # ============================================================

  logger.info("pass1_outline_generation", article_id=article_id)



  outline = await self.generate_outline(locked_facts, plan, config)



  # Score outline quality

  outline_score = await self.scorer.score_outline(outline, plan)

  if outline_score < config.min_outline_score:

    logger.warning("outline_score_low", score=outline_score)

    # Retry with adjusted parameters

    outline = await self.retry_outline(locked_facts, plan, config)



  # ============================================================
# PASS 2: Generate Full Draft

# ============================================================

logger.info("pass2_draft_generation", article_id=article_id)



sections = await self.generate_sections_parallel(

    locked_facts, outline, plan, config

)



# Verify fact adherence

fact_check = await self.verify_fact_adherence(sections, locked_facts)

if not fact_check.passes:

    logger.warning("fact_adherence_failed", violations=len(fact_check.violations))

    # Regenerate violating sections

    sections = await self.correct_fact_violations(

        sections, fact_check.violations, locked_facts, plan, config

    )



# ============================================================

# PASS 3: Editorial Refinement

# ============================================================

logger.info("pass3_editorial_refinement", article_id=article_id)



refined_sections = await self.refine_article(

    sections, locked_facts, plan, config

)
# Apply brand voice

branded_sections = await self.brand_voice.apply(

    refined_sections, plan.PublicationID

)



# Generate headlines based on completed article

headlines = await self.generate_headlines_from_article(

    branded_sections, locked_facts, config

)



# Generate summary

summary = await self.generate_summary(

    branded_sections, locked_facts, config

)



# Final quality scoring

final_scores = await self.scorer.score_final_article(

    branded_sections, headlines, summary, locked_facts

)



article = GeneratedArticle(

    article_id=article_id,

    story_id=locked_facts.story_id,

    archetype=plan.story_archetype,

    headlines=headlines,

    summary=summary,
      sections=branded_sections,

      word_count=sum(s.word_count for s in branded_sections),

      reading_time_minutes=self.calculate_reading_time(branded_sections),

      quotes_included=self.extract_included_quotes(branded_sections),

      sources_cited=self.extract_cited_sources(branded_sections),

      generation_metadata={

           "model": config.model,

           "passes": 3,

           "tokens_used": self.llm.get_token_count(),

           "generation_time_ms": self.get_elapsed_ms(),

      },

      quality_scores=final_scores,

  )



  return article



async def generate_outline(

  self,

  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

  plan: GenerationPlan,

  config: ArticleConfig,

) -> ArticleOutline:

  """PASS 1: Generate article structure and outline."""



  prompt = self.prompts.get_outline_prompt(

      locked_facts=locked_facts,
      archetype=plan.story_archetype,

      tone=plan.tone_profile,

      target_length=config.target_word_count,

  )



  response = await self.llm.generate(

      prompt=prompt,

      model=config.model or "claude-3-sonnet",

      temperature=0.3, # Lower temperature for structure

      max_tokens=2000,

      response_format={"type": "json_object"},

  )



  outline = ArticleOutline.parse(response)



  # Validate outline includes all must-include facts

  self.validate_outline_coverage(outline, locked_facts)



  return outline



async def generate_section(

  self,

  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

  section_plan: SectionPlan,

  outline: ArticleOutline,

  plan: GenerationPlan,
  config: ArticleConfig,

) -> ArticleSection:

  """PASS 2: Generate a single article section."""



  # Get context from previous sections

  previous_context = self.get_previous_section_summaries(

      outline, section_plan

  )



  prompt = self.prompts.get_section_prompt(

      locked_facts=locked_facts,

      section_plan=section_plan,

      previous_context=previous_context,

      tone=plan.tone_profile,

      target_words=section_plan.target_word_count,

  )



  # Inject CRITICAL constraints

  prompt += f"""



       CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS — VIOLATION WILL CAUSE REGENERATION:



  1. ONLY use facts from the provided fact set above

  2. DO NOT invent, embellish, or assume any facts

  3. Quotes MUST be reproduced VERBATIM exactly as provided

  4. All statistics MUST match exactly as provided
  5. All attributions MUST use the exact attribution text provided

  6. If a fact is not in the fact set, write "according to available information"

      rather than fabricating details

  7. DO NOT use any of these phrases: {', '.join(locked_facts.forbidden_phrases[:10])}

  """



  response = await self.llm.generate(

      prompt=prompt,

      model=config.model or "claude-3-sonnet",

      temperature=config.creativity or 0.7,

      max_tokens=section_plan.target_word_count * 3,

  )



  section = ArticleSection(

      section_id=section_plan.section_id,

      heading=section_plan.heading,

      content=response.text,

      word_count=len(response.text.split()),

      order=section_plan.order,

  )



  return section



async def refine_article(

  self,

  sections: List[ArticleSection],
  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

  plan: GenerationPlan,

  config: ArticleConfig,

) -> List[ArticleSection]:

  """PASS 3: Editorial refinement of the full article."""



  full_draft = self.assemble_draft(sections)



  prompt = self.prompts.get_refinement_prompt(

      draft=full_draft,

      locked_facts=locked_facts,

      tone=plan.tone_profile,

      publication_style=plan.publication_style,

  )



  response = await self.llm.generate(

      prompt=prompt,

      model="claude-3-opus", # Best model for refinement

      temperature=0.3,

      max_tokens=4000,

  )



  # Parse refined sections from response

  refined_sections = self.parse_refined_sections(response, sections)



  return refined_sections
```



3.2 Fact Adherence Verification



```python

# services/content-factory/article-generator/src/generator/fact_checker.py

"""

Fact adherence verification — ensures generated content doesn't deviate from locked facts.

"""



class FactAdherenceChecker:

      """Verifies generated content matches locked facts exactly."""



      async def verify_fact_adherence(

        self,

        sections: List[ArticleSection],

        locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

      ) -> FactAdherenceReport:

        """Check all generated content against locked facts."""



        report = FactAdherenceReport()

        full_text = " ".join([s.content for s in sections])



        # Check 1: All must-include facts present

        for fact in locked_facts.core_facts:

          if fact.must_include:
    found = self.find_fact_in_text(fact, full_text)

    if not found:

      report.add_violation(FactViolation(

           severity="CRITICAL",

           fact_id=fact.fact_id,

           issue="MISSING_REQUIRED_FACT",

           detail=f"Required fact not found: {fact.fact_text[:100]}",

      ))



# Check 2: All quotes are verbatim

for quote in locked_facts.attributed_quotes:

  if quote.cannot_be_paraphrased:

    exact_match = self.verify_quote_verbatim(quote.quote_text, full_text)

    if not exact_match:

      report.add_violation(FactViolation(

           severity="CRITICAL",

           quote_id=quote.quote_id,

           issue="QUOTE_ALTERED",

           detail=f"Quote text modified from verified original",

      ))



# Check 3: No hallucinated claims (claims not in locked facts)

generated_claims = await self.extract_claims_from_text(full_text)

for claim in generated_claims:

  if not self.claim_in_locked_set(claim, locked_facts):

    report.add_violation(FactViolation(
         severity="CRITICAL",

         issue="HALLUCINATED_CLAIM",

         detail=f"Claim not in verified fact set: {claim[:100]}",

    ))



# Check 4: Required attributions present

for attr in locked_facts.required_attributions:

  if attr.lower() not in full_text.lower():

    report.add_violation(FactViolation(

         severity="HIGH",

         issue="MISSING_ATTRIBUTION",

         detail=f"Required attribution missing: {attr}",

    ))



# Check 5: Forbidden phrases absent

for phrase in locked_facts.forbidden_phrases:

  if phrase.lower() in full_text.lower():

    report.add_violation(FactViolation(

         severity="MEDIUM",

         issue="FORBIDDEN_PHRASE",

         detail=f"Forbidden phrase found: {phrase}",

    ))



report.passes = len([v for v in report.violations if v.severity == "CRITICAL"]) == 0



return report
```

4.1 Headline Generation Engine



```python

# services/content-factory/headline-engine/src/generator/headline_engine.py

"""

Headline Intelligence Engine — Generates multiple headline variants

optimized for different platforms and purposes.

"""



class HeadlineGenerationEngine:

  """Generates platform-optimized headlines with factual constraint enforcement."""



  HEADLINE_TYPES = {

      "primary": {

           "max_chars": 100,

           "purpose": "Main article headline",

           "requirements": ["include_key_entity", "include_key_action", "informative"],

           "forbidden": ["clickbait", "question_format_unless_investigative"],

      },

      "seo": {

           "max_chars": 70,
     "purpose": "Search engine optimization",

     "requirements": ["primary_keyword_frontloaded", "include_entity", "descriptive"],

     "forbidden": ["keyword_stuffing"],

},

"social_twitter": {

     "max_chars": 100,

     "purpose": "X (Twitter) engagement",

     "requirements": ["hook_first", "entity_prominent", "shareable"],

     "forbidden": ["misleading_truncation"],

},

"social_facebook": {

     "max_chars": 100,

     "purpose": "Facebook engagement",

     "requirements": ["conversational", "entity_prominent"],

     "forbidden": ["engagement_bait"],

},

"mobile": {

     "max_chars": 60,

     "purpose": "Mobile app notification",

     "requirements": ["concise", "entity_prominent"],

     "forbidden": ["truncation_likely"],

},

"push_notification": {

     "max_chars": 65,

     "purpose": "Push notification",

     "requirements": ["urgency_if_breaking", "key_takeaway", "action_driving"],
         "forbidden": ["vague", "clickbait"],

    },

}



async def generate_headlines(

    self,

    locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

    article: Optional[GeneratedArticle],

    plan: GenerationPlan,

    requested_types: List[str],

) -> List[Headline]:

    """Generate headline variants for all requested types."""



    headlines = []



    for headline_type in requested_types:

         rules = self.HEADLINE_TYPES.get(headline_type)

         if not rules:

            continue



         # Generate multiple candidates

         candidates = await self.generate_candidates(

            locked_facts=locked_facts,

            article=article,

            headline_type=headline_type,

            rules=rules,
       count=5,

  )



  # Score each candidate

  scored = []

  for candidate in candidates:

       scores = await self.score_headline(

           candidate, locked_facts, rules, headline_type

       )

       scored.append((candidate, scores))



  # Select best

  scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[1].overall_score, reverse=True)

  best_text, best_scores = scored[0]



  headlines.append(Headline(

       headline_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),

       text=best_text,

       headline_type=headline_type,

       character_count=len(best_text),

       scores=best_scores,

       alternatives=[t for t, _ in scored[1:3]],

  ))



return headlines
async def score_headline(

  self,

  headline: str,

  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

  rules: dict,

  headline_type: str,

) -> HeadlineScores:

  """Score a headline across multiple dimensions."""



  scores = HeadlineScores()



  # 1. Factual accuracy (CRITICAL — must not distort facts)

  scores.factual_accuracy = await self.check_factual_accuracy(headline, locked_facts)



  # 2. Clickbait detection (lower is better)

  scores.clickbait_risk = self.detect_clickbait(headline)



  # 3. Entity inclusion

  scores.entity_coverage = self.check_entity_inclusion(headline, locked_facts)



  # 4. Readability

  scores.readability = self.calculate_readability(headline)



  # 5. Length compliance

  scores.length_compliance = 1.0 if len(headline) <= rules["max_chars"] else 0.5
  # 6. Click-through prediction (ML model)

  scores.predicted_ctr = await self.predict_ctr(headline, headline_type)



  # 7. Forbidden pattern check

  scores.forbidden_check = self.check_forbidden_patterns(

      headline, rules.get("forbidden", [])

  )



  # Weighted overall score

  scores.overall_score = (

      scores.factual_accuracy * 0.35 +       # Highest weight

      (1.0 - scores.clickbait_risk) * 0.20 +

      scores.entity_coverage * 0.15 +

      scores.readability * 0.10 +

      scores.length_compliance * 0.05 +

      scores.predicted_ctr * 0.10 +

      scores.forbidden_check * 0.05

  )



  return scores



def detect_clickbait(self, headline: str) -> float:

  """Detect clickbait patterns. Returns 0-1 risk score."""



  clickbait_patterns = [

      (r"you won'?t believe", 0.9),
          (r"what happens next", 0.8),

          (r"this will shock you", 0.9),

          (r"mind.?\s*blowing", 0.7),

          (r"doctors hate", 0.9),

          (r"one weird trick", 0.9),

          (r"secret .+ don'?t want you to know", 0.8),

          (r"number \d+ will", 0.7),

          (r"changed my life", 0.6),

          (r"you need to see", 0.5),

      ]



      risk = 0.0

      headline_lower = headline.lower()



      for pattern, weight in clickbait_patterns:

          if re.search(pattern, headline_lower):

            risk = max(risk, weight)



      return risk

```

# services/content-factory/brand-voice/src/enforcer/voice.py

"""
Brand Voice Service — Enforces editorial style and tone consistency.

"""



class BrandVoiceEnforcer:

  """Enforces publication-specific brand voice and style guide rules."""



  def __init__(self, publication_configs: Dict[str, PublicationStyle]):

      self.publications = publication_configs

      self.grammar_checker = GrammarChecker()

      self.tone_analyzer = ToneAnalyzer()

      self.readability_scorer = ReadabilityScorer()

      self.banned_terms = self.load_banned_terms()



  async def apply(

      self,

      content: str,

      publication_id: str,

      content_type: str,

  ) -> Tuple[str, VoiceComplianceReport]:

      """Apply brand voice rules and return compliance report."""



      config = self.publications[publication_id]

      report = VoiceComplianceReport()



      # 1. Grammar check and correction

      grammar_issues = self.grammar_checker.check(content)
if grammar_issues:

  content = self.grammar_checker.correct(content)

  report.grammar_corrections = len(grammar_issues)



# 2. Style guide enforcement

content = self.apply_style_rules(content, config.style_rules)



# 3. Tone verification and adjustment

expected_tone = config.content_tones.get(content_type)

if expected_tone:

  actual_tone = self.tone_analyzer.analyze(content)

  if actual_tone.dominant != expected_tone:

    content = await self.adjust_tone(content, actual_tone, expected_tone)

    report.tone_adjusted = True



# 4. Banned term replacement

found_banned = self.check_banned_terms(content)

for term, alternative in found_banned.items():

  content = content.replace(term, alternative)

report.banned_terms_replaced = len(found_banned)



# 5. Readability optimization

readability = self.readability_scorer.score(content)

target = config.readability_targets.get(content_type, 60)

if readability < target:

  content = await self.improve_readability(content, target)
     report.readability_improved = True



  # 6. Calculate compliance score

  report.compliance_score = self.calculate_compliance(report, config)



  return content, report



async def adjust_tone(

  self,

  content: str,

  current: ToneAnalysis,

  target: str,

) -> str:

  """Adjust content tone to match target using LLM."""



  prompt = f"""

  Adjust the following text to match the target tone profile.

  Maintain all factual information exactly.

  Do not add or remove any facts.



  CURRENT TONE: {current.dominant} (confidence: {current.confidence})

  TARGET TONE: {target}



  TEXT:

  {content}
  ADJUSTED TEXT:

  """



  response = await self.llm.generate(

      prompt=prompt,

      model="claude-3-haiku",

      temperature=0.2,

  )



  return response.text



# Style rules for a publication

def apply_style_rules(self, content: str, rules: StyleRules) -> str:

  """Apply editorial style rules."""



  if rules.oxford_comma:

      content = self.ensure_oxford_commas(content)



  if rules.em_dash_spacing == "no_spaces":

      content = self.fix_em_dash_spacing(content)



  if rules.quote_style == "double":

      content = self.normalize_quotes(content, "double")



  if rules.numbers_under_10 == "spell_out":

      content = self.spell_out_numbers(content, threshold=10)
      if rules.percentages == "symbol":

        content = self.normalize_percentages(content, use_symbol=True)



      if rules.attribution_verb == "said":

        content = self.normalize_attribution_verbs(content, preferred="said")



      return content

async def translate_content(

  self,

  content: ContentPackage,

  target_languages: List[str],

  config: TranslationConfig,

) -> Dict[str, TranslatedContent]:

  """Translate all content components to target languages."""



  translations = {}



  # Translate in parallel

  tasks = []

  for lang in target_languages:

    if lang == content.source_language:

          continue

    task = self.translate_single_language(content, lang, config)

    tasks.append((lang, task))



  for lang, task in tasks:

    try:

          translated = await task

          translations[lang] = translated

    except Exception as e:

          logger.error("translation_failed", language=lang, error=str(e))



  return translations
async def translate_single_language(

  self,

  content: ContentPackage,

  target_lang: str,

  config: TranslationConfig,

) -> TranslatedContent:

  """Translate all content components to a single language."""



  # Get language-specific glossary

  glossary = self.terminology.get_glossary(target_lang)



  # Translate article

  translated_article = await self.translate_article(

      content.article, target_lang, glossary

  )



  # Translate headlines (preserve entity names where appropriate)

  translated_headlines = await self.translate_headlines(

      content.headlines, target_lang, glossary

  )



  # Translate summary

  translated_summary = await self.translate_summary(

      content.summary, target_lang, glossary

  )
# Cultural adaptation

adapted_article = await self.cultural_adaptation(

    translated_article, target_lang, content.category

)



# Quality check

quality_report = await self.quality.check_translation(

    original=content,

    translated=adapted_article,

    target_lang=target_lang,

)



if quality_report.score < config.minimum_quality:

    if config.retry_on_low_quality:

      return await self.translate_single_language(content, target_lang, config)

    quality_report.requires_human_review = True



return TranslatedContent(

    translation_id=str(uuid.uuid4()),

    target_language=target_lang,

    article=adapted_article,

    headlines=translated_headlines,

    summary=translated_summary,

    quality_report=quality_report,

)
      async def cultural_adaptation(

        self,

        content: str,

        target_lang: str,

        category: str,

      ) -> str:

        """Adapt content for cultural context of target language."""



        cultural_rules = self.get_cultural_rules(target_lang, category)



        # Replace culturally-specific references

        content = self.replace_cultural_references(content, target_lang, cultural_rules)



        # Adjust measurements/units

        content = self.localize_measurements(content, target_lang)

// GenerateSocialPost creates a platform-optimized social media post

func (scg *SocialContentGenerator) GenerateSocialPost(

    ctx context.Context,

    lockedFacts *LockedFactSet,

    article *GeneratedArticle,
  platform string,

) (*SocialPost, error) {



  rules, exists := PlatformRulesConfig[platform]

  if !exists {

       return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown platform: %s", platform)

  }



  // Build platform-specific prompt

  prompt := scg.buildPlatformPrompt(lockedFacts, article, platform, rules)



  // Generate post text

  response, err := scg.llmGateway.Generate(ctx, LLMRequest{

       Prompt:      prompt,

       Model:       "claude-3-haiku",

       Temperature: 0.5,

       MaxTokens: 300,

  })

  if err != nil {

       return nil, fmt.Errorf("LLM generation: %w", err)

  }



  postText := response.Text



  // Enforce character limit

  if len(postText) > rules.MaxChars {
          postText = scg.truncateIntelligently(postText, rules.MaxChars)

      }



      // Generate hashtags

      hashtags := scg.hashtagEngine.GenerateForPlatform(

          lockedFacts, article, platform, rules.MaxHashtags,

      )



      // Build final post

      post := &SocialPost{

          PostID: uuid.NewV7().String(),

          Platform: platform,

          Text:   postText,

          Hashtags: hashtags,

          URL:    article.CanonicalURL,

          MediaURLs: scg.selectMediaForPlatform(article.MediaURLs, platform),

          GeneratedAt: time.Now(),

      }



      return post, nil

}

```python

# services/content-factory/quality-assurance/src/qa/pipeline.py

"""

AI Quality Assurance Pipeline — Validates all generated content

before packaging and distribution.

"""



class QualityAssurancePipeline:

      """Multi-stage quality validation for AI-generated content."""



      def __init__(self):

           self.checks = [
      FactConsistencyCheck(),

      HallucinationDetectionCheck(),

      GrammarCheck(),

      StyleComplianceCheck(),

      PlagiarismCheck(),

      ToxicityCheck(),

      BiasCheck(),

      ReadabilityCheck(),

      QuoteAccuracyCheck(),

      AttributionCheck(),

      SEOValidationCheck(),

  ]



async def run_full_qa(

  self,

  content: ContentPackage,

  locked_facts: LockedFactSet,

) -> QualityReport:

  """Run all QA checks on generated content."""



  report = QualityReport(content_id=content.package_id)



  # Run all checks in parallel

  tasks = [check.run(content, locked_facts) for check in self.checks]

  results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
critical_issues = []

high_issues = []



for i, result in enumerate(results):

  if isinstance(result, Exception):

     report.add_error(f"Check {self.checks[i].__class__.__name__} failed: {result}")

     continue



  report.add_check_result(result)



  if not result.passes:

     if result.severity == "CRITICAL":

       critical_issues.append(result)

     elif result.severity == "HIGH":

       high_issues.append(result)



# Determine pass/fail

report.passes = len(critical_issues) == 0

report.retryable = len(high_issues) > 0 and len(critical_issues) == 0



# Calculate overall score

report.overall_score = self.calculate_overall_score(report)



# Generate publication readiness

report.publication_ready = (

  report.passes and
      report.overall_score >= 85.0

  )



  return report



def calculate_overall_score(self, report: QualityReport) -> float:

  """Calculate weighted overall quality score."""



  weights = {

      "fact_consistency": 0.30,

      "hallucination_detection": 0.25,

      "grammar": 0.10,

      "style_compliance": 0.10,

      "plagiarism": 0.10,

      "toxicity": 0.05,

      "bias": 0.05,

      "readability": 0.03,

      "quote_accuracy": 0.02,

  }



  total = 0.0

  total_weight = 0.0



  for check_result in report.check_results:

      weight = weights.get(check_result.check_name, 0.01)

      total += check_result.score * weight
          total_weight += weight



        if total_weight == 0:

          return 0.0



        return total / total_weight

```

SERVICE DECISION RECORDS (SDR)
SDR-STG-001: Neo4j as Primary Story Graph Database



Decision: Use Neo4j Enterprise 5.x as the primary Story Graph database with causal clustering
for high availability. PostgreSQL stores operational metadata; MongoDB stores full content
snapshots.

Rationale: Neo4j's native graph engine is purpose-built for relationship-heavy workloads like
story evolution, entity linking, and provenance tracking. Graph traversals that would require
complex SQL joins are expressed naturally in Cypher. Causal clustering provides the write
consistency required for editorial workflows.

Alternatives: PostgreSQL with recursive CTEs (rejected — performance degrades beyond 3-hop
traversals); Amazon Neptune (rejected — vendor lock-in, higher cost); ArangoDB (rejected —
smaller ecosystem).

Trade-offs: Additional operational complexity managing Neo4j alongside PostgreSQL/MongoDB,
but graph query performance is 10-100x better for story relationship queries.



SDR-STG-002: Event-Sourced Story Versioning



Decision: Every story mutation is recorded as an immutable event in Kafka, with materialized
views in Neo4j and PostgreSQL. Story versions are derived from event replay, not direct
mutation.

Rationale: Event sourcing provides complete audit trail, enables time-travel queries, supports
conflict resolution, and allows rebuilding any historical state. Essential for editorial provenance.

Alternatives: Traditional CRUD with version columns (rejected — no event history, harder
conflict resolution); Git-like branching model (rejected — overcomplicated for editorial
workflows).

Trade-offs: Increased storage for event log, but essential for editorial integrity and regulatory
compliance.



SDR-STG-003: pgvector for Embedding Storage with Neo4j for Graph Traversal
Decision: Store document and entity embeddings in PostgreSQL with pgvector for ANN
similarity search. Store graph relationships in Neo4j. Combine both via a hybrid search service.

Rationale: pgvector provides production-grade vector search within existing PostgreSQL
infrastructure. Neo4j handles graph-specific queries. Hybrid approach leverages each database's
strengths.

Alternatives: Neo4j with graph embeddings only (rejected — vector search less mature);
dedicated vector DB like Pinecone (rejected — additional infrastructure).

Trade-offs: Two systems to query for hybrid search, but each optimized for its domain.



SDR-STG-004: CQRS for Story Read/Write Separation



Decision: Implement Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS) for stories. Commands
(create, update, merge) write through the domain model and publish events. Queries read from
optimized materialized views.

Rationale: Story graph queries are complex and read-heavy. CQRS allows optimizing reads
independently from writes, scaling read replicas, and building specialized query models.

Alternatives: Single model for reads and writes (rejected — query performance suffers under
write load).

Trade-offs: Eventual consistency between write and read models, but acceptable for story
content (seconds of lag).

1.1 Story Graph Philosophy



```

STORY GRAPH — PHILOSOPHY & PRINCIPLES:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┐

│           THE STORY GRAPH IS THE SINGLE SOURCE OF                           │

│              EDITORIAL TRUTH FOR THE PLATFORM                           │

├
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
┤

│                                              │

│ CORE PRINCIPLES:                                        │

│                                              │

│ 1. ONE CANONICAL STORY PER REAL-WORLD EVENT                                         │

│   Every real-world event has exactly one canonical story in the graph.                  │

│   Multiple perspectives are story variants, not separate stories.               │

│                                              │

│ 2. STORIES EVOLVE, NOT DUPLICATE                                    │

│   New information merges into existing stories. The graph grows richer                      │

│   over time, not more cluttered.                            │

│                                              │

│ 3. EVERYTHING IS CONNECTED                                      │

│   Stories link to entities, claims, evidence, sources, topics, and each             │

│   other. The graph reveals relationships invisible to linear text.          │

│                                              │

│ 4. PROVENANCE IS IMMUTABLE                                      │

│   Every change is recorded. Every claim traces to its source. Every                 │

│   editorial decision is documented. The graph IS the audit trail.               │

│                                              │
│ 5. THE GRAPH LEARNS                                          │

│     Entity knowledge accumulates. Relationship patterns emerge. The graph         │

│     becomes smarter as it grows, powering better AI recommendations.          │

│                                                │

│ 6. TEMPORAL AWARENESS                                             │

│     The graph understands time. It knows what was known when. It can          │

│     reconstruct any historical state.                        │

│                                                │

┘

1.4 Canonical Story Model



```go

// services/story-graph/story-lifecycle-engine/internal/domain/model.go

package domain



// CanonicalStory is the single source of truth for a real-world event
type CanonicalStory struct {

  // Identity

  StoryID         uuid.UUID      `json:"story_id"`

  TenantID         uuid.UUID       `json:"tenant_id"`

  CanonicalURL string             `json:"canonical_url"`



  // Core Content

  Headline         string      `json:"headline"`

  Summary           string       `json:"summary"`

  LeadParagraph string             `json:"lead_paragraph"`



  // Classification

  Category         StoryCategory `json:"category"`

  Subcategory       string       `json:"subcategory,omitempty"`

  Archetype        StoryArchetype `json:"archetype"`

  Priority       StoryPriority `json:"priority"`



  // Lifecycle

  State          StoryState     `json:"state"`

  Version         int64        `json:"version"`

  TruthState       string       `json:"truth_state"`    // From Truth Engine

  ConfidenceScore float64           `json:"confidence_score"`



  // Scope

  GeographicScope GeographicScope `json:"geographic_scope"`

  Language         string       `json:"language"`
    Audience       []string    `json:"audience,omitempty"`



    // Relationships (IDs only — full graph in Neo4j)

    ParentStoryID *uuid.UUID        `json:"parent_story_id,omitempty"`

    MergedFromIDs []uuid.UUID         `json:"merged_from_ids,omitempty"`

    RelatedStoryIDs []uuid.UUID      `json:"related_story_ids,omitempty"`



    // Temporal

    FirstDetectedAt time.Time       `json:"first_detected_at"`

    FirstPublishedAt *time.Time     `json:"first_published_at,omitempty"`

    LastUpdatedAt time.Time         `json:"last_updated_at"`

    CreatedAt      time.Time     `json:"created_at"`

    ArchivedAt     *time.Time     `json:"archived_at,omitempty"`



    // Editorial

    CreatedBy      string      `json:"created_by"`      // "AI_AGENT" or "USER_ID"

    LastModifiedBy string        `json:"last_modified_by"`

    EditorialStatus EditorialStatus `json:"editorial_status"`

    ReviewCount      int        `json:"review_count"`



    // Event Sourcing

    EventStreamID string         `json:"event_stream_id"`

    EventVersion int64          `json:"event_version"`

}

3.1 Story State Machine
```go

// services/story-graph/story-lifecycle-engine/internal/domain/state_machine.go

package domain



// StoryStateMachine manages the complete story lifecycle

type StoryStateMachine struct {

    story   *CanonicalStory

    currentState StoryState

    transitions map[StoryState]map[StoryEvent]StoryState

    eventStore EventStore

}



type StoryEvent string

const (

    EventStoryDetected        StoryEvent = "STORY_DETECTED"

    EventCandidateAccepted StoryEvent = "CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED"

    EventCandidateRejected StoryEvent = "CANDIDATE_REJECTED"

    EventVerificationPassed StoryEvent = "VERIFICATION_PASSED"

    EventVerificationFailed StoryEvent = "VERIFICATION_FAILED"

    EventBreakingDeclared StoryEvent = "BREAKING_DECLARED"

    EventNewInformationAdded StoryEvent = "NEW_INFORMATION_ADDED"

    EventUpdatePublished       StoryEvent = "UPDATE_PUBLISHED"

    EventCorrectionIssued StoryEvent = "CORRECTION_ISSUED"

    EventStoryClosed      StoryEvent = "STORY_CLOSED"

    EventStoryReopened         StoryEvent = "STORY_REOPENED"

    EventStoryArchived        StoryEvent = "STORY_ARCHIVED"
    EventStoryRetracted         StoryEvent = "STORY_RETRACTED"

    EventDuplicateDetected StoryEvent = "DUPLICATE_DETECTED"

    EventMergeProposed           StoryEvent = "MERGE_PROPOSED"

    EventMergeCompleted           StoryEvent = "MERGE_COMPLETED"

    EventSplitRequested         StoryEvent = "SPLIT_REQUESTED"

    EventSplitCompleted         StoryEvent = "SPLIT_COMPLETED"

)



func NewStoryStateMachine(story *CanonicalStory, eventStore EventStore) *StoryStateMachine
{

    sm := &StoryStateMachine{

        story:      story,

        currentState: story.State,

        eventStore: eventStore,

    }



    sm.transitions = map[StoryState]map[StoryEvent]StoryState{

        StoryStateDiscovered: {

             EventCandidateAccepted: StoryStateCandidate,

             EventDuplicateDetected: StoryStateDiscovered, // Will be merged

             EventBreakingDeclared: StoryStateBreaking,

        },

        StoryStateCandidate: {

             EventCandidateRejected: StoryStateClosed,

             EventVerificationPassed: StoryStateVerified,

        },
StoryStateVerified: {

     EventNewInformationAdded: StoryStateDeveloping,

     EventBreakingDeclared: StoryStateBreaking,

     EventStoryClosed:      StoryStateClosed,

},

StoryStateDeveloping: {

     EventVerificationPassed: StoryStateVerified,

     EventUpdatePublished:    StoryStateActive,

     EventStoryClosed:      StoryStateClosed,

},

StoryStateActive: {

     EventNewInformationAdded: StoryStateDeveloping,

     EventCorrectionIssued: StoryStateCorrecting,

     EventStoryClosed:      StoryStateClosed,

     EventStoryArchived:     StoryStateArchived,

},

StoryStateBreaking: {

     EventNewInformationAdded: StoryStateDeveloping,

     EventUpdatePublished:    StoryStateActive,

     EventCorrectionIssued: StoryStateCorrecting,

},

StoryStateCorrecting: {

     EventUpdatePublished:    StoryStateActive,

     EventStoryRetracted:    StoryStateRetracted,

},

StoryStateClosed: {
             EventStoryReopened:    StoryStateDeveloping,

             EventStoryArchived:   StoryStateArchived,

        },

        StoryStateArchived: {

             EventStoryReopened:    StoryStateDeveloping,

        },

        StoryStateRetracted: {

             // Terminal state

        },

    }



    return sm

}



func (sm *StoryStateMachine) Transition(event StoryEvent, metadata map[string]interface{})
error {

    validEvents, exists := sm.transitions[sm.currentState]

    if !exists {

        return fmt.Errorf("no transitions from state: %s", sm.currentState)

    }



    nextState, valid := validEvents[event]

    if !valid {

        return fmt.Errorf("invalid transition: %s -[%s]-> ?", sm.currentState, event)

    }
      // Record event

      domainEvent := NewStoryDomainEvent(

          sm.story.StoryID,

          event,

          sm.currentState,

          nextState,

          metadata,

      )



  if err := sm.eventStore.Append(sm.story.EventStreamID, domainEvent,
sm.story.EventVersion); err != nil {

          return fmt.Errorf("append event: %w", err)

      }



      // Update state

      sm.currentState = nextState

      sm.story.State = nextState

      sm.story.EventVersion++

      sm.story.LastUpdatedAt = time.Now()

      sm.story.Version++



      return nil

}

```



3.2 Story Merge Engine
```go

// services/story-graph/story-lifecycle-engine/internal/domain/merge.go

package domain



// StoryMergeEngine handles merging duplicate or related stories

type StoryMergeEngine struct {

    neo4jClient neo4j.Driver

    eventStore    EventStore

    similarityEngine SimilarityEngineClient

    editorialQueue EditorialQueueClient

}



type MergeRequest struct {

    SourceStoryID uuid.UUID        `json:"source_story_id"` // Story being merged

    TargetStoryID uuid.UUID       `json:"target_story_id"` // Story receiving merge

    MergeStrategy MergeStrategy `json:"merge_strategy"`

    Reason       string      `json:"reason"`

    RequestedBy     string     `json:"requested_by"`

}



type MergeStrategy string

const (

    MergeStrategyAbsorb MergeStrategy = "ABSORB"          // Source absorbed into target

    MergeStrategyCombine MergeStrategy = "COMBINE" // Both combined into new story

    MergeStrategySupersede MergeStrategy = "SUPERSEDE" // Source supersedes target
)



type MergeResult struct {

    MergeID        uuid.UUID       `json:"merge_id"`

    SourceStoryID uuid.UUID            `json:"source_story_id"`

    TargetStoryID uuid.UUID            `json:"target_story_id"`

    ResultStoryID uuid.UUID            `json:"result_story_id"`

    Strategy      MergeStrategy `json:"strategy"`

    ChangesApplied []MergeChange `json:"changes_applied"`

    ConflictsFound []MergeConflict `json:"conflicts_found"`

    Status       MergeStatus       `json:"status"`

    CompletedAt       time.Time        `json:"completed_at"`

}



type MergeChange struct {

  ChangeType string          `json:"change_type"` // ADD_CLAIM, UPDATE_HEADLINE,
ADD_SOURCE, etc.

    Description string      `json:"description"`

    BeforeValue interface{} `json:"before_value"`

    AfterValue interface{} `json:"after_value"`

}



type MergeConflict struct {

    ConflictType string `json:"conflict_type"`

    Field      string `json:"field"`

    SourceValue interface{} `json:"source_value"`
    TargetValue interface{} `json:"target_value"`

    Resolution string `json:"resolution"` // KEEP_SOURCE, KEEP_TARGET, MANUAL

}



// ExecuteMerge performs a story merge operation

func (sme *StoryMergeEngine) ExecuteMerge(

    ctx context.Context,

    request *MergeRequest,

) (*MergeResult, error) {



    // 1. Load both stories with all relationships

    sourceStory, err := sme.loadFullStory(ctx, request.SourceStoryID)

    if err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("load source story: %w", err)

    }



    targetStory, err := sme.loadFullStory(ctx, request.TargetStoryID)

    if err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("load target story: %w", err)

    }



    // 2. Validate merge is appropriate

    if err := sme.validateMerge(sourceStory, targetStory); err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("merge validation: %w", err)

    }
  // 3. Calculate similarity and detect conflicts

  similarity := await sme.similarityEngine.CalculateSimilarity(ctx, sourceStory, targetStory)

  conflicts := sme.detectConflicts(sourceStory, targetStory)



  result := &MergeResult{

       MergeID:      uuid.NewV7(),

       SourceStoryID: request.SourceStoryID,

       TargetStoryID: request.TargetStoryID,

       Strategy:    request.MergeStrategy,

       ConflictsFound: conflicts,

       Status:     MergeStatusInProgress,

  }



  // 4. If conflicts exist and strategy is COMBINE, escalate to human

  if len(conflicts) > 0 && request.MergeStrategy == MergeStrategyCombine {

       return sme.escalateToHumanReview(ctx, result, sourceStory, targetStory, conflicts)

  }



  // 5. Execute merge in Neo4j transaction

  session := sme.neo4jClient.NewSession(ctx, neo4j.SessionConfig{

       AccessMode: neo4j.AccessModeWrite,

  })

  defer session.Close(ctx)



  changes, err := session.ExecuteWrite(ctx, func(tx neo4j.ManagedTransaction) (interface{},
error) {
    return sme.executeMergeTransaction(ctx, tx, sourceStory, targetStory,
request.MergeStrategy, conflicts)

  })

  if err != nil {

       result.Status = MergeStatusFailed

       return result, fmt.Errorf("execute merge transaction: %w", err)

  }



  result.ChangesApplied = changes.([]MergeChange)



  // 6. Determine result story

  switch request.MergeStrategy {

  case MergeStrategyAbsorb:

       result.ResultStoryID = request.TargetStoryID

  case MergeStrategySupersede:

       result.ResultStoryID = request.SourceStoryID

  case MergeStrategyCombine:

       result.ResultStoryID = request.TargetStoryID // Updated target

  }



  // 7. Record merge events

  sme.recordMergeEvents(ctx, result)



  // 8. Update source story state

  sme.closeSourceStory(ctx, request.SourceStoryID, request.TargetStoryID)
    result.Status = MergeStatusCompleted

    result.CompletedAt = time.Now()



    return result, nil

}



func (sme *StoryMergeEngine) executeMergeTransaction(

    ctx context.Context,

    tx neo4j.ManagedTransaction,

    source *CanonicalStory,

    target *CanonicalStory,

    strategy MergeStrategy,

    conflicts []MergeConflict,

) ([]MergeChange, error) {



    changes := []MergeChange{}



    // 1. Move all claims from source to target

    result, err := tx.Run(ctx, `

      MATCH (source:Story {story_id: $sourceId})

      MATCH (source)-[:CONTAINS_CLAIM]->(claim:Claim)

      MATCH (target:Story {story_id: $targetId})

     CREATE (target)-[:CONTAINS_CLAIM {merged_from: $sourceId, merged_at: datetime()}]-
>(claim)

      RETURN count(claim) as claim_count

    `, map[string]interface{}{
     "sourceId": source.StoryID.String(),

     "targetId": target.StoryID.String(),

})



if err == nil && result.Next() {

     count := result.Record().Values[0].(int64)

     changes = append(changes, MergeChange{

          ChangeType: "MOVE_CLAIMS",

          Description: fmt.Sprintf("Moved %d claims from source to target", count),

     })

}



// 2. Link all sources from source story to target

result, err = tx.Run(ctx, `

     MATCH (source:Story {story_id: $sourceId})-[r:SOURCED_FROM]->(src:Source)

     MATCH (target:Story {story_id: $targetId})

     CREATE (target)-[:SOURCED_FROM {

          relevance: r.relevance,

          merged_from: $sourceId

     }]->(src)

     RETURN count(src) as source_count

`, map[string]interface{}{

     "sourceId": source.StoryID.String(),

     "targetId": target.StoryID.String(),

})
if err == nil && result.Next() {

     count := result.Record().Values[0].(int64)

     changes = append(changes, MergeChange{

          ChangeType: "LINK_SOURCES",

          Description: fmt.Sprintf("Linked %d sources to target story", count),

     })

}



// 3. Link all entities

result, err = tx.Run(ctx, `

     MATCH (source:Story {story_id: $sourceId})-[r:INVOLVES_ENTITY]->(e:Entity)

     MATCH (target:Story {story_id: $targetId})

     MERGE (target)-[:INVOLVES_ENTITY {

          role: r.role,

          merged_from: $sourceId

     }]->(e)

     RETURN count(e) as entity_count

`, map[string]interface{}{

     "sourceId": source.StoryID.String(),

     "targetId": target.StoryID.String(),

})



if err == nil && result.Next() {

     count := result.Record().Values[0].(int64)

     changes = append(changes, MergeChange{

          ChangeType: "LINK_ENTITIES",
          Description: fmt.Sprintf("Linked %d entities to target story", count),

     })

}



// 4. Create MERGED_INTO relationship

_, err = tx.Run(ctx, `

     MATCH (source:Story {story_id: $sourceId})

     MATCH (target:Story {story_id: $targetId})

     CREATE (source)-[:MERGED_INTO {

          strategy: $strategy,

          merged_at: datetime()

     }]->(target)

     SET source.state = 'CLOSED',

          source.last_updated_at = datetime()

     SET target.source_count = target.source_count + source.source_count,

          target.claim_count = target.claim_count + source.claim_count,

          target.last_updated_at = datetime(),

          target.version = target.version + 1

`, map[string]interface{}{

     "sourceId": source.StoryID.String(),

     "targetId": target.StoryID.String(),

     "strategy": string(strategy),

})



if err != nil {

     return nil, fmt.Errorf("create merge relationship: %w", err)
    }



    changes = append(changes, MergeChange{

         ChangeType: "MERGE_RELATIONSHIP",

         Description: "Created MERGED_INTO relationship and updated story states",

    })



    return changes, nil

}



func (sme *StoryMergeEngine) detectConflicts(

    source *CanonicalStory,

    target *CanonicalStory,

) []MergeConflict {

    conflicts := []MergeConflict{}



    // Headline conflict (different headlines for same event)

    if source.Headline != target.Headline &&

         sme.headlinesAreSubstantiallyDifferent(source.Headline, target.Headline) {

         conflicts = append(conflicts, MergeConflict{

              ConflictType: "HEADLINE",

              Field:   "headline",

              SourceValue: source.Headline,

              TargetValue: target.Headline,

              Resolution: "KEEP_TARGET", // Default: keep more established story's headline

         })
    }



    // Category conflict

    if source.Category != target.Category {

        conflicts = append(conflicts, MergeConflict{

             ConflictType: "CATEGORY",

             Field:    "category",

             SourceValue: source.Category,

             TargetValue: target.Category,

             Resolution: "MANUAL",

        })

    }



    // Priority conflict

    if source.Priority != target.Priority {

        conflicts = append(conflicts, MergeConflict{

             ConflictType: "PRIORITY",

             Field:    "priority",

             SourceValue: source.Priority,

             TargetValue: target.Priority,

             Resolution: "KEEP_HIGHEST",

        })

    }



    return conflicts

}

package domain



// StoryBranchEngine handles creating story branches for different perspectives

type StoryBranchEngine struct {

type BranchRequest struct {

type BranchReason string

const (

      BranchReasonPerspective BranchReason = "DIFFERENT_PERSPECTIVE"

      BranchReasonLocalization BranchReason = "LOCALIZATION"

      BranchReasonUpdate         BranchReason = "SIGNIFICANT_UPDATE"
    BranchReasonCorrection BranchReason = "CORRECTION_BRANCH"

)



// CreateBranch creates a new story branch from a parent story

func (sbe *StoryBranchEngine) CreateBranch(

    ctx context.Context,

    request *BranchRequest,

) (*CanonicalStory, error) {



    // Load parent story

    parentStory, err := sbe.loadFullStory(ctx, request.ParentStoryID)

    if err != nil {

        return nil, fmt.Errorf("load parent story: %w", err)

    }



    // Create branch story (copy of parent)

    branchStory := sbe.copyStory(parentStory)

    branchStory.StoryID = uuid.NewV7()

    branchStory.ParentStoryID = &parentStory.StoryID

    branchStory.State = StoryStateDeveloping

    branchStory.Version = 1

    branchStory.EventVersion = 0

    branchStory.CreatedAt = time.Now()

    branchStory.LastUpdatedAt = time.Now()

    branchStory.CreatedBy = request.RequestedBy
// Create in Neo4j

session := sbe.neo4jClient.NewSession(ctx, neo4j.SessionConfig{

     AccessMode: neo4j.AccessModeWrite,

})

defer session.Close(ctx)



_, err = session.ExecuteWrite(ctx, func(tx neo4j.ManagedTransaction) (interface{}, error) {

     // Create branch story node

     _, err := tx.Run(ctx, `

       CREATE (branch:Story {

            story_id: $branchId,

            tenant_id: $tenantId,

            headline: $headline,

            summary: $summary,

            state: $state,

            priority: $priority,

            category: $category,

            version: 1,

            created_at: datetime(),

            last_updated_at: datetime()

       })

       WITH branch

       MATCH (parent:Story {story_id: $parentId})

       CREATE (branch)-[:BRANCHED_FROM {

            reason: $reason,

            description: $description,
       branched_at: datetime()

     }]->(parent)

     RETURN branch

`, map[string]interface{}{

     "branchId": branchStory.StoryID.String(),

     "tenantId": branchStory.TenantID.String(),

     "headline": branchStory.Headline,

     "summary":      branchStory.Summary,

     "state":     string(branchStory.State),

     "priority": string(branchStory.Priority),

     "category": string(branchStory.Category),

     "parentId": parentStory.StoryID.String(),

     "reason":      string(request.BranchReason),

     "description": request.Description,

})

if err != nil {

     return nil, fmt.Errorf("create branch node: %w", err)

}



// Copy claims from parent

_, err = tx.Run(ctx, `

     MATCH (parent:Story {story_id: $parentId})-[:CONTAINS_CLAIM]->(claim:Claim)

     MATCH (branch:Story {story_id: $branchId})

     CREATE (branch)-[:CONTAINS_CLAIM {inherited: true}]->(claim)

`, map[string]interface{}{

     "parentId": parentStory.StoryID.String(),
          "branchId": branchStory.StoryID.String(),

     })



     // Copy entities

     _, err = tx.Run(ctx, `

          MATCH (parent:Story {story_id: $parentId})-[r:INVOLVES_ENTITY]->(entity:Entity)

          MATCH (branch:Story {story_id: $branchId})

          CREATE (branch)-[:INVOLVES_ENTITY {role: r.role, inherited: true}]->(entity)

     `, map[string]interface{}{

          "parentId": parentStory.StoryID.String(),

          "branchId": branchStory.StoryID.String(),

     })



     return nil, err

})



if err != nil {

     return nil, fmt.Errorf("execute branch transaction: %w", err)

}



// Record event

sbe.eventStore.Append(branchStory.EventStreamID, NewStoryDomainEvent(

     branchStory.StoryID,

     EventSplitRequested,

     "",

     string(branchStory.State),
        map[string]interface{}{

              "parent_story_id": parentStory.StoryID,

              "branch_reason": request.BranchReason,

        },

      ), 0)



      return branchStory, nil

}

# services/story-graph/knowledge-graph-service/src/knowledge/extractor.py

"""

Knowledge Extraction & Enrichment Engine.

Extracts entities, relationships, and topics from stories to enrich the graph.

"""
class KnowledgeExtractionEngine:

  """Extracts structured knowledge from story content."""



  def __init__(self, nlp_models: Dict[str, Any], neo4j_driver, embedding_model):

    self.ner_model = nlp_models["named_entity_recognition"]

    self.relation_model = nlp_models["relation_extraction"]

    self.entity_linker = nlp_models["entity_linking"]

    self.topic_model = nlp_models["topic_modeling"]

    self.neo4j = neo4j_driver

    self.embedding_model = embedding_model



  async def extract_and_enrich(

    self,

    story: CanonicalStory,

    content: str,

  ) -> KnowledgeExtractionResult:

    """

    Extract entities, relationships, and topics from story content

    and enrich the knowledge graph.

    """



    result = KnowledgeExtractionResult(story_id=story.story_id)



    # 1. Named Entity Recognition

    entities = await self.ner_model.extract(content)
# 2. Entity Linking — resolve to canonical entities

resolved_entities = []

for entity in entities:

    canonical = await self.entity_linker.resolve(

        entity.name,

        entity.entity_type,

        context=content[:500],

    )

    resolved_entities.append(canonical)



# 3. Relationship Extraction

relationships = await self.relation_model.extract_triples(

    content, entities=resolved_entities

)



# 4. Topic Detection

topics = await self.topic_model.detect(content)



# 5. Update Neo4j Knowledge Graph

async with self.neo4j.session() as session:

    await session.execute_write(

        self._update_graph,

        story.story_id,

        resolved_entities,

        relationships,
             topics,

       )



     # 6. Generate embeddings

     entity_embeddings = await self._generate_entity_embeddings(resolved_entities)

     story_embedding = await self.embedding_model.embed(content[:2000])



     result.entities_extracted = len(resolved_entities)

     result.relationships_extracted = len(relationships)

     result.topics_detected = len(topics)

     result.story_embedding = story_embedding



     return result



async def _update_graph(

     self,

     tx,

     story_id: str,

     entities: List[ResolvedEntity],

     relationships: List[ExtractedRelationship],

     topics: List[Topic],

):

     """Update Neo4j with extracted knowledge."""



     # Merge entities (create if not exists, update if exists)

     for entity in entities:
await tx.run("""

  MERGE (e:Entity {canonical_name: $canonical_name})

  ON CREATE SET

     e.entity_id = $entity_id,

     e.name = $name,

     e.entity_type = $entity_type,

     e.wikidata_id = $wikidata_id,

     e.description = $description,

     e.prominence_score = $prominence_score,

     e.created_at = datetime()

  ON MATCH SET

     e.prominence_score = CASE

         WHEN e.prominence_score < $prominence_score

         THEN $prominence_score

         ELSE e.prominence_score

     END,

     e.updated_at = datetime()

  WITH e

  MATCH (s:Story {story_id: $story_id})

  MERGE (s)-[:INVOLVES_ENTITY {role: $role}]->(e)

""", {

  "entity_id": entity.entity_id,

  "canonical_name": entity.canonical_name,

  "name": entity.name,

  "entity_type": entity.entity_type,

  "wikidata_id": entity.wikidata_id or "",
       "description": entity.description or "",

       "prominence_score": entity.prominence_score,

       "story_id": story_id,

       "role": entity.role_in_story or "MENTION",

  })



# Create relationships between entities

for rel in relationships:

  await tx.run("""

       MATCH (e1:Entity {canonical_name: $subject})

       MATCH (e2:Entity {canonical_name: $object})

       MERGE (e1)-[r:RELATED_TO {relationship_type: $rel_type}]->(e2)

       ON CREATE SET r.created_at = datetime(), r.confidence = $confidence

       ON MATCH SET r.confidence = CASE

         WHEN r.confidence < $confidence THEN $confidence

         ELSE r.confidence

       END

  """, {

       "subject": rel.subject_canonical_name,

       "object": rel.object_canonical_name,

       "rel_type": rel.relationship_type,

       "confidence": rel.confidence,

  })



# Link topics

for topic in topics:
          await tx.run("""

               MERGE (t:Topic {name: $topic_name})

        ON CREATE SET t.topic_id = $topic_id, t.keywords = $keywords, t.created_at =
datetime()

               WITH t

               MATCH (s:Story {story_id: $story_id})

               MERGE (s)-[:BELONGS_TO_TOPIC {relevance: $relevance}]->(t)

          """, {

               "topic_id": str(uuid.uuid4()),

               "topic_name": topic.name,

               "keywords": topic.keywords,

               "story_id": story_id,

               "relevance": topic.relevance,

          })
